articles.title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
articles.summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
articles.summary_zh: 🇪🇷厄立特里亚·21世纪10年代
articles.title_zh: 他在自己工作的医院被捕，并将监狱变成了讲坛。
articles.content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.
articles.content_zh:
Berhane博士是耶稣的新信徒,在厄立特里亚的一家医院工作,当时秘密警察来找他。 他的罪行是他的信仰。 他们把他关进监狱11个月,在地球上最严酷的系统之一,一个旨在使基督徒消失和安静的地方. 他做的恰恰相反。

"每天我拍手,"他说:"囚犯会站出来,我分享福音". 一个刚认识耶稣的人决定 他的牢房只是下一个介绍他的地方 三个圣经和一个死亡之谷 当局拿走了他的圣经。 他又偷渡进来了 他们也拿走了那个 他走私了三分之一

他极力倚靠"诗经",当狱友被带出处死时,关于走过死亡阴影谷的老台词不再是诗歌,成为了扶他站直的东西. 11个月没有打倒他。 这让他成了传教士。 守卫们打算让新基督徒安静下来,反而给了他一个无处可去的会众.

无论他们把你放在哪里,耶稣都跟着你,他不受墙壁的恐吓. Berhane博士在厄立特里亚的一所监狱发现了这一点。 你可以相信它 无论你在哪里。

articles.title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
articles.summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
articles.summary_zh: 🇲🇬马达加斯加·2013年
articles.title_zh: 一位在马达加斯加的建筑工程师确信圣经是真的
articles.content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.
articles.content_zh:
梅利亚斯在马达加斯加为生计而建东西,他是一位稳定的建筑工程师,据他自己说,他并不特别期望上帝会打断他。 2013年,21时,上帝做到了. 这不是戏剧性的雷声。 更安静,更难争论 "圣灵使我的心相信圣经是真的,"梅利亚斯说.

"我发现新的快乐和兴奋 通过圣经学习耶稣。" 他可能放弃的书 成为他一生中最活的 从建房到建教堂 他本可以保持他作为私人慰藉的新信仰,继续从事工程工作. 相反,他给了它一切。

2015年,他作为传教士接受了半年的训练,此后他在伊孔戈的塔纳拉人和诺西贝的萨卡拉瓦人中种植了教堂和门徒新信徒,其中部分到达的岛角最少. 现在他正在训练另外三名马达加斯加传教士, 马达加斯加不是上帝所作所为的一个脚注。

他正在培养梅利亚斯,工程师和商人以及普通工人等当地人,并将他们送到他们自己无法接触到的邻居那里. 当圣灵说服你的心脏 这一切都是真的, 它不仍然是爱好。 它成为你围绕你生活的东西。 他准备说服你

articles.title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
articles.summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
articles.summary_zh: 🇳🇪阿加德兹·21世纪初
articles.title_zh: 一本新约圣经一直放在他的焊接车间里，直到一位少年终于读了它。
articles.content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.
articles.content_zh:
有人在尼日尔的皮埃尔焊接车间留下了一份新约, 他少年时期,最终他捡到了. 他所读的内容与他被告知的基督徒的情况不符。 它充满了温柔,与最贫穷的人的亲近, 正是他年轻时所希望的世界是真实的。

多年后,他搬到阿加德兹, 向着沙漠, 在那里他发现了书上描述的东西。 一个来自贝宁、多哥、布基纳法索、法国和尼日尔的教会家庭,靠他只读过的东西生活。 没有遗憾,没有一天,皮埃尔成为了一名非专业的传教士,他谈论这件事时不设套.

"我从未后悔过皈依基督教信仰",他说:"即使是一天也没有". 在尼日尔,这是一件大胆的事,在那里,圣战团体追随耶稣,而他自己的孩子则留在穆斯林手中,他带着爱,没有压力。 不过,没有遗憾。 一日不见.

他曾诵读了真主--对于贫民是温和的--他发现真主确是彻知的。 无论你听到什么关于耶稣的二手消息 当你们终于亲眼见到他时 他都挺过来了 Pierre会告诉你打开书看看

articles.title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
articles.title_zh: 他被教导说基督徒不祷告。然后，他看到叔叔在饭前祷告。
articles.content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.
articles.content_zh:
查尔斯·亚巴加·迪亚拉(Charles Yabaga Diarra)在马里勒尔一个严格的穆斯林家庭长大,在那里基督徒受到嘲笑和误解. 他的父亲是一名校长和政治家,他像学校一样管理着房子. 童年时,查尔斯逃离了大约一百五十英里,与一个叔叔住在一起,在那里,他直接遇到了他被告知的东西并不存在.

他的叔叔,一位基督教牧师,低头祷告,在饭前祷告. 查尔斯被惊呆了 "因为我们是基督徒,我们吃饭前祈祷",叔叔解释道. 查尔斯被告知基督徒根本不祷告 用他自己的语言祈祷,他不会离开。

只要告诉我他父亲把他拉回来的方式 强迫他进入古兰经学校 但种子是种的 多年之后,与他的叔叔一起回来,疲惫和寻找,查尔斯终于自己祈祷. "主啊,我真的厌倦了寻找真相. "给我带路" 他在一所假期圣经学校听到的一首诗回到了他身边,1981年11月他把生命献给了耶稣.

代价是真实的。 查尔斯现在是一名传教士,因马里的冲突而流离失所,每天都面临压力。 但他没有一个人去。 他的十四个兄弟姐妹中,大多数现在都跟随耶稣,大约一百名基督徒聚集在他的大家庭活动中. 一个叔叔为晚餐祷告 整个家庭都向耶稣倾斜 你安静的,普通的忠诚 可能是种更多 比你知道。

articles.title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
articles.summary: Laos· 2022
articles.title_zh: 一位寡妇从一位推销员那里听到了好消息，从此念念不忘。
articles.content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.
articles.content_zh:
裴 was在老挝是一位52岁的寡妇,养大了整个村庄的养殖方式,在政府推崇无神论的地方崇拜祖先和地方灵灵,邻居警告说,追随外国人神会冒犯家乡神灵. 然后一个推销员走过来,在出售他的商品之间,告诉她耶稣的事. 救世是礼物,不是报酬

裴 believed信之. 她放弃了她毕生怀念的祖先的崇拜,悄悄地跟随耶稣. 在她自己的前门付出的代价 她被秘密地关了四个月, 变得足够强大,可以说话。 她告诉的第一个人是她的女儿和女婿,她们碰巧是一名警察。 他们没有庆祝。

他威胁她,说如果她不停止相信耶稣,他们会告发她,监禁她,或者把她赶出去. 6月,他们在上面做得很好,把她的衣服扔到院子里,并告诉她去和给她这个耶稣的人一起生活. 她去了 她去了吗? 她没有回去。 一个什么都没有的寡妇选择了耶稣 而不是一个屋顶, 因为她已经发现了一些没人能从她的心脏里赶走的东西。

追随耶稣并不总是安全的,但总是值得的. 裴氏发现的比付出的代价更值钱,也是献给你的.

articles.title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
articles.summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
articles.summary_zh: 乌兹别克斯坦和塔吉克斯坦·2020年代
articles.title_zh: 女儿被杀后，他祈祷能拥有一本无人能夺走的圣经
articles.content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.
articles.content_zh:
拉希德·卡迪罗夫(Rashid Kadirov)是中亚穆斯林,当时最糟糕的事情发生了. 他的六岁女儿Azizza被驾拖拉机喝醉的邻居杀死. 在悲痛中,他去寻找可以安息的东西,他去了可兰经. 在那里,他读到了一行,在苏拉5:70中,指向福音书作为圣经. 所以他祈祷了一个奇怪的,具体的祈祷.

他向上帝祈求"印吉尔","新约". 他的朋友给他带来了一个。 是一辆被偷来的吉迪恩圣经 从被破坏的汽车上拍下来的 它没有持续。 当朋友们收回它时,拉希德再次祈祷,这次要一本圣经,没有人能夺走他. 留下来的书 之后一对夫妇从塔吉克斯坦赶来,他们是由自己来到基督的前同学派来的.

他们携带了圣经和JESUS电影的拷贝. 拉希德和他的妻子阿莱卡观看了,正如好消息被解释的那样,他们每个人都在不告诉对方的情况下悄悄地祈祷要接受耶稣. 阿莱卡根本不懂这些

"她对福音几乎没有什么了解,"后来她说,"然而和平却淹没了她的心. 他们在塔吉克斯坦接受洗礼,拉希德开始告诉其他人他发现了什么. 一个悲伤的父亲要求一本书,上帝给了他一个人. 和平拉希德无法在耶稣到达的时候制造。 他与心碎者密不可分,他与你们密不可分。

articles.title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
articles.summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
articles.summary_zh: 北中央省
articles.title_zh: 35位神父都无法帮助她。在教堂里，她看到耶稣粉碎了正在扼住她喉咙的东西。
articles.content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.
articles.content_zh:
钱德拉住在斯里兰卡中北部省的一个乡村,她慢慢地分崩离析. 痛苦,软弱,一个无缘无故的心脏 医生无法命名 她和她的家人是印度教徒,所以他们做了他们知道的事。 他们跟随牧师去了牧师那里. 三十五门. 什么都没有改变。 2021年7月,他们走进了一座教堂。

当人们为她祈祷时,钱德拉看到了一些东西. 恶魔试图掐死她,然后耶稣基督介入并盖在他们身上. 她感到痛苦和疾病 排出她的身体 当他们被打败。 在视觉中,耶稣说圣经 超过她,从Psalm 34。 他说:他们崇拜他,而且赞颂他超绝万物。他说:她也超绝万物,如果她信任他。

一个父亲祈祷她的丈夫迪尼什(Dinesh),一个白天的劳工,看着他的妻子复活,并给上帝一个承诺. "上帝,如果你能治愈我的妻子, 我将奉献我的女儿为你服务。" 几乎听不到耶稣之名的全家都为他献出了生命.

他们的女儿特努沙告诉了班上所发生的事情,她的母亲是自由的,耶稣宽恕了罪人,使他们成为新人. 他们没有保守秘密。 一所房屋教堂在他们家中开始,共有4人. 时已四十六. 耶稣仍然比任何 扼杀你生命的东西更强大 他走进来,他把它印下来,他叫你光辉。

articles.title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
articles.summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
articles.summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
articles.title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
articles.content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
articles.content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

articles.title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
articles.summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
articles.summary_zh: 拉基拉基·1990年代
articles.title_zh: 因果报应说他必须修功德才能上天堂。17岁时，他听说自己可以得到宽恕。
articles.content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.
articles.content_zh:
西蒙·古德出生于斐济一个严格的印度教家庭. 他的曾祖父在1874年英国人攻占群岛后,作为合同工从印度被运走,全家定居在维提莱武北部的一个小村庄. 西蒙在一个有明确规则的系统中长大. "作为一个印度教徒,我们相信因果报应,"他说. "若作善因缘即得上天.

若作恶报果报果报果. " 这是他无法平衡的分类账 他对自己的错误太了解了 结账的那一晚 17岁时,一位朋友邀请他到另一个城镇的一次基督教青年会议. 在那里,他听到一些不符合他所教过的东西。 耶稣基督可以宽恕罪过

不抵消它们, 也不平均出一生。 原谅他们 西蒙感受到了自己失败的轻重,并首次提出摆脱这些失败. "当晚我把生命交给耶稣,"他说. 起初他瞒着父母 当他们发现, 他们不高兴。 但回家的儿子变了 并没有停下来。

时他带领全家来到基督身边,他继续栽培一个对别人同样怀有宽恕的部. 卡玛一直有追踪器 你永远无法清除 耶稣撕开标签。 无论你今晚携带什么 他现在仍然要马上原谅这一切

articles.title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
articles.summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
articles.title_zh: 一名本应死于战斗的士兵走进了恶魔的神殿
articles.content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.
articles.content_zh:
牧师达诺在担任牧师之前是一名军人. 他毫无理由地活着走出战场,从未动摇过为什么的感官. "我相信上帝为了某种目的在战场上拯救了我的生命". 宗旨现于一佛村中欲与他无相. 副宰相的儿子被折磨,妖魔吞噬,无人能助.

达诺斋戒祈祷三天. 然后,近午夜,他去了男孩所在的神殿,做了他唯一知道该做的事. "我呼唤天主之名,"他说:"妖魔离开了少年. 夜神社失声村民说 每一个邪恶的灵魂 立刻离开村庄

达诺从神社到神社,祈祷反抗历代统治这个地方的黑暗. 副局长的家族,他为愤怒而坚韧不拔,却找到了恩典。 他们把生命献给了耶稣,还有四个家庭随行. 曾经反对他的人现在遵循他的路线。 今天村里有一座教堂 曾经有神社

耶稣的名字仍然比每件令你害怕的黑暗事物更强大. 一个信徒在午夜祈祷 足以让整个村庄自由

articles.title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
articles.title_zh: 他们把牧师关进了精神病病房。他带领一百人归向耶稣
articles.content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.
articles.content_zh:
2013年5月哈萨克斯坦逮捕Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev牧师时,他是一位老人。 指控是奇怪的,他伤害了一名教会成员的健康并煽动了宗教仇恨。 他们判处他十年监禁,并把他关进精神病病房,囚犯经常在那里服药。 进来的路上,他觉得这也许是他心智的终结.

"这可能是我最后一次在正确的思想中和你说话,"他说. 然后,一个问题来到他身上,神用的那种。 "你的信仰在哪里?" 在升起的上帝的掩护下 有东西解除了 "我觉得自己在升天主的掩护下,"他说. 期待失去自我的老人却发现耶稣比墙壁更靠近. 他开始和周围的人交谈

对一个吸毒成瘾的囚犯来说 他只是说 只有耶稣才能帮助你 里面有九个月,近一百名囚犯为基督献出了生命。 "在狱中",他说"圣灵为我打开了祈祷的一个维度". 打算打破他的地方成为了他一生中最有成果的支点. 他们于2014年初释放了他。

他走了出去 埋下了好消息 在最后的地方 没有人会寻找它。 上帝不会被任何锁住你的门锁住 他已经在里面等了

articles.title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
articles.summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
articles.title_zh: 她的教会奉献金刚好等于她的电费，一分不差。
articles.content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.
articles.content_zh:
莉娜·约翰逊没有足够的钱来支付她的权力法案. 她没有告诉任何人这个数额。 不是朋友,也不是她的教堂,没有人 这是她的私人担忧, 你悄悄地携带的, 希望某种程度上解决。 在同一周,教堂里出现了一具供奉物,供奉一个有需要的家庭,莉娜尽了力. 26分钱. 几乎什么都没有,她还是给了它。

下到一分钱 第二天,一个朋友告诉她了其余的故事. 教堂的供奉是给她的 当他们数起来时, 她的权力法案的准确数额就到了。 至一分钱. "他们昨天在教堂里接受的献礼是给我的,"莉娜说,"这是确切的金额,就像我的权力法案.

我从来没有告诉任何人我的账单是多少". 这是让你难受的细节 如果她付出超过26美分,总额会超过法案,而规定会失去优势. 她的小礼物也是上帝算术的一部分 神不是围观或猜测。

他知道她从不大声说话的号码 他通过不知道的人 准确地认识了这个号码 算你头上头发的神父也知道你的帐单 一直到最后一分钱

As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, […]  The post  Manta ray led marine scientist to lost fin  first appeared on  God Reports .
articles.summary_zh: 文：马克·埃利斯（Mark Ellis）——安珀·斯帕克斯（Amber Sparks）在加利福尼亚州拉古纳海滩长大，对海洋产生了深厚的热爱，这促使她在加州大学伯克利分校学习海洋科学，并在圣地亚哥的斯克里普斯研究所获得了硕士学位。作为蓝纬度基金会的联合创始人，她与业界合作，寻找保护机会，[…]  这篇题为《蝠鲼引导海洋科学家找到失去的鳍》的文章最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 蝠鲼带领海洋科学家找到失去的鳍
articles.content: By Mark Ellis — Amber Sparks (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) Growing up in Laguna Beach, California, Amber Sparks developed a deep love for the ocean, which led her to study marine science at UC Berkeley and earn a master’s degree at Scripps Institute in San Diego. As co-founder of Blue Latitudes Foundation, she works with industry to find opportunities for conservation, especially with the Rigs-to-Reefs program, when oil drilling platforms are decommissioned. “We work with the oil companies to repurpose certain parts of the platform, retrofit it so that it can remain in place and continue to function as an artificial reef,” she told God Reports. Amber’s work has taken her around the world, with many dive experiences and encounters in the ocean with marine life. But there is one story she will never forget. It happened in the Gulf of Mexico shortly after Amber graduated from Scripps Institute and was invited on a research industry cruise with oil company representatives, scientists, and regulators on a liveaboard vessel. At the Flower Garden National Banks, a marine protected area 200 miles offshore, Amber was excited about her first dive, but slightly nervous. “You don’t know what you’re going to see or what this experience is going to be like,” she recalls. Dropping in (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook) Each diver had to jump off the vessel to get in the water. “We’re all geared up with our snorkel, our buoyancy control device, our wetsuit, and fins are the last thing you put on. So, I put on my fins and I jumped off the side of the boat.” “The second that I hit the water, one of my fins fell off, and I looked down and watched as it slowly descended to the bottom.” Amber glanced over at her dive buddy, and said, “I’m gonna go down. I’m going down.” Normally she would wait for her dive partner and they would go down together, but in this case, she thought, “I can’t (wait). I gotta go get my fin.” So Amber slowly began to descend to the bottom, about 60 feet below the ocean surface. “I felt completely lost. I was in a completely new area. I never dove before, and now I only had one fin.” She realized there were major currents that could have moved her fin in any direction. “I realized I can’t really swim with just one fin. So now not only am I at depth, but I’m handicapped with just one fin, and I started to feel pretty nervous.” It would probably take her 10 minutes to get back the surface, with safety stops. At the moment before panic set in, she looked upward and saw an amazing sight. It was a giant manta ray, with wings extending at least 10 feet. “Its wingspan was double mine. Its arms were out, and it was coming up over the side of a reef. “I’ve never seen a manta ray like this before. It totally took my breath away, it was so magnificent.” Another manta ray (Blue Latitudes Foundation Facebook page) She noted that manta rays are known in the ocean community to be “majestic, God-connected creatures with an understanding maybe beyond what humans can fully comprehend. They see the world and feel it in another way,” she notes. Mantas have the largest known brain of any fish. Their brains are large in absolute terms and relative to body size, which is also true of elephants, dolphins, and people. Their brains have enlarged areas associated with intelligence, vision, and motor coordination, and some of their brain cells are more like those in birds and mammals than in other fish.(1) As the manta ray drew close to Amber, she had an unusual communication experience. “I felt this sense where it said, ‘I want you to follow me. I’m going to help you find your fin.’ Amber Sparks Amber’s diving partner had just descended next to her, and they both began to swim after the manta. “I was barely making it, following this manta ray across the reef. At this point, I was so excited to see a manta ray. I kind of forgot about being handicapped, and I was just trying to go as fast as I can to keep up with it. Then Amber got the sur

articles.summary: While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence […]  The post  Lanier’s Sixth Annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series: A Grand Success  first appeared on  God Reports .

在德克萨斯州休斯顿拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我转而请图书管理员莎伦·科夫兰和执行主任Dr.

大卫·弗莱明(David Fleming)说,“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(John Warwick Montgomery)将非常满意拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利的书信[.] Lanier的第六届年度John Warwick Montgomery讲座系列:大成功首次出现在上帝报告上。
articles.title_zh: 拉尼尔第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利系列讲座：圆满成功
articles.content: John Warwick Montgomery While sitting in the John Warwick Montgomery Study Center at the Lanier Library and Study Center in Houston, Texas, awaiting a meeting, I turned to librarian Sharon Cofran and Executive Director Dr. David Fleming and remarked, “John Warwick Montgomery would be very pleased with what Lanier has accomplished on his behalf.” From Montgomery’s framed correspondence with C. S. Lewis and his barrister gowns to the thousands of books that comprise his remarkable personal collection, Lanier has provided the Christian world with a marvelous tribute to one of the great Christian intellectuals of the twentieth and twenty-first centuries. Born in 1931, John Warwick Montgomery (d. 2024) was a distinguished Christian apologist, theologian, attorney, and scholar whose extraordinary career spanned several disciplines. Holding numerous academic degrees, including doctorates in theology, philosophy, and law, Montgomery became internationally recognized for his defense of Christianity through historical evidence, legal reasoning, and philosophical argumentation. His influential books, including History and Christianity , Faith Founded on Fact , and The Shape of the Past , helped establish a rigorous approach to Christian apologetics. Whether lecturing in universities, debating skeptics, or practicing law, Montgomery maintained that Christianity was not merely a matter of subjective belief but a faith grounded in historical reality and rational inquiry. Yet to stop at the library would be to understate Lanier’s remarkable work. The sixth annual John Warwick Montgomery Lecture Series was a tour de force of distinguished thinkers, passionate Christians, and intellectually engaging presentations. More than a commemoration of Montgomery’s life, the gathering represented a continuation of his intellectual legacy: the conviction that Christianity can withstand serious scrutiny and offer compelling answers to life’s most profound questions. Mark Lanier, Nancy Pearcey, Paul Gould, Adam Francisco, and Michael Horton From the opening panel discussion hosted by attorney and philanthropist Mark Lanier to Dr. Paul Gould’s thoughtful presentation on worldviews, followed by attorney Craig Parton’s lecture on jurisprudential apologetics, one theme emerged with unmistakable clarity: Christianity is a reasonable faith. The presentations reflected Montgomery’s own interdisciplinary approach to apologetics: the Christian faith and intellectual inquiry need not be adversaries. Indeed, the Christian tradition has long insisted that faith and reason are complementary avenues in the pursuit of truth. The following day continued this rich intellectual exploration. Professor Nancy Pearcey addressed questions surrounding truth, dismantling various modern ideologies, while Dr. Adam Francisco offered an informative overview of Islamic history and belief, helping participants better understand one of world’s biggest religions. The keynote address by Dr. Michael Horton examined the challenge of reaching those who identify as “spiritual but not religious,” a growing segment of contemporary society. Horton’s presentation underscored the importance of communicating historic Christian truth in a culture increasingly suspicious of religious institutions yet often deeply interested in spiritual meaning. Dr. Michael Horton On Sunday morning, Lanier founder, Mark Lanier, hosted many participants during his Biblical literacy class, where he continued the dialogue with Michael Horton. Taken together, the lectures, discussions, and interviews demonstrated the breadth of Christian scholarship and the continuing relevance of thoughtful apologetics in an age of skepticism, religious pluralism, and cultural uncertainty. As I reflected on the weekend, I was reminded of the Festschrift Christianity for the Tough-Minded , a collection of scholarly essays honoring Montgomery’s life and ministry. Like that volume, the Lanier lecture series brought together diverse intellec
articles.content_zh:
约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利 在德克萨斯州休斯敦拉尼尔图书馆和研究中心的约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利研究中心等待开会时,我找图书管理员沙龙·科夫兰和执行主任戴维·弗莱明博士说:“约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利将非常高兴拉尼尔代表他取得的成就。” 蒙哥马利与C.S.的书信

刘易斯和他的大律师礼服为他杰出的个人收藏的数千本书,为基督教世界向20世纪和21世纪伟大的基督教知识分子之一致敬。 1931年出生于约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利(d.

2024年)是一位杰出的基督教道歉学家,神学家,律师和学者,其非凡的事业跨越多个学科. 蒙哥马利拥有众多学术学位,包括神学,哲学和法学的博士学位,他通过历史证据,法律推理,哲学论证,为基督教辩护而获得国际承认.

他的有影响力的著作,包括历史和基督教、基于事实的信仰、以及过去的造型,帮助确立了对基督教学的严格态度。 无论是在大学里讲课,辩论怀疑论,还是执业法律,蒙哥马利都坚持认为基督教不仅仅是主观信仰的问题,而是建立在历史现实和理性调查基础上的信仰.

然而, 停留在图书馆将会低估拉尼尔的出色工作。 第六届年度约翰·沃里克·蒙哥马利讲座系列是由杰出的思想家,充满热情的基督徒,以及智力参与的演讲组成的巡回演出.

这场集会不仅仅是纪念蒙哥马利的一生,它代表着他思想遗产的延续:相信基督教能够经受住严肃的审视,为人生最深刻的问题提供令人信服的答案.

马克·拉尼尔 南希·皮尔西 保罗·古尔德 亚当·弗朗西斯科 迈克尔·霍顿 从律师和慈善家马克·拉尼尔主持的开场小组讨论到保罗·古尔德博士关于世界观的深思熟虑的演讲,然后是克雷格·帕顿律师关于法学理论的演讲,一个主题以明确无误的方式出现: 基督教是一种合理的信仰.

这些介绍反映了蒙哥马利自己对学说采取的跨学科方法:基督教信仰和知识调查不必是对手。 事实上,基督教传统长期以来一直坚持信仰和理性是追求真理的补充途径。 次日继续进行这种丰富的知识探索.

Nancy Pearcey教授谈到了围绕真理的问题,摧毁了各种现代意识形态,而Adam Francisco博士则提供了伊斯兰历史和信仰的翔实概览,帮助与会者更好地理解世界上最大的宗教之一。 由Dr.A.先生作主旨发言。

迈克尔·霍顿研究了帮助那些认为是“精神上但并非宗教上”的当代社会日益扩大的阶层的挑战。 霍顿的演讲强调了在一种对宗教机构越来越怀疑、但往往对精神意义很感兴趣的文化中传播基督教历史真理的重要性。 医生

迈克尔·霍顿 星期天早上,拉尼尔创始人马克·拉尼尔(Mark Lanier)在他的圣经识字课期间接待了许多参与者,在那里他继续与迈克尔·霍顿进行对话.

讲座、讨论和访谈共同显示了基督教奖学金的广度,以及深思熟虑的学说在怀疑主义、宗教多元化和文化不确定性的时代的持续相关性。

articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——在第二次世界大战南太平洋的一场海战中，一名日本水兵所在的驱逐舰被美国人击沉，他的大多数战友都淹死了。令人惊奇的是，尽管鱼雷官新谷通晴与其他人一起被卷入波涛之下，随着战舰的沉没，但他却奇迹般地在这场1942年的灾难中幸存下来。（只有18名……）  这篇文章《二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”》最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 二战日本战俘在战俘营中找到“自由”
articles.content: By Charles Gardner — When a Japanese sailor’s destroyer was sunk by the Americans in a World War II South Pacific battle, most of his companions drowned. Amazingly, even though he was sucked underneath the waves with others as the ship went down, torpedo officer Michiharu Shinya somehow survived this 1942 disaster. (Only 18 of the 200-strong crew did). But he would rather have died at that point as his people had been indoctrinated to believe that it was shameful to be captured. Nevertheless, he was badly wounded but nursed back to health by medics. In time, he was picked up and eventually taken to a Prisoner-of-War camp at Featherston, near Wellington, in New Zealand, where he was to spend the next three years, as Don Stephens records in his inspirational book War and Grace (Evangelical Press, an imprint of 10Publishing). Shinya and his fellow inmates were treated with much kindness (in sharp contrast to the torture often experienced by Allied prisoners at the hands of the Japanese). Being showered with gifts at Christmas, a feast he knew nothing about, seemed especially strange. However, he was determined not to be ‘taken in’ by the Christian teaching offered after some of the prisoners requested spiritual help and a Japanese Bible was made available. That is until he chanced upon an article entitled ‘Sorrow in Victory’ in which the author quoted a ‘Hebrew prophet’ as saying: “Those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They shall soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary; they will walk and not be faint.” It made a deep impression on him, and he was determined to find out where it came from. Assuming it was from the Old Testament, he began reading the Bible, starting at Genesis chapter 1. Eventually, to his joy, he discovered that the profound words were from the Book of the prophet Isaiah (chapter 40, verse 31). After flagging somewhat in his search, he found himself hospitalised with malaria when a friend brought him a booklet called The Reason Why explaining the way to salvation. It so happened that the camp’s chaplain, Pastor Hessell Troughton, had been a missionary to Japan and spoke the language. Shinya joined others in his Bible studies and came to know and love Jesus as his Saviour. So much did this “complete freedom” now rule his life that prison had morphed into what he described as “a unique paradise on earth”. He never looked back after that and became convinced that his post-war calling would be in service of his Lord. When he finally returned home, his family were shocked to see him alive for he had been reported as killed in action. He had also given a false name to his captors because of the supposed shame of falling into enemy hands. Shinya subsequently became a pastor and prolific writer and translator following years of theological study both in Tokyo and the US. The Old Testament, he came to believe, demonstrated that sin is “the ultimate problem of mankind” and clearly pointed to Christ as the answer. On seeking to understand why so few Japanese became Christians, he felt it was partly due to their pride borne of believing they were a superior race. As for those three Christmases he spent in New Zealand, author Don Stephens writes: “Of all the gifts he received, the one he valued most was ‘the boundless and deep grace and peace of God in the Lord Jesus Christ’.” The post WWII Japanese POW found ‘freedom’ in camp first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
查尔斯·加德纳编著: 当一艘日本水手的驱逐舰在二战南太平洋战役中被美国人击沉时,大部分同伴溺毙. 令人惊奇的是,尽管随着船只的下沉,他与其他人一起被吸在海浪下,但鱼雷军官Michiharu Shinya却不知何故幸免于1942年的灾难。 (200人的船员中只有18人这样做).

但他宁愿死在那个时候,因为他的族人被灌输相信被俘虏是可耻的. 然而,他受了重伤,但被医护人员喂养。

在时间上,他被接了起来,最终被带到新西兰惠灵顿附近的费瑟斯顿(Featherston)的战俘营,在那里他将度过接下来的三年,正如唐·斯蒂芬斯在他的励志书"战争与格蕾丝"(福音出版社,10Publishing的印记)中记载的那样.

信也和同狱囚犯受到很大程度的善待(与盟军囚犯经常在日本人手中遭受的酷刑形成鲜明对比). 在圣诞节用礼物淋浴 一个他一无所知的宴会 看起来特别奇怪

然而,在一些囚犯要求精神帮助和提供日本圣经后,他决心不再接受基督教教义的 " 接纳 " 。 直到他看到一篇题为“为胜利而悲伤”的文章,作者在文章中引用了一位“赫布鲁先知”的话:“那些希望主复活的人。 他们将像鹰一样飞翔,

他们将奔驰,而不会疲倦,他们将走路,而不会晕倒。 这给他留下了深刻的印象,他下定决心要找出它来自何处. 假设它来自旧约,他开始阅读圣经,从创世纪第一章开始. 最终,在他的喜悦中,他发现深刻的文字来自先知以赛亚的经典(第40章第31节).

在搜索中略微浮出水面后,他发现自己患上了疟疾,一位朋友给他带了一本小册子,名为《原因》,解释救世之路。 难民营的牧师Hessell Troughton牧师曾是日本的传教士, 信也加入了其他人的圣经研究,来到了了解和热爱耶稣作为他的救世主.

这种“完全自由”现在统治了他的生活,监狱变成了他所称的“地球上独一无二的天堂”。 他从此之后再也没有回头看,并且确信他的战后召唤将会为他的主服务. 当他最终回家时,家人震惊地看到他活着,因为他被报道为阵亡.

他还给抓捕者取了一个假名,因为被假定是落入敌人手中的耻辱。 在东京和美国多年的神学研究之后,信也后来成为一名牧师和多产作家和翻译。 他逐渐相信,《旧约》表明了罪恶是“人类的最终问题”,并明确指出基督是答案。

在试图理解为什么如此少的日本人成为基督徒时,他感到部分是由于他们的自豪感,因为他们相信他们是优越的种族。

至于他在新西兰度过的三个圣诞节,作者Don Stephens写道:"在他收到的所有礼物中,他最珍视的一件是`上帝在耶稣基督中无限和深厚的恩惠与和平 ' 。 日本战俘在营地发现「自由」,

articles.summary_zh:

articles.title_zh: 在西部明星的阴影下：格罗弗·刘易斯、拉里·麦克默特里和文字的胜利
articles.content: With The Grover Lewis Reader: Splendor in the Short Grass and Western Star , the newest biography of Larry McMurtry, in hand, I load my truck and head toward Archer City, Texas, accompanied by my wife, Melanie, and our friend Eliott. Archer City is, of course, McMurtry country, a small Texas town made famous through the literary imagination of one of America’s most celebrated novelists. Having written about McMurtry’s faith—or lack thereof—in a previous article , following an earlier visit to Archer City, I’m returning with a somewhat different interest. This time, my attention turns to Grover Lewis, the gifted journalist, critic, and poet whose life intersected with McMurtry’s during their college years. Lewis’ story, however, begins not with literary achievement but with almost unimaginable tragedy. As a child, he experienced the devastating loss of both parents when his father murdered his mother and was subsequently shot with the same gun, either by his dying wife or another person present. Lewis was only eight years old. It is difficult to imagine a more horrific beginning. Yet rather than allowing that tragedy to become the entirety of his story, Lewis eventually found a voice through literature. Perhaps the cards life dealt him gave him plenty to write about. Or perhaps writing became his way of making sense of a world that had revealed its cruelty far too early. In his autobiographical poem “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis writes: “You asked me once, Ann/Over coffee gone cold with talk/In your mother’s rain-drowsy/House, who they were, how it/Was with them in their breathless/Time in the wilds of years.” For Lewis, those early years were indeed wild. But they were also the soil from which his literary imagination would eventually grow. A Life in Words Born in Texas in 1934, Grover Lewis emerged as a distinctive voice in American journalism, particularly through his cultural criticism and reporting on the rapidly changing landscape of the 1960s and 1970s. He became known for his sharp observations, literary flair, and ability to capture the personalities and contradictions of American culture, even if he occasionally stretched the truth in the telling. His work appeared in prominent publications, including Rolling Stone , where his reporting helped establish his reputation as an insightful, sometimes cutting observer of popular culture. Lewis was more than a journalist, however. He was a poet and literary craftsman, someone who understood that words could do more than convey information. They could illuminate the human condition, expose its contradictions, and perhaps even provide a measure of healing. Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) Continuing “Hillbilly Song,” Lewis ponders: “At last, breathless and dry-mouthed/With private desire in the blue,/Swollen dark, we all lie down together—/My mother, my father, their perishing/Dreams, and I this unborn prisoner son…” There is something haunting about these lines. The dead remain present. The past refuses to disappear. And the poet, even as an adult, seems to wrestle with the circumstances that shaped his entrance into the world. Yet the very act of writing suggests something else: a refusal to remain silent. Two Texans, Two Literary Paths Lewis and Larry McMurtry crossed paths as students at North Texas State College, now the University of North Texas, during the 1950s. Both were young Texans drawn to literature and the possibilities of the written word. Their friendship developed within a shared intellectual environment, one that encouraged reading, conversation, and the pursuit of literary ambitions. Although their careers eventually followed different paths—McMurtry toward novels, screenplays, and literary fame, Lewis toward journalism, poetry, and cultural criticism—they shared an interest in the complexities of American life. articles.content_zh:
与《格罗弗·刘易斯读者:短草中的辉煌与西部之星》,拉里·麦克默特里的最新传记, 手持,我装载我的卡车并前往德克萨斯州阿彻城, 由我的妻子梅兰妮和我们的朋友埃利奥特陪同。 阿彻城当然是麦克默特里国家,一个通过美国最著名的小说家之一的文学想象而成名的德克萨斯小镇.

在之前访问Archer城后, 我对McMurtry的信仰(或缺乏信仰)有一番兴趣, 这一次,我转而关注有天赋的记者、评论家和诗人格罗弗·刘易斯,他在大学时代的生活与麦克默特里的生活交织在一起。

然而,刘易斯的故事并非从文学成就开始,而是从几乎难以想象的悲剧开始. 他从小就经历了父母的惨痛损失,当时他的父亲谋杀了他的母亲,随后被他即将死亡的妻子或在场的其他人用同一把枪射杀。 刘易斯才八岁 很难想象一个更可怕的开端。

然而,刘易斯最终没有让这场悲剧成为他的全部故事,而是通过文学找到了声音. 也许他命中注定的卡片 给他写了很多东西 或写作成为他理解世界的方式, 这个世界已经揭示了它的残酷性,还为时过早。

刘易斯在自传诗“Hillbilly Song”中写道 : “ 你曾经问过我,Ann/Over咖啡随着谈话而变得冷淡,在你妈妈的雨滴/住所里,他们是谁,他们在无气息的年代/在野外时如何。 ” 对刘易斯来说,那些早年的确很狂野. 但它们也是他的文学想象最终会成长的土壤.

1934年出生于德克萨斯州的"言语生活"(A Life in Words Born in Texas),格罗弗·刘易斯(Grover Lewis)成为美国新闻业中一个有特色的代言人,特别是通过他对1960年代和1970年代迅速变化的地貌的文化批评和报道.

他以尖锐的观察,文学的才华,以及能够捕捉美国文化的个性和矛盾而闻名,即使他偶尔在讲述中伸张真理. 他的作品出现在包括滚石公司在内的著名出版物中,他的报道帮助他树立了自己作为有见地,有时剪切流行文化观察者的声誉.

然而,刘易斯不只是一名记者。 他是一位诗人和文学家,一个懂得文字可以比传递信息更有用的人. 它们可以揭示人类的状况,暴露其矛盾,甚至可能提供某种治疗方法。

Grover Lewis (ChatPGT) 继续“Hillbilly Song,” 刘易斯思考道:“最后,无气息和干燥的嘴唇/在蓝色的暗处私欲下,我们都躺在一起——/我的母亲、父亲、他们的死亡/梦想,我这个未出生的囚犯儿子......” 这些台词有些困扰。 死者仍然在场。 过去拒绝消失。

而诗人,即使作为一个成年人,似乎也与塑造他进入世界的环境相搏. 然而,写作本身就暗示了另一种情况:拒绝保持沉默。 两德克萨斯州立大学,两条文学道路刘易斯州立大学和拉里·麦克默特里(英语:Larry McMurtry)在1950年代作为北德克萨斯州立学院,即现在的北德克萨斯大学的学生跨过道路.

两人都是年轻的德克萨斯人,被吸引到文学和写字的可能性. 他们的友谊是在共同的知识环境中发展起来的,这种环境鼓励阅读,对话,追求文学野心.

尽管他们的职业生涯最终走的是不同的道路——小说、剧本和文学名人、刘易斯新闻、诗歌和文化批评——但他们对美国生活的复杂性有着共同的兴趣。 麦克默特里和刘易斯在大学期间(ChatGPT)都拥有超越德克萨斯州和美国西部神话的能力,认识到孤独,凝视

articles.summary_zh: 文：查尔斯·加德纳（Charles Gardner）——一位犹太籍陆军外科医生对一名年轻士兵的勇气感到惊叹，这名士兵在美国内战（1861-65）的葛底斯堡战役中身受重伤。为了挽救这个男孩的生命，马克斯·罗斯瓦利（Max Rossvally）博士不得不截肢，截掉了他的一条腿和一条胳膊。但这改变了他自己……  这篇题为《犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归向耶稣》的文章  最初发表在《上帝报道》上。
articles.title_zh: 犹太军医在目睹病人的勇气后归信耶稣
articles.content: Pastor Peter Colon portraying Major Rossvally in the movie of his story By Charles Gardner — A Jewish army surgeon was amazed by the courage of a young soldier badly wounded in the Battle of Gettysburg during the American Civil War (1861-65). Dr Max Rossvally was forced to amputate both a leg and arm in a bid to save the boy’s life. But it changed his own life. For the 17-year-old Drummer Boy – too young for frontline duty – refused chloroform or brandy to dull the pain. Charlie Coulson chose instead to trust in Jesus, his Lord and Saviour. The doctor – an army major and Orthodox Jew – was understandably stunned by the boy’s bravery, as well as his boldness in declaring his faith in Christ and imploring the officer (whom he knew to be Jewish) to put his own trust in Jesus, since he was also the Jewish Messiah. Max, however, was shaken rigid, and in a great dilemma, as he had always been taught to hate Jesus. For his people had largely rejected him as an ‘impostor’ and false Messiah. Charlie died just days later, apparently more concerned for the doctor’s eternal destiny than for his own painful exit from this life. Ten years later, Max found himself in a barber’s chair in New York once more being urged to trust in Jesus. Having explained the gospel, the barber promised to pray for him and said that, whenever he came in contact with a Jew, he felt it his duty to introduce him to the one who came for “the lost sheep of Israel” (Matthew 10:6). The surgeon subsequently boarded a train for a business meeting in Washington, where a newspaper advertisement drew him to a ‘revival’ service where the preacher echoed the messages he had heard from the barber and the boy soldier, leaving him in tears. He agonised at home in prayer for some time afterwards, struggling most of all with the thought that, if he accepted Christ, he would be going against all the advice and teaching he had known, not to mention the Jewish community as a whole. But he finally became convinced that Jesus was indeed the fulfilment of Old Testament prophecies (in particular, Genesis 49:10, Micah 5:2 and Isaiah 7:14). So he prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. You know I am sincere in this thing. If Jesus Christ is the Son of God, reveal him to me this night, and I will accept him as my Messiah.” A long battle ensued, but his doubts were eventually replaced by joy and happiness as he praised God that he had found the true Shiloh, Ruler of Israel and Emmanuel. He was to pay a high price, however, as do all who follow Christ. His wife walked out on him; his parents disowned him. But he never gave up hope as he constantly prayed and reached out to his family. After 54 days, his wife joined him as a disciple of Jesus and, in time, his daughter also became a believer. But his son disowned him for many years until he was eventually reconciled both with his earthly and heavenly Father. In an extraordinary sequel some 18 months after he came to Christ, Max met up with Mrs Coulson, the mother of his dying young patient all those years earlier on the battlefield. With great joy, he was able to share how her son had set him on the path to a glorious future in Christ, which was to touch lives across the world, including my home county of Yorkshire in England. In fact, he came to live in Leeds to reach out to the Jewish community there and is buried at Lawnswood Cemetery in the city. An Irish friend of mine, Colin Nevin, has visited the grave, which includes an excerpt from one of the doctor’s hymns, I am Coming Soon, and was able to give a copy of Max’s story to a caretaker, so continuing the evangelist’s legacy more than a century after his death in 1892, aged 64. A 54-minute movie – Rossvally: From the Synagogue to the Saviour – has been produced on DVD and can apparently be ordered online. The post Jewish army doctor turned to Jesus after witnessing patient’s courage first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
牧师彼得·科隆在他的故事电影"查尔斯·加德纳"(By Charles Gardner)中描绘了罗斯瓦利少校——一位犹太军队外科医生对美国内战期间格底斯堡战役(1861-65)中一名年轻士兵严重受伤的勇气感到惊讶. Max Rossvally医生被迫截肢, 但这改变了他自己的生活。

对于17岁的Drummer Boy — — 年龄太小,无法承担前线任务 — — 拒绝氯仿或白兰地来消磨疼痛。 查理·科尔森选择了信任耶稣,他的主和救世主.

这位医生是一名陆军少校和正统犹太人,对男孩的勇敢以及他大胆地宣布对基督的信仰,恳求军官(他知道是犹太人)相信耶稣是可以理解的,因为他也是犹太弥赛亚。 然而,马克思被动摇僵硬,陷入了巨大的困境,因为他一直被教导要憎恨耶稣.

他的宗族曾否认他是一个 " 骗子 " 和假的弥赛亚。 Charlie在几天后就去世了,显然更关心医生的永恒命运,而不是他自己痛苦地离开这一生。 10年后,马克思发现自己在纽约的理发师座椅上再次被敦促信任耶稣.

在解释了福音之后,理发师答应为他祈祷,并说每当他与一个犹太人接触时,他觉得有义务将他介绍给前来寻找“迷失的以色列羊”的人(Matthew 10:6)。

外科医生随后登上火车在华盛顿举行商务会议,报纸的广告将他引向 " 复活 " 服务,传教士重复了他从理发师和男孩士兵那里听到的信息,使他流泪。

他在家里苦苦地祈祷了一段时间,他首先想到,如果他接受基督,他将反对他所知道的所有建议和教导,更不用说整个犹太社区了。 但他最终确信耶稣确实是"旧约预言"的实现(特别是创世纪49:10,米迦5:2和以赛亚7:14).

他就祈祷说:易卜拉欣、易司哈格、叶尔孤白的主啊! 你知道我对这件事很真诚 如果耶稣基督是上帝之子,那么今晚把他告诉我,我将接受他为我的弥赛亚。” 一场漫长的战斗随之而来,但他的疑虑最终被欢乐和幸福所取代,因为他称赞上帝找到了真正的希洛,以色列统治者和埃马纽埃尔.

但他要付出高昂的代价,跟随基督的所有人一样。 他的妻子抛弃了他;他的父母抛弃了他。 但是,他从未放弃过希望,因为他不断祈祷和联系家人。 在54天后,他的妻子作为耶稣的门徒加入了他,在时间上,他的女儿也成为了信徒.

但他的儿子与他断绝关系多年,直到他最终与他的大地父和天父都和解. 在他来到基督的大约18个月之后的一段非凡续集中,马克思在战场上遇见了那些年前他死去的年轻病人的母亲科尔森夫人.

他怀着极大的喜悦,得以分享她儿子如何使他踏上基督辉煌未来的道路,这就是触摸世界各地的生活,包括我的家乡英格兰约克郡. 事实上,他来到利兹居住,向那里的犹太社区伸出援手,并被埋在城内的草坪林墓地.

我的一个爱尔兰朋友科林·内文参观了这个坟墓,其中包括医生颂歌"I am Coming Soon"的节录,并且能够把马克思的故事复制给看守人,因此在1892年去世后一个多世纪的福音派传承下来,享年64岁.

一部54分钟的电影 — — Rossvally: 从Synagogue到救世主 — 已经在DVD上制作,显然可以在网上订购. 在目睹病人的勇气首次出现在上帝的报告之后,

articles.title_zh: 两只卡车轮胎和一只白鸽教会了我信靠上帝
articles.content: By Mike Shreve — Tent meeting in the 80s Evangelism has been my focus for 55 years, ministering throughout the United States and in 14 other nations. God mercifully saved me during the Jesus Revolution (1970), out of a hippie lifestyle and a passionate, though misguided pursuit of truth through far eastern religious practices (yoga and meditation). Shortly after encountering Jesus and being delivered, along with another brother in the Lord, I began hitchhiking around the country, preaching the Gospel on street corners and college campuses. That developed through the years into ministry in churches, auditoriums, conferences, and tent crusades. Supernatural provision and divine intervention has always carried me, through every phase of this five-and-a-half-decade-long adventure. However, the following story is a classic. For about 25 years I carried big Gospel tents around the country. At the time of this “miracle,” I was transporting a 60’ x 90’ tent from one city to the next in an old, dilapidated bus that kept introducing new challenges to our amateur mechanic skills (putting it mildly). One day, on our way to Tampa, Florida—unfortunately—we hit a large pothole in the road that put a serious dent in the rear left rim on which a large truck tire was mounted. From that point, the inner tube would not retain air, making it necessary to stop every thirty miles or so to fill it up again . . . and again . . . and again . . . making the trip painfully slow. Adding to the problem, the other rear tire was bald, and we had no spare (couldn’t afford one). So, a flat would have brought us to a complete standstill. Sometimes, I think back on those days (when our zeal for the Kingdom outran any wisdom we might have possessed), and I marvel at the many times God took care of us anyway (like the loving heavenly Father that He is). Thousands of pounds of equipment were packed into that groaning, creaking, rusty, decrepit bus — heavy canvas tent sections, metal poles, stakes, platform, and 300 chairs—and only a few days allowed in between cities for transit and setup. No, we really could not afford any setbacks. And yes, a lot of “faith prayers” were uttered during every trip (or were they “presumptive proclamations”—not sure—maybe a mix of the two). An old split rim tire mounted on an old bus Once we got to Tampa, attempting to be frugal, I visited the junkyards hoping to find a used replacement rim. As if they had conspired to dissuade me, every junkyard owner/manager shot down my hopes with a similar assessment, “Fella, you won’t find one of them old split-rims anywhere. They’re dangerous. When you try to mount a tire on one, they can snap open and injure somebody real bad, cutting off a hand, even killing a person. We melted ‘em all down as scrap metal.” (Go ahead, look them up online—they were even called “widow-makers.”) It was the same story everywhere I went. Nobody could help. Then three weeks passed and we had to pack the bus and head to our next location—Bessemer City, North Carolina. It was a college-level, biblically-sound course on developing long-suffering and patience: stopping every thirty miles or so to air up that unpredictable tire, pleading with God to somehow supernaturally assist us in our journey by making sure none of the tires blew. Somehow, we made it—around 600 miles—stopping about 25 times. Then an incredible miracle happened! God did it and I still feel awestruck, just writing about it. As we turned into the fairgrounds area, right in the middle of the entrance were two brand new, neatly-stacked truck tires (unclaimed), exactly the size we used on the bus—mounted (you guessed it!) on the very same split rims our bus required. Talk about worshiping God—we launched into a praise session right then and there! What were the odds? We all knew it had to be God. Jehovah-Jireh (the Lord our provider) had fulfilled His amazing promise to do “exceedingly, abundantly above all” we could ask or think (Ephesians 3:20). Then li

麦克史瑞夫 80年代的帐篷会议是我55年来的焦点,在美国和14个其他国家担任部长。 上帝在耶稣革命期间(1970年)从嬉皮的生活方式和热情中怜悯地拯救了我,尽管通过远东宗教实践(瑜伽和冥想)错误地追求真理.

在遇到耶稣和被送走后不久,我与上帝的另一个兄弟一起,开始搭便车到全国各地,在街角和大学校园传福音. 多年来,这在教堂、礼堂、会议和帐篷十字军中发展成部。

超自然的供给和神的干预 总是让我在五年半的历险历程中 然而,以下的故事是一个经典的故事. 大约25年来,我在全国各地搭载着大型福音帐篷。

在这个“奇迹”发生时,我正用一辆老旧、破旧的公交车将60×90的帐篷从一个城市运送到另一个城市,这辆公交车不断给我们的业余技工技能带来新的挑战(轻轻地推开)。 有一天,在前往佛罗里达州坦帕的路上——不幸地——我们撞上了路边的一个大坑洞,在后左侧竖起一个大型卡车轮胎,后侧有严重的凹痕。

从此,内管不会保留空气,使得每30英里左右必须停一次才能再次填充. . . 再加上问题, 另一台后轮胎是秃头, 因此,一个公寓会 使我们完全停顿。

有时,我想起那些时候(那时我们对王国的热情超越了我们可能拥有的任何智慧),我惊讶地看到,无论怎样,上帝总是照顾我们(就像他那慈爱的天父)。

数千磅的设备被装进那辆呻吟、颤抖、生锈、破烂的巴士——重型帆布帐篷路段、金属杆、木桩、平台和300张椅子——而且只有几天时间允许在城市之间过境和布置。 不,我们真的无法承受任何挫折。

在每次旅行中都发表了许多“信仰祷告”(或它们是否“假定的宣告”——不确定——可能是两者的混合)。 一辆旧公共汽车上挂着一个旧的分叉轮圈轮胎 一旦我们到了坦帕, 试图节俭, 我参观了垃圾场 希望找到一个旧的替代轮圈。

就像他们密谋劝阻我一样, 每个垃圾场老板/经理都用类似的评估来击落我的希望, “伙计, 他们很危险。 当你试图安装一个轮胎, 他们可以撕开和伤害一个人 真正的坏,切断一只手,甚至杀死一个人。

我们把它们都融化成废金属。” 他们甚至被称为“寡妇制造者”。 我去过的地方都一样 没人能帮上忙 然后三个星期过去了,我们不得不收拾公交车 并前往下一个地点——北卡罗莱纳州的贝瑟默市。

这是一个关于发展长期痛苦和耐心的大学级、圣经般的教程:每隔30英里左右就停下来吹吹那个不可预测的轮胎,恳求上帝以某种超自然的方式协助我们的旅程,确保没有轮胎爆炸。 不知何故,我们大约在600英里的距离里,停了25次。 奇迹发生了!

上帝做到了,我仍然感觉 西车,只是写它。 当我们变成广场时, 就在入口的中间, 两个全新的, 整洁的卡车轮胎(无人认领), 说到崇拜上帝——我们发起了一次赞美会议,

什么机会? 我们都知道那是真主。耶和华已满足了。 他令人惊奇地承诺“超越一切, 然后说

articles.title: Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith
articles.summary: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno, in […]  The post  Rejoice in the Lamb: Benjamin Britten, Christopher Smart, and the Poetry of Faith  first appeared on  God Reports .
articles.summary_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现.

上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授 谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我受到很大启发,在[.]中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗歌,大庆阿格诺. 以及《信仰之诗》,
articles.title_zh: 喜悦羔羊：本杰明·布里顿、克里斯托弗·斯马特和信仰的诗歌
articles.content: When music meets poetry, the result can be more than art, it can become an expression of spiritual wonder. Christopher Smart The last time I heard Professor Bruce Redford speak about the eccentric British clergyman and poet Christopher Smart (1722–1771), I was so inspired that I included a substantial portion of Smart’s extraordinary poem, Jubilate Agno , in my book Beauty (And the Banana) . I described Smart as a theopoet , someone whose deep religious convictions found expression through a distinctive and imaginative poetic vision. Smart was no ordinary poet. His writings moved freely between the sacred and the seemingly mundane, finding divine significance in everything from biblical figures to animals and the natural world. His poetry was exuberant, unconventional, and, at times, wonderfully strange. For Smart, creation itself was a chorus of praise, and every living thing had a part to play. Recently, I had another opportunity to hear Redford explore Smart’s remarkable literary legacy, this time through the music of British composer Benjamin Britten (1913–1976). As part of an All Saints’ Day concert at the Cathedral of St. John in Albuquerque, New Mexico, celebrating Britten’s music, Redford delivered a pre-concert lecture focusing on the composer’s Rejoice in the Lamb , a choral masterpiece that brings Smart’s unusual poetry to life. The evening offered a fascinating intersection of literature, music, theology, and history, demonstrating how two artists separated by nearly two centuries could share a common vision of wonder. The Musical Imagination of Benjamin Britten Benjamin Britten. Photo: Public Domain. Redford, a former professor at Boston University who was living in England when Britten died in 1976, identified three defining characteristics of the composer’s work. First, Britten’s music is distinguished by “passion and variety.” His compositions resist easy categorization, moving between emotional intensity, dramatic storytelling, and moments of remarkable spiritual intimacy. Redford described Britten’s approach as creating a kind of musical parable, pointing to Curlew River , one of Britten’s church parables, as a particularly compelling example. Second, Britten demonstrated an extraordinary ability to balance “economy and scope.” Redford compared this quality to the novels of Jane Austen, whose carefully constructed narratives reveal entire worlds through seemingly modest details. Similarly, Britten could communicate profound emotional and spiritual truths through restrained musical means. Nothing was wasted; every note served a purpose. Third, and perhaps most important for the evening’s performance, Britten possessed an exceptional “sensitivity to words.” Redford described him as an “inspired” interpreter of literary texts, a composer who understood that music should not merely accompany poetry but illuminate its deeper meaning. It was this third characteristic that led Redford to Christopher Smart. When an Eccentric Poet Meets a Brilliant Composer In 1943, Britten composed Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30), a festival cantata scored for four soloists, SATB choir, and organ. The composition draws its text from Smart’s Jubilate Agno , a work of religious poetry that remained largely unknown for nearly two centuries. Christopher Smart Smart wrote much of the poem during his confinement in a private madhouse in eighteenth-century London. Its unconventional structure, biblical references, exuberant language, and seemingly spontaneous declarations of praise made it unlike almost anything else in English religious literature. The manuscript remained unpublished until W. F. Stead brought it to public attention in 1939. Soon afterward, the poet W. H. Auden introduced Britten to Smart’s newly published work while the composer was living in the United States. The connection proved fruitful. Britten recognized something remarkable in Smart’s poetry: an unrestrained celebration of creation that could be translated into music.
articles.content_zh:
当音乐与诗歌相遇时,结果可以超越艺术,成为精神奇迹的体现. 克里斯托弗·聪明 上次我听到布鲁斯·雷德福德教授谈到古怪的英国神职人员和诗人克里斯托弗·斯马特(1722–1771)时,我深受启发,在我的书《美人(和香蕉)》中包含了一大部分斯马特非凡的诗集《阿格诺大庆》。

我形容Smart是一位戏剧家, 聪明不是普通诗人 他的著作在圣人和看似庸俗的人之间自由移动,在从圣经人物到动物和自然世界的一切事物中都发现了神圣的意义.

他的诗歌充满了活力,与众不同,有时也非常奇怪. 对于Smart来说,创作本身是赞美的合唱,每一个活物都有角色可以扮演. 最近,我又有机会听到雷德福德探索Smart杰出的文学遗产,这次是通过英国作曲家本杰明·布里顿的音乐(1913–1976).

作为新墨西哥州阿尔布开克圣约翰大教堂庆祝布列顿音乐的全圣人节音乐会的一部分,雷德福德发表了一场音乐会前演讲,重点讲述了作曲家在羊羔中的欢乐,这是一部将斯马特不寻常的诗歌带给人生的奇特杰作.

晚上提供了文学、音乐、神学和历史的奇妙交汇点,展示了两个艺术家如何在将近两个世纪的时间里分开,可以分享一个共同的奇观。 本杰明·布林顿·本杰明·布林顿的音乐想象. 图片:公共域名.

雷德福德(Redford)是波士顿大学前教授,1976年布里顿逝世时居住在英国,他确定了作曲家作品的三个决定性特征. 首先,布列顿的音乐以“热情和多样性”来区分。 他的构思抵制轻松的分类,在情感的强度,戏剧性的故事性,以及非凡的精神亲密的时刻之间移动.

Redford将布列顿的做法描述为创造了一种音乐比喻,指向了布列顿教堂比喻之一的Curlew River,作为特别有说服力的例子.

第二,Britten表现出了平衡“经济和范围”的非凡能力。 雷德福德将这种品质与简·奥斯汀的小说相比较,他精心构建的叙事通过看似微小的细节揭示了整个世界. 同样,布列顿可以通过受约束的音乐手段传达深刻的情感和精神真理. 没有浪费任何东西;每张纸条都有作用。

第三,或许对晚间演出来说最重要的,布列顿拥有一种非凡的“言语敏感性 ” 。 Redford将他描述为文学文本的“受启发的”解释者,他是一个作曲家,他明白音乐不应仅仅伴随着诗歌,而应阐明其更深层次的意义。 正是这第三个特征导致雷德福找到克里斯托弗·斯马特.

1943年,当一位爱心诗人遇到一位杰出的作曲家时,布列顿在"羔羊"(Op. 30)中编曲了"欢乐"(Rejoice in the Lamb (Op. 30)),一个节日的Cantata为四位独奏家,SATB合唱团和管风琴打分. 内容来自Smart's Jubilate Agno, 一部宗教诗歌作品,

克里斯托弗·斯马特(Christopher Smart Smart)在18世纪伦敦一个私人疯人院禁闭期间写下了这首诗的大部分内容. 它的非常规结构,圣经的参考文献,兴旺的语言,以及看似自发的赞美宣言,使得它几乎不同于英国宗教文献中的其他任何内容. 手稿直到W. F.

施泰德在1939年引起了公众的注意. 不久之后,诗人W·H·奥登(W. H. Auden)在作曲家在美国居住期间,向布里顿介绍了斯马特新出版的作品. 这种联系证明是富有成果的。 Britten在Smart的诗歌中承认了一些令人瞩目的事物:一种可以被翻译成音乐的无限制的创作庆典.

articles.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
articles.content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . articles.content_zh:
据报告,11月10日,民主同盟军伊斯兰叛乱分子在刚果东北部伊图里省曼巴萨县发动了新的袭击,造成26人死亡,另有数人被绑架,该国近93%的人口是基督教徒。

据当地协会协调员Malikidogo说,有6个以上的村庄受到影响,其中包括Kangwayi、Misele、Mingazi和Mambaka。 “局势非常严重;我们确认有26人被杀害,另有数人被绑架,许多家庭仍在寻找失踪的亲人。”

“除了许多人的死亡外,还有五所房屋与一些摩托车一起被烧毁。 我们呼吁当局采取紧急行动保护人民。” 成功逃脱的幸存者一无所有地离开,报告说,许多家庭不得不逃命,留下家园和财物。

一位幸存者说,“当我们意识到敌人已经在村里时,我们非常害怕,当我们听到人们在哭,而其他人则朝每个方向奔跑时”。 “我们刚刚逃离,没有时间收集我们的财产,只是为了拯救我们的生命。

我们不知道接下来会发生什么,我们担心他们会来到我们今天所在的曼巴萨市。” 袭击发生在当地社区面临埃博拉威胁的困难时刻。 居民们现在正在处理对疾病的恐惧和进一步攻击的危险。

人们担心暴力也可能使控制埃博拉疫情变得更加困难。 逃离村庄的人可能把这种疾病传播到其他社区,而不安全则可能妨碍保健工作者帮助需要医疗帮助的人。 一名当地领导人还对局势表示关切,呼吁加强对平民的保护。

他说,“由于民主同盟军伊斯兰恐怖分子的暴行,我们受苦多年。” “我们已经在与埃博拉作斗争,现在我们再次面临这些袭击。 我们不能继续这样生活。 我们要求政府和安全部队在更多的无辜者丧生之前保护我们的社区。” 阅读更多新闻,

articles.title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
articles.content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . 马巴拉科再次面临民主同盟军的暴力, 据当地民间社会代表说,死亡人数从最初的3人增加到4人,而在致命的入侵中,还有七座房屋被点燃。

袭击使已经因不到一周前袭击Cantine-Aloya的暴力而受到创伤的平民再次感到恐惧。 这两起袭击在时间和地点上接近,使人们更加担心民主同盟军对贝尼各地平民继续构成威胁。 幸存者穆尔瓦哈利说:“我们生活在持续的恐惧之中”。

“我们尚未从坎廷发生的痛苦中恢复过来,在那里,无辜者惨遭杀害,家园沦为灰烬。 现在,暴力已蔓延到马巴拉科,我们再次哀悼我们的亲人,并观看我们的家园被烧毁。 我们不知道下一个是谁,也不知道这些袭击者将在哪里再次袭击。 我们甚至厌倦了无头埋葬我们的人民。

我们只想在家中过上和平的生活和睡觉,而不必担心再有早晨。” 地方民间社会代表呼吁安全部门全面负责保护平民,加强安全行动,防止进一步的袭击。

还敦促Runzayi、Malondo、Ngazi和Kibunamaru的居民保持警惕,保持平静,并与安全部队合作,报告可疑行动。 一位当地天主教主教说,“我们不能继续受武装袭击者的摆布”。

“虽然刚果(金)武装部队的干预有助于限制对马巴拉科的破坏,但袭击者可能袭击并消失而不了解他们的方向这一事实使我们深感恐惧。 我们要的是安全,而不是另一次屠杀。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件

After…   The post  The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage  first appeared on  International Christian Concern .
articles.summary_zh: 11月6日，一名名叫阿贾克·马比奥尔（Ajak Mabior）的18岁基督徒女孩在南苏丹琼莱州因拒绝接受家人包办的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。她本应嫁给一位年长的穆斯林男子——由于她的基督教信仰以及不愿意被强迫结婚，她反对这桩婚事。此后……   这篇题为《因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩》的文章  最初发表在  国际基督徒关注组织  网站上。
articles.title_zh: 因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害的女孩
articles.content: On Nov. 6, an 18-year-old Christian girl named Ajak Mabior was beaten to death in Jonglei, South Sudan, after refusing to enter a forced marriage arranged by her family. She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it. After attempting to escape, she was killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives. A Common Problem The killing has raised serious concerns among Christian leaders about the pressure Christian girls face when their faith and personal convictions conflict with family expectations. “When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor said. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.” For Christian girls in South Sudan , forced marriages can become a matter of religious persecution when they are pressured to marry outside their faith and abandon their Christian convictions. Those who refuse may face rejection, threats, intimidation, and violence from their own families. Mabior’s death highlights the vulnerability of young Christian women who seek to remain faithful to Christ while facing pressure to submit to marriages that violate their faith and conscience. “The church teaches that every life is precious because it is created in the image of God,” the pastor added. “Yet when a Christian girl refuses a marriage that would bind her against her will, she can be treated as a traitor to the community. We have buried too many who paid that price.” Seeking Justice The authorities’ response has added to the church’s concerns. Police reportedly released the suspects without the consent of the Jonglei State Caretaker Commissioner. The justification that the suspects were relatives raises serious questions about the protection available to Christian girls facing forced marriages and violence. When perpetrators are released without facing justice, vulnerable Christian women are left with little confidence that the authorities will protect their right to practice their faith and make decisions according to their conscience. “We preach freedom in Christ, but our young people still live in fear of the consequences of that freedom,” the pastor said. “If the police and local authorities remain quiet, the church becomes the only place left where these girls and boys can find a voice. We need courage to speak, and we need the wider Body of Christ to stand with us.” Mabior’s case raises concerns about forced interfaith marriages, religious pressure, and violence against young Christian women in South Sudan. “We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an International Christian Concern (ICC) staffer said. “Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Girl They Killed for Refusing a Forced Marriage first appeared on International Christian Concern .
articles.content_zh:
11月6日,一名名叫Ajak Mabior的18岁基督教女孩在南苏丹琼格莱州因拒绝参加家庭安排的强迫婚姻而被殴打致死。 她被期望嫁给一个年长的穆斯林男子——她反对这种婚姻,因为她的基督教信仰以及她不愿意被迫加入. 在试图逃跑后,她被自己的哥哥和表妹杀死.

几天后,Bor的警察逮捕了这两名男子,但在家属要求他们自由后,在没有指控的情况下将他们释放,他们辩称“没有案件”,因为他们是亲属。 常见问题 杀害事件引起了基督教领袖的严重关切,基督教女孩在信仰和个人信念与家庭期望相冲突时面临压力。

“当一名年轻女孩因拒绝强迫婚姻而被杀害,而杀人者因是家人而自由行动时,信息是明确的:传统比法律更强大,比生命的价值更强大。” 一位当地牧师说。

“我们许多基督教女儿生活在这种阴影下。” 对于南苏丹的基督教女孩来说,当她们被迫在信仰之外结婚并放弃基督教信仰时,强迫婚姻就可能成为宗教迫害的问题。 拒绝者可能面临自己家庭的排斥、威胁、恐吓和暴力。

Mabior的死亡凸显了基督教青年妇女的脆弱性,她们试图保持对基督的忠诚,同时面临压力,迫使她们向违反其信仰和良心的婚姻屈服。 牧师补充说,“教会教导每一条生命都是宝贵的,因为它是以上帝的形象创造的。”

“当一个基督教女孩拒绝违背她意愿而束缚她的婚姻时,她可以被当作一个叛徒对待。 我们埋葬了太多付出这一代价的人。” 寻求正义 当局的反应增加了教会的关注。 据报告,警方未经琼格莱州看守专员同意释放了嫌疑人。

关于嫌疑人是亲属的理由,令人对面临强迫婚姻和暴力的基督教女孩获得的保护提出严重问题。 当肇事者在没有受到法律制裁的情况下被释放时,脆弱的基督教妇女对当局将保护其信仰和根据其良心作出决定的权利缺乏信心。

牧师说,“我们在基督中宣扬自由,但我们的年轻人仍然生活在对这种自由的后果的恐惧之中。” “如果警察和地方当局保持安静,教堂就成了这些女孩和男孩能够发表意见的唯一地方。

我们需要勇气说话,我们需要更广泛的基督与我们站在一起。” Mabior案引起了人们对南苏丹境内强迫不同信仰间婚姻、宗教压力以及针对基督教青年妇女的暴力的关注。

“我们呼吁广大的基督机构为阿贾克的正义祈祷,并保护因信仰而面临强迫婚姻的基督教女孩。” 一位国际基督教关注组织的工作人员说。

“祈祷教会有勇气反对宗教胁迫和暴力,并祈祷当局将维护法律,保护脆弱的信徒。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

articles.title_zh: 持续向慕拉第献金奉献，有助于为中东的失聪群体提供福音传播的机会
articles.content: An IMB missionary among the Deaf records a Bible story in sign language. IMB Photo Every dollar you give to the Lottie Moon offering goes to support missionaries like Noah Lewis who live and serve among the lost. Will you consider giving today? Noah Lewis couldn’t help signing along with a worship song playing in the background as Deaf friends gathered in his home for dinner. The International Mission Board appoints missionaries who are both Deaf and hearing to serve among the global Deaf. Many missionaries learn sign language for the first time, while others use their American Sign Language to more quickly learn global sign languages. IMB Photo The International Mission Board missionary was sitting in the living room with his roommate and two friends while others prepared food nearby. As a young, single adult, simply opening the doors to his home in the Middle East has created some of his most fruitful opportunities for gospel conversations. That evening, Lewis was stirred to worship the Lord. “I just love worshiping in sign language because it’s a full-body experience,” Lewis said. Lewis, who is hearing, began signing the song in American Sign Language. Across the room, one of his Muslim friends watched intently. When the song ended, his friend told him it was beautiful and asked to see another. Lewis explained that Christians use songs to worship God. His friend compared what he had seen to hearing the Islamic call to prayer. The exchange opened an opportunity for Lewis to explain Christian worship and why Christians worship Jesus. When his friend asked to see more, Lewis continued signing songs from the playlist. “He was just really captivated by it,” Lewis said. “It really felt like in that moment the Spirit was working in his heart.” The conversation did not end with a profession of faith. Instead, it became another step in a friendship where Lewis has watched spiritual curiosity grow over time. During Ramadan, the same friend asked about fasting. On another night, he asked how Christians pray. Each question has allowed Lewis to explain what Christians believe and why he follows Jesus. Those conversations reflect much of Lewis’ ministry. He has served in the Middle East for nearly a year and a half, spending much of his time learning sign language and building relationships in the local Deaf community. Learning sign language, like learning any language, requires time, practice and immersion in the community that uses it. For Lewis, that process has looked different from the experience of missionaries who can spend several hours each day in a formal language school. There are no comparable sign language centers where he serves, so much of his language learning happens through relationships with Deaf friends. Although Lewis has not had a dedicated language tutor since arriving on the field, personal relationships help him develop a strong conversational understanding of the sign language used where he serves. The process has also drawn him more deeply into the Deaf community he came to reach. “I want to genuinely learn about their language,” he said. “I want to be friends with them. I want to know who they are.” As Lewis’ ability to communicate grows, relationships deepen and opportunities to share the gospel follow. Even when he doesn’t know the exact sign he needs, friends help him find ways to communicate biblical truths. Lewis has learned to faithfully use the language he has while continuing to grow in his ability to communicate the gospel clearly. An IMB worker among the Deaf records a Bible story. Generous giving to the Lottie Moon Christmas Offering supports missions among the global Deaf. IMB Photo When the plan disappeared That dependence on God came into clearer focus during a recent trip to Central Asia. Lewis currently lives and serves in the Middle East, but he arrived on the field with a long-term desire to serve in Central Asia. articles.content_zh:
一名IMB在聋人中的传教士用手语记录圣经故事. IMB照片 你给洛蒂月球的每一美元 都用来支持传教士 比如诺亚·刘易斯 你会考虑今天给钱吗? 当聋人朋友聚集在家中吃饭时,

国际代表团委员会任命聋人和听力传教士在全球聋人中任职。 许多传教士首次学习手语,而其他传教士则使用他们的美国手语更快地学习全球手语.

IMB照片 国际传教委员会传教士与他的室友和两个朋友坐在客厅里,而其他人则在附近准备食物. 作为一个年轻、单身的成年人,只要打开通往他在中东的家的大门,就为他的福音对话创造了一些最富有成果的机会。 当晚,刘易斯被激起崇拜主.

「我只是喜欢手语崇拜, 正在听话的刘易斯开始用美国手语签署歌曲. 在房间里,他的一个穆斯林朋友故意观看。 歌曲结束的时候,他的朋友告诉他这很美丽,并请求见另一首. 刘易斯解释说,基督徒使用歌曲来崇拜上帝.

他的朋友比较了他所看到的听到的伊斯兰祈祷的呼声. 这次交流为刘易斯解释基督教崇拜和基督徒为何崇拜耶稣提供了机会. 当他的朋友要求看到更多时,刘易斯继续从播放列表上签名歌曲. 刘易斯说:“他只是被它迷住了。”

“在那个时刻,精神确实在他心中发挥作用。” 对话没有以信仰职业结束。 相反,它成为友谊的又一个步骤,刘易斯目睹了精神好奇心随时间推移而增长. 斋月期间,同友问斋事. 在另一个晚上,他问基督徒如何祈祷.

每个问题都让刘易斯解释基督徒相信什么,为什么他跟随耶稣. 这些谈话反映了刘易斯部的许多情况。 他在中东服务了近一年半,花了很多时间学习手语,在当地聋人社区建立关系.

学习手语,就像学习任何语言一样,需要时间,练习和沉浸在使用手语的社区中. 对刘易斯来说,这一进程与传教士的经历不同,传教士可以每天在一所正式语言学校中度过几个小时。

他所服务的手语中心并不存在类似的手语中心,所以他的许多语言学习都是通过与聋人朋友的关系发生的. 虽然刘易斯自到达球场后便没有专门的语言辅导员,但个人关系帮助他发展出对他所服务的手语的强烈的对话理解.

这一过程还使他更深入地融入了他所接触的聋人社区。 他说:“我想真正了解他们的语言。” “我想与他们成为朋友。 我想知道他们是谁。” 随着刘易斯沟通能力的增长,关系加深,分享福音的机会随之而来。

即使他不知道自己需要什么具体标志, 刘易斯学会了忠实使用他拥有的语言,同时继续增强他明确传达福音的能力. 一个IMB工人在聋人中记录了一个圣经故事. 慷慨地给洛蒂月亮圣诞节 提供全球聋人中的支持任务

IMB 图片 当计划消失时 在最近访问中亚期间,这种对上帝的依赖得到了更明确的关注。 刘易斯目前在中东生活和服役,但他远期带着在中亚服役的愿望赶到现场. 他最近的旅行使他能够更多地了解文化,聋人社区
