articles.title: Aku Simon dari Kirene
articles.summary_zh: 我是来自古利内的西门。 我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。
articles.title_zh: 我是古利奈人西门。
articles.content: Aku Simon dari Kirene. Namaku menunjukkan bahwa aku tinggal di benua Afrika. Meski demikian, kulitku tidak hitam dan bibirku pun tidak tebal. Dan meskipun sudah selama beberapa generasi keluargaku berdiam di Kirene, ibu kota Kireneika -- sebuah kota Yunani di Afrika Utara yang terkenal karena kemakmuran dan para ahli filsafatnya -- kulitku tidaklah putih. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku orang Yahudi asli sampai ke jantung hati. Sejak kecil, kutaati semua hukum agama tanpa kecuali, walaupun aku tidak lagi fasih berbahasa Aram akibat dibesarkan dalam masyarakat yang berbahasa Yunani. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku tidak ingin berkisah tentang diri sendiri. Juga tidak tentang semua pengalaman hidupku. Aku cuma ingin bercerita tentang pengalamanku yang satu itu. Pengalaman yang kemudian mengubah seluruh jalan hidupku. Dan seluruh jalan hidup Anda, sekiranya Anda juga mengalaminya. Hari itu adalah hari Jumat. Aku baru saja tiba di Yerusalem pagi itu. Tujuanku melakukan perjalanan yang jauh itu adalah untuk merayakan hari raya Paskah. Setiap tahun aku melakukannya. Tidak sedikit pun aku heran melihat orang-orang penuh sesak memadati kota. Walaupun letih, segera setelah menaruh barang-barangku di hotel dan membersihkan badan, aku keluar berjalan-jalan untuk menikmati keriuhan kota yang sedang larut dalam semarak pesta. Lengking jeritan anak-anak yang berlari ria kian kemari, teriakan membujuk bahkan kadang-kadang memaksa para pedagang yang menjajakan barang-barangnya, dan bau asap dupa atau suara syahdu orang-orang yang menyanyikan kidung-kidung pujaan -- semua itu membuat aku lupa akan keletihanku. Suasana yang agak liar ini memang berbeda benar dengan suasana Kirene yang sopan dan tertib. Namun, lebih hidup. Tiba-tiba ada kegaduhan yang tak biasa. Para serdadu Roma menyeruak massa. "Ah, lagi-lagi pawai laskar-laskar Romawi untuk mengingatkan siapa yang berkuasa di negeri ini," pikirku. Akan tetapi tidak. Di baris paling depan, ada seorang serdadu yang memegang panji bertulis: "Yesus, orang Nazaret, raja orang Yahudi." Aku memang belum pernah berjumpa dengan-Nya. Akan tetapi, nama "Yesus", siapa yang tidak mengenal-Nya? Dia adalah tokoh paling kontroversial. Yang tidak dapat kumengerti, mengapa serdadu Romawi mengarak panji seperti itu. Karena itu, aku mendekat untuk melihat lebih dekat. Di tengah pagar betis laskar-laskar Roma itu, tiga orang melangkah pelan memanggul salib. "Penjahat-penjahat besar," pikirku. Namun, apa hubungannya dengan panji itu? Kemudian aku semakin mengerti. Riuh rendah massa rakyat menyebut-nyebut nama Yesus sambil mencemooh-Nya. Tidak kurang pula yang meludahi-Nya. Akan tetapi, yang manakah Yesus di antara ketiga orang itu? Aku Simon dari Kirene. Aku semakin mendekat. Lalu aku tahu dengan pasti yang mana Yesus. Dia paling kecil, hampir tidak berotot. Rambut panjang-Nya terurai, lekat di sana-sini oleh darah kering yang berasal dari duri-duri yang teranyam di kepala-Nya. Sekujur tubuh-Nya biru lebam. Langkah-Nya tertatih-tatih. Amat letih. Akan tetapi mata-Nya -- meski merah sebab kurang tidur -- namun tetap tajam menusuk setiap kali menatap. Anehnya, juga begitu lembut menyejukkan. Aku tak dapat lepas memandang mata-Nya itu. Penuh wibawa, tetapi juga begitu menenangkan dan kebapakan. Lalu Dia roboh. Tubuh-Nya yang kecil dan nyaris hancur itu tidak kuat lagi menahan bobot salib di pundak-Nya. Massa berteriak kesenangan bagai binatang liar yang haus darah. Cemeti melayang menyayat punggung-Nya. Darah menyembur. Dan Dia pun bangkit lagi pelan-pelan. Keletihan. Tetapi mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. Lalu Dia berjalan beberapa langkah. Namun, roboh lagi. Arak-arakan berhenti. Massa semakin buas. Cemeti melayang berulang-ulang. Darah menyembur. Namun, Dia tak mampu bangun kembali. Aku Simon dari Kirene. Entah mengapa, aku tidak terkesan benar oleh semua itu. Kecuali oleh tatapan mata-Nya. Mata-Nya itu, oi, mata-Nya. 我是来自古利内的西门。我的名字表明我住在非洲大陆。尽管如此，我的皮肤并不黑，嘴唇也不厚。尽管我的家族已经在昔兰尼生活了几代人，昔兰尼是昔兰尼加的首府，这是一座位于北非的希腊城市，以其繁荣和哲学家而闻名，但我的肤色并不白。我是古利奈的西门。

我从心底里是一个地道的犹太人。从小到大，我毫无例外地遵守所有宗教律法，尽管由于在讲希腊语的社区长大，我已经不再精通阿拉姆语。我是古利奈人西门。我不想谈论我自己。也不想讲述我所有的生活经历。我只想讲述我那一次的经历。

这段经历后来改变了我的人生轨迹。如果您也经历过，那么也会改变您的人生轨迹。那天是星期五。那天早上我刚抵达耶路撒冷。我长途跋涉的目的就是为了庆祝逾越节。我每年都这样做。看到熙熙攘攘的人群挤满了这座城市，我一点也不感到惊讶。

尽管很累，但在酒店放下行李并洗漱完毕后，我还是出门散步，享受这座沉浸在节日气氛中的城市的喧嚣。

到处跑来跑去的孩子们尖叫声，叫卖的小贩们劝诱甚至有时强迫的吆喝声，还有熏香的味道或人们吟唱赞美诗的悠扬声音——这一切都让我忘记了疲惫。这种略显喧闹的氛围与古利奈文雅有序的氛围截然不同，但却更有活力。

突然间，出现了一阵不寻常的喧哗。罗马士兵挤过人群。“唉，又是罗马士兵的游行，用来提醒人们谁才是这个国家的统治者。”我想。但是不是。在最前面一排，有一名士兵拿着一面旗帜，上面写着：“拿撒勒人耶稣，犹太人的王。” 我确实从未见过祂。

但是，“耶稣”这个名字，谁不认识他呢？他是最具争议的人物。我不明白的是，为什么罗马士兵要举着这样的旗帜游行。因此，我走近仔细观察。在罗马士兵的方阵中间，有三个人背着十字架缓缓前行。“大坏蛋，”我想。不过，这和那面旗帜有什么关系？

然后我渐渐明白了。人群喧嚣着，一边喊着耶稣的名字，一边嘲笑祂。还有不少人向祂吐唾沫。但是，这三个人当中哪一个是耶稣呢？我是古利奈人西门。我走得越来越近。然后我确切地知道谁是耶稣。他是三人中个子最小的，几乎没有肌肉。

祂的长发散乱，这里那里都沾满了干涸的血迹，这些血迹来自祂头上戴着的荆棘冠。祂的全身都瘀青了。祂的步伐蹒跚。祂非常疲惫。但是祂的眼睛——尽管因为睡眠不足而发红——但每次注视时仍然锐利如刀。奇怪的是，他的眼神也如此温柔、令人舒心。我无法移开视线，不去看祂的眼睛。

充满威严，但也非常平和和慈父般。然后祂倒下了。祂瘦小而几乎破碎的身体再也承受不住肩上十字架的重量。人群像嗜血的野兽一样欢呼雀跃。鞭子抽打着祂的背。鲜血喷涌而出。祂又慢慢地站了起来。祂疲惫不堪。但是祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

然后他走了几步。然而，祂又倒下了。游行队伍停了下来。人群变得越来越凶狠。鞭子一次又一次地挥舞着。鲜血喷涌而出。然而，祂再也无法站起来了。我是古利奈人西门。不知为何，这一切并没有真正触动我。除了祂的眼神。祂的眼睛，哎呀，祂的眼睛。

因此，当一名士兵突然拉我时，我好像失去了知觉。然后把十字架放在我身上。

articles.title: Kasih Tuhan Tiada Taranya
articles.summary_zh: p style="margin-bottom:1em; ">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。
articles.title_zh: 上帝的爱是无与伦比的
articles.content: p style="margin-bottom:1em;">Oleh: Romauli br Marpaung Shalom, Nama saya Romauli br Marpaung. Saat ini, saya berusia 23 tahun. Saya berasal dari keluarga Kristen. Saya anak pertama dari lima bersaudara. Keluarga saya, dahulunya, bukan keluarga yang harmonis. Orang tua saya sering bertengkar. Namun, saat kelas IV SD, bapak saya bertobat sungguh-sungguh dan menyerahkan dirinya untuk diperlengkapi di Sekolah Alkitab Purbasari Pematang Siantar. Setelah selesai sekolah, beliau akhirnya diangkat menjadi seorang Pendeta, dan saya mulai pelayanan sejak kelas V SD di Gereja Kemuliaan Sion sebagai pemain musik tunggal. Pada 2013, saat saya lulus SMA, saya berharap bisa kuliah di Universitas Sumatera Utara (USU) Medan. Namun, saat mengikuti SBMPTN, saya gagal karena tidak lulus seleksi. Akhirnya, bapak saya mengusulkan supaya saya kuliah di Solo karena dia punya rekan pendeta yang anaknya kuliah di Solo juga. Saya mengikuti keinginan bapak saya karena beliau rindu saya bisa menjadi seorang hamba Tuhan. Akhirnya, saya kuliah di STT Berita Hidup, Solo, dan mengikuti semua kegiatan, aturan yang ada di kampus tersebut. Saya dibaptis saat duduk di bangku SMA kelas XI. Awalnya, saya kuliah di Berita Hidup karena orang tua dan pelarian, tetapi pada akhirnya saya bertobat dan percaya sungguh-sungguh kepada Tuhan Yesus saat kuliah semester 2. Pelayanan-pelayanan yang Tuhan percayakan kepada saya itu tidak mudah. Ada banyak masalah yang saya hadapi, baik itu dari asrama, tempat pelayanan, maupun kampus. Kalau bukan karena kekuatan Tuhan, mungkin saya tidak mampu. Namun, Tuhan Yesus baik, Dia memberi pertolongan saat saya benar-benar tidak mampu menjalaninya. Saya pelayanan di Gereja Bethel Tabernakel, Karanganyar. Saya mulai melayani di sana sejak Agustus 2014 sampai saat ini. Saya dipercaya untuk melayani di beberapa bagian, seperti melayani anak-anak sekolah minggu, pemuda/remaja, jemaat dewasa, maupun yang sudah lanjut usia. Selain itu, saya juga ambil bagian dalam musik, yaitu melatih anak-anak sekolah minggu belajar musik. Selain itu, saya juga diberi kesempatan oleh pendeta saya untuk membuka Bimbingan Belajar di Bibis Luhur Solo. Sewaktu kuliah, saya ditempatkan praktik tahunan di Gereja Kristus Rahmani Indonesia (GKRI), Jimbaran Bali. Tantangan yang saya hadapi adalah saya melayani orang-orang Kristen yang sudah berkeluarga, tetapi belum terikat dalam pernikahan. Saya juga membantu mengajar di PAUD Shinam, Jimbaran, milik gereja tersebut. Saya bersyukur untuk semua pelayanan yang telah dipercayakan gereja kepada saya. Saya bisa menjalani semua ini dengan pertolongan Tuhan. Yang saya rindukan dalam pelayanan adalah saya bisa memberikan yang terbaik untuk Tuhan dan gereja, menjadi berkat bagi banyak orang, dan tetap setia terhadap panggilan Tuhan. Saya juga rindu suatu saat saya bisa membuka pelayanan sendiri. Saya tahu itu tidak mudah, tetapi saya percaya kuasa pertolongan Tuhan nyata bagi saya. Kiranya kesaksian ini bisa menjadi berkat bagi semua orang, dan saya rindu kita tetap percaya bahwa segala sesuatu yang kita lakukan untuk Tuhan tidak akan kembali dengan sia-sia, melainkan Dia akan memberkati kita senantiasa (Kolose 3:23). Mulailah mengatakan bahwa pelayanan itu adalah sebuah kehormatan, bukan beban. Tuhan Yesus memberkati. "Dan, Maria berkata, "Sesungguhnya, aku ini hamba Tuhan. Terjadilah padaku seperti yang engkau katakan itu." Kemudian, malaikat itu pergi meninggalkannya."(Lukas 1:38, AYT)

p style="margin-bottom:1em;">作者：Romauli br Marpaung Shalom，我叫 Romauli br Marpaung。我今年 23 岁。我来自一个基督徒家庭。我是五个兄弟姐妹中的老大。我的家庭以前并不和谐。我的父母经常吵架。

然而，当我上小学四年级时，我父亲真心悔改，并前往位于Pematang Siantar的Purbasari圣经学校接受装备。毕业后，他最终被任命为牧师，而我从小学五年级开始就在锡安荣耀教会担任独奏乐手。

2013 年，当我高中毕业时，我希望能在棉兰的北苏门答腊大学 (USU) 上大学。然而，在参加全国统一高考（SBMPTN）时，我因为没有通过选拔而落榜了。最后，我父亲建议我去梭罗上大学，因为他有一位牧师朋友，他的孩子也在梭罗上大学。我听从了父亲的意愿，因为他希望我能成为神的仆人。

最后，我在梭罗的生命福音神学院（STT Berita Hidup）上学，并参加了该校的所有活动，遵守了该校的所有规定。我在读高一的时候受洗。起初，我因为父母和逃避现实的原因而就读于生命信息神学院，但最终我在第二学期时悔改并真心信靠主耶稣。

神托付给我的服侍并不容易。我面临着很多问题，无论是来自宿舍、事工场所还是校园。如果不是因为上帝的力量，我可能无法做到。然而，主耶稣是良善的，当我已经实在无法承受时，祂会伸出援手。我在卡朗亚尔的伯特利会幕教会（Gereja Bethel Tabernakel）服侍。

我从 2014 年 8 月开始在那里服侍，至今仍在继续。我受托在几个部门服侍，例如服侍主日学儿童、青年/青少年、成年会众以及老年人。此外，我还参与音乐方面的工作，即指导主日学儿童学习音乐。

此外，我的牧师还给了我机会，在梭罗的Bibis Luhur开设学习辅导班。在大学期间，我被安排在巴厘岛金巴兰的印度尼西亚基督慈悲教会（GKRI）进行年度实习。我面临的挑战是我要服侍那些已经有家庭但尚未缔结婚姻的基督徒。

我还协助在属于该教会的金巴兰 Shinam 幼儿教育中心（PAUD Shinam）进行教学。我感谢教会将所有这些事工托付给我。在神的帮助下，我能够做到这一切。我在侍奉中渴望的是，我能够为上帝和教会尽我所能，成为许多人的祝福，并始终忠于上帝的呼召。

我也希望有一天我能自己开办一间教会。我知道这并不容易，但我相信上帝的帮助对我来说是真实的。愿这个见证能成为所有人的祝福，我希望我们能继续相信，我们为神所做的一切都不会徒劳无功，祂必会永远赐福于我们（歌罗西书 3:23）。

开始说服自己，服侍是一种荣誉，而不是一种负担。愿主耶稣赐福。 “马利亚说：‘我是主的使女。愿照你的话成就在我身上。” 天使就离开她去了。”（路加福音 1:38，AYT）

articles.title_zh: 马来西亚法院将一名皈依基督教者的宗教自由诉讼移交地区法庭
articles.content: A 34-year-old law graduate’s multi-year battle exposes the severe reality of religious control and the legal trap facing citizens who want to leave Islam. A high-stakes constitutional challenge highlighting the erosion of religious freedom in Malaysia has taken a procedural step backward. The Kuala Lumpur High Court has ordered that a lawsuit filed by a 34-year-old legal researcher seeking legal recognition as a Christian be transferred to the Shah Alam High Court. The case lays bare the rigid and intrusive control exercised by state apparatuses and Islamic religious authorities over personal faith, showcasing a system where basic human rights — such as choosing one’s own religion — are tightly policed by the government. A Life Labeled Without Consent The plaintiff, Shameer PV, identifies as a Christian and has lived as one since he was 18. However, under strict Malaysian administrative regulations, the word “Islam” was stamped on his compulsory national identity card (MyKad) when he was just 12, following a bureaucratic policy introduced under the National Registration Act. Despite decades of personal conviction and his marriage to a Christian wife, the state continues to legally treat him as a Muslim, directly violating his parental and marital status and refusing to recognize his family. Shameer’s legal challenge names the federal government, the Selangor state government, and the Selangor Islamic Religious Council (MAIS) as defendants. He argues that labeling citizens by religion on state identity cards violates Article 11(1) of the Federal Constitution, which ostensibly guarantees every person the right to profess and practice their religion. Trapped in Shariah Bureaucracy Shameer’s ordeal underscores the labyrinthine and punishing hurdles forced upon religious minorities and converts in Malaysia’s dual-justice system, which runs a parallel set of Islamic (Shariah) courts alongside the civil judiciary. In 2018, Shameer initiated proceedings in a Selangor Shariah court seeking official recognition of his Christian faith. After an exhausting 72 court sessions spanning over seven years, the Shariah court dismissed his application in January. Rather than allowing him to move on with his life, the religious court went a step further, ordering state departments and Islamic authorities to “guide and control” his practice of Islam — effectively treating his desire to leave the faith as a disciplinary or correctional matter. Having exhausted the religious tribunal system, Shameer turned to the civil high court in July, filing an originating summons to ask the highest judicial authorities whether state-mandated religious labeling on identity cards is unconstitutional, and whether Shariah courts have any lawful jurisdiction over individuals who do not practice Islam. A Wider Crisis for Freedom of Conscience International human rights observers and religious freedom advocates have long criticized Malaysia’s legal framework regarding apostasy and conversion. While the Malaysian Constitution theoretically protects freedom of religion, civil courts have repeatedly ruled that only Islamic Shariah courts have the authority to permit someone to leave Islam — creating an effective judicial catch-22, as Shariah courts rarely grant permission to renounce the religion. For international human rights advocates and supporters of religious liberty, Shameer’s case is a stark reminder of the state-enforced religious controls facing millions in Southeast Asia. As his case moves to the Shah Alam court, the legal battle continues to test whether Malaysia’s secular constitutional framework can protect an individual’s fundamental right of conscience against a totalizing state religious bureaucracy. 一个34岁的法学毕业生的多年战斗暴露了宗教控制的严重现实和想要离开伊斯兰教的公民所面临的法律陷阱. 马来西亚宗教自由受到侵蚀,

吉隆坡高等法院下令将34岁法律研究者提出的寻求法律承认为基督徒的诉讼移交沙阿拉姆高等法院.

这一案件暴露了国家机构和伊斯兰宗教当局对个人信仰的严格和侵扰性控制,表明政府严格控制基本人权(如选择自己的宗教)的制度。 未经同意的生活标签 原告Shameer PV确认为基督教徒,自18岁起就一直作为一个教徒生活在一起。

然而,根据严格的马来西亚行政条例,他12岁时的强制性国民身份证(MyKad)上印有“伊斯兰”一词,这是根据《国家登记法》实行的官僚政策。

尽管几十年的个人信念和他与基督教妻子的婚姻,但国家继续在法律上将他视为穆斯林,直接侵犯了他的父母和婚姻状况,并拒绝承认他的家人. 沙门的法律质疑将联邦政府,雪兰莪州政府,雪兰莪伊斯兰宗教委员会(MAIS)列为被告.

他辩称,以宗教方式将公民贴在州身份证上违反了《联邦宪法》第11(1)条,该条表面上保障每个人信奉和奉行其宗教的权利。

伊斯兰教法官僚沙姆耶的折磨凸显了Labyrinthine和惩罚强加给宗教少数派和皈依马来西亚双重司法制度的障碍,马来西亚的双重司法制度与民事司法平行设有一套伊斯兰(伊斯兰教法)法院。 2018年,沙姆耶在塞兰哥教法法院提起诉讼,寻求官方承认他的基督教信仰.

经过历时七年的72次开庭,教法法院于1月驳回了他的申请。

宗教法庭没有让他继续自己的生活,而是更进一步,命令国家部门和伊斯兰当局“指导和控制”他的伊斯兰教习俗——实际上将他放弃信仰的愿望视为纪律或惩戒事项。

在用尽了宗教法庭制度之后,Shameer于7月向民事高等法院提交了原传票,询问最高司法当局在身份证上贴上国家规定的宗教标签是否违宪,伊斯兰教法法院是否对不信奉伊斯兰教的个人拥有任何合法管辖权。

国际人权观察员和宗教自由倡导者长期批评马来西亚关于叛教和皈依的法律框架。

虽然马来西亚宪法理论上保护宗教自由,但民事法院一再裁定只有伊斯兰教法法院有权允许某人离开伊斯兰教——这创造了有效的司法抓捕-22,因为伊斯兰教法法院很少允许放弃该宗教.

对国际人权倡导者和宗教自由支持者来说,Shameer一案明确提醒人们注意东南亚数百万人所面临的国家强制宗教控制。

articles.title_zh: 少女被囚禁六个月后死亡
articles.content: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in April. One had escaped, but five died at the camp, and the rest were released with Bulus — including the 4-year-old daughter of a woman who had died in captivity. Bulus’ village, Awon, is predominantly Christian and has been the target of Fulani attacks, just like Ariko, a neighboring village in Kaduna state. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. Ariko is home to the 37 Christians who were kidnapped during the Easter services earlier this year in a neighboring village. Of these, 17 people have died in captivity, 12 have escaped, and eight have since been released. The abductees from both these villages were held in the same forest hideout, where they were kept in inhumane conditions. “They [the villagers] told us how they would stay for two weeks without food,” one woman, whose father died in the camp, told Open Doors . “They only boil water to drink. That’s how they struggled before the bandits gave them corn flour, and they started making swallow (a porridge). The men are restrained, chained in groups; they are not free to move around.” All of the male abductees in these groups had died in the camp. Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW) is calling for Nigerian authorities to protect these communities and fight to free more people left in bondage. “We continue to urge the Nigerian government at state and federal levels to prioritize the protection of vulnerable communities throughout the nation, to combat the threat posed by the litany of terrorist groups that are active in the country far more effectively, and to secure the release of all abductees,” CSW CEO Scot Bower said. “Nigeria’s Christians do not need another statement of sympathy,” ICC’s president, Shawn Wright, said. “They need protection , justice , and accountability . When those who murder innocent Christians face no meaningful consequences, impunity becomes an invitation to the next attack. The Nigerian government must protect vulnerable communities, pursue the perpetrators, and make clear that these crimes will not go unanswered.” Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post Teenage Girl Dies After Six Months in Captivity first appeared on International Christian Concern .

articles.title: The Festive Attire We Really Need
articles.summary: Even in our finest clothes we can still be dirty on the inside. Advent reminds us that Jesus dresses us in his righteousness.
articles.summary_zh: 即使穿着我们最好的衣服 内心还是可以脏的 基督提醒我们,耶稣穿戴我们的正义。
articles.title_zh: 我们真正需要的节奏
articles.content: Read He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years. (Mal. 3:3–4) Reflect My grandmother always made going to church a special event. She helped me pick the right dress, made sure my shoes were shiny and clean, and withstood burns from the curling iron to perfect my hairdo. I know church attire can vary. But I still get dressed up for corporate worship because, no matter how cliché it sounds, I want to wear my Sunday best for Jesus. Yet even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Hidden sins are, after all, hidden. We can sing hymns at max volume, forgetting the way we treated our coworkers last week. We can kneel in prayer, easily dismissing what we posted on the internet earlier that morning. We can take the bread and wine even if we lost it with our kids in the car. People at church only see what’s on the outside, but God looks on the heart (1 Sam. 16:7). And unless we come clean, we can’t come into his presence at all. Even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Purity in God’s presence is a major theme in Scripture. In Leviticus, we learn how Israel was to distinguish between the clean and unclean. These categories extended to foods and animals. Even people could be defiled by disease or by touching unclean things such as a dead body. The temple was off-limits for the unclean. Only ritual washings and animal sacrifices made reentry into God’s presence achievable. But even this wasn’t permanent—for the blood of bulls and goats couldn’t fully atone for sin (Heb. 10:4). Like Israel, we dare not present ourselves before God in our sinful condition. As the psalmist asks, “Who shall stand in [God’s] holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (Ps. 24:3–4). While soap and water might wash our filthy hands, what can purify our sin-stained hearts? In today’s verses, the prophet Malachi announced the coming of One who would refine his people as gold and silver. Later, the author of Hebrews clarified the refiner’s identity: If the blood of goats and bulls . . . sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God. (Heb. 9:13–14) During Advent, we remember that Jesus is the great Refiner. He came to shed his purifying blood to cover our sins and forgive us. Then, like a refiner who heats metal to remove impurities, the Lord sanctifies us so that on judgment day we’ll be an unblemished offering to God. On that day, because of Jesus, we’ll wear white robes of righteousness (Rev. 6:11). Grandma made sure I looked pretty for church, but I wasn’t truly clean. Jesus, the great Purifier of sinners, is the only One who can wash away every stain and remove every impurity. When he dresses us in white robes, we’ll enter God’s presence because we’ll be clean—not just on the outside but on the inside too. Respond Sometimes the Lord refines us through trials and difficult circumstances. How have you experienced his refining process this year? Write a prayer thanking God for Christ who cleanses, purifies, and refines us so we’ll one day be holy and acceptable in his presence.
articles.content_zh:
读取 他必坐作炼银的精炼者,他必洗涤利未之子,并如金银般精炼,他们必以善报主耶和华. 犹大和耶路撒冷的供奉,将像往年和往年一样,为耶和华所喜悦。 (3:3-4) 反映 我奶奶总是把去教堂做成一件特殊的事

她帮我选合适的裙子 确保我的鞋子光亮洁洁 从卷曲的铁里烧伤 我知道教堂的服装会有所不同 但我还是穿好衣服去参加公司礼拜 因为不管这听起来多么陈词滥调 我想穿我的星期天最好的耶稣。 即便穿着我们最好的衣服 我们内心仍然可以肮脏

隐藏的罪恶毕竟是隐藏的。 我们可以用最高音量唱颂歌 忘记上周我们对待同事的方式 我们可以跪在祷告中, 轻易地放弃我们当天早晨在互联网上发布的内容。 我们可以拿走面包和酒 即使我们失去了它与我们的孩子在车里。 人们在教堂只看到外面的东西,但上帝看着心脏(1Sam. 16:7).

除非我们坦白,否则我们根本无法进入他的存在。 即使穿着我们最好的衣服, 我们内部仍然可以脏。 上帝面前的纯洁是圣经中的一个主要主题。 在利维提库斯,我们了解到以色列如何区分干净和不干净。 这些类别扩大到食物和动物。

甚至人们也可能因疾病或触摸尸体等不干净的东西而受到玷污。 该寺对不洁者禁入. 只有仪式洗涤和动物牺牲才能使重返上帝的存在。 但即使是这也不是永久的 — — 因为公牛和山羊的血无法完全赎罪(Heb. 10:4)。

与以色列一样,我们不敢在罪恶的条件下站在上帝面前。 正如诗人所问的, " 谁会站在[上帝]的圣地? 手清净而心清净者”(第24:3-4页)。 虽然肥皂和水可能洗我们的脏手,但什么能净化我们的罪恶的心? 先知马拉奇在今天的诗文中宣布,

后来,希伯来人的作者澄清了提炼者的身份: 如果山羊和公牛的血... ...为净化肉体而神圣化, 基督的血会有多少, 他通过永恒的灵献给自己 没有污垢上帝, (Heb. 9:13-14)在"启示录"中,我们记得耶稣是伟大的炼油者.

他为了掩盖我们的罪孽 并原谅我们而来 然后,像精炼者一样,他用金属加热去除杂质,主使我们圣洁,这样,在审判日,我们将成为向上帝献礼的无瑕疵者。 因为耶稣的缘故, 外婆确保我看起来很适合教堂,

耶稣,罪人的伟大净化者,是唯一可以洗去每一个污点,去除每一个杂质的人. 当他穿白袍时, 我们将进入上帝的面前, 有时主会通过考验和困难的环境来完善我们 你今年是怎么经历他的提炼过程的?

感谢上帝净化、净化、精炼我们,

articles.title: Don’t Be Afraid of the Alien Question
articles.summary: ‘Faith in Space’ shows that many Americans throughout history have already taken the question of extraterrestrial life seriously, but they’ve done so from outside an orthodox Christian framework.
articles.summary_zh: ”“宇宙信仰”表明, 历史上许多美国人已经认真对待地球外生命问题,
articles.title_zh: 不要害怕外星人的问题
articles.content: Have you ever wondered whether other worlds exist, and, if they do, whether they’re filled with intelligent life? If so, you’ve tapped into a deeply human instinct. Americans have long looked up at the night sky and asked that question. For Christians, though, the answers can feel unnerving. We already believe in nonhuman intelligence. We call them angels and demons. But aliens would be something else—material, embodied, literally otherworldly . In 2016, NASA started a conversation among religious scholars at the Center of Theological Inquiry in Princeton about what the existence of extraterrestrial life would mean for religion. Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls professor of English at Indiana University, has been wrestling with that question for years. Faith in Space: American Religious Belief in Extraterrestrial Life is his considered answer. He thinks we need to look back at existing “extraterrestrial cosmologies” in American religions rather than merely pondering future possibilities (7). Faith in Space is ultimately a history of what happens when religious communities take extraterrestrial life seriously. Many minority religions have, and it has shaped their cosmology and even their soteriology. But for many evangelical Christians, Gutjahr’s history raises a more uncomfortable question: What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Alien Religion Early Americans didn’t need much help imagining inhabited worlds. According to Gutjahr, many Americans “believed there to be life elsewhere in the universe” (19). By the end of the 19th century, “every stratum of American society had been exposed” to this belief (43). For example, Emanuel Swedenborg taught that the universe is populated with humans bearing God’s image and claimed to have conversed with them. His American followers never numbered more than a few thousand, and yet his ideas traveled across the young nation; Helen Keller held them, as did John Chapman (a.k.a. Johnny Appleseed). What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Andrew Jackson Davis, the father of American Spiritualism, was similarly inspired, convinced that “if life is to be found on other planets, it is human life.” He arranged extraterrestrial humans in “a progression of degrees that move from less to more spiritual” (64). Then Joseph Smith took things further. Latter-day Saints (Mormons) took an “aggressive extraterrestrial cosmological stance,” linking all worlds under one governing structure (79). God created many inhabited worlds arranged in “a hierarchy where some worlds rule over others” (89). Among these many worlds, Earth holds the least desirable title of “the most wicked, and thus most in need of a savior” (86). God himself is an enfleshed exalted man dwelling on a planet near the star Kolob. I’d add that the Salt Lake Temple bears the Big Dipper, and early Latter-day Saint temple iconography is thick with suns, moons, and stars. Next came the founder of Seventh-day Adventism, Ellen G. White. Where William Miller’s followers read comets and meteor showers as signs of Christ’s return, White gave Seventh-day Adventists “a far more complex understanding of their relationship with the stars” (124). Ours “was the only wicked world” (125). White distinguished strongly between the righteous and unrighteous worlds, and put Earth on the wrong side of that distinction. By the 20th century, the heavens were packed and theories about the heavens were part of salvation. Then comes Helena Blavatsky (Theosophy), L. Ron Hubbard (Scientology), Wallace Fard Muhammad and Louis Farrakhan (Nation of Islam), Malachi Z. York (Nuwaubian Nation), Ashtar Command, and Heaven’s Gate. All these figures or groups saw extraterrestrial life as part of the human story, whether for our good or our ill, or both. While the subtitle promises to cover American religions broadly, Gutjahr sets aside Catholics, Jews, and native traditions. The only “Protestants” h
articles.content_zh:
你有没有想过其他世界是否存在,如果存在,他们是否充满了智慧生命? 如果是这样的话,你已经深入到了人类的本能之中。 美国人早就仰望着夜空,问了这个问题. 但对于基督徒来说 答案会让人不安 我们已经相信非人类智慧 我们称他们为天使和恶魔。

但外星人会是别的东西——物质的,体现的,其实是异世界的。 2016年,NASA在普林斯顿神学调查中心开始了宗教学者之间的对话,讨论外星生命的存在对宗教的意义. 保罗·古特贾赫(Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls),印第安纳大学英语教授,多年来一直在与这个问题搏斗.

信仰太空:美国宗教信仰外星生活是他深思熟虑的答案. 他认为,我们需要回顾美国宗教中现有的“地外宇宙论”,而不是仅仅考虑未来的可能性(7)。 对太空的信仰最终是宗教界严肃对待外星生活时所发生的历史.

许多少数宗教都有,它塑造了他们的宇宙学甚至其神学. 但对于许多福音派基督徒来说, 如果我们不认真对待外星生命的可能性, 早期美国人不需要多少帮助,

Gutjahr说,许多美国人“相信宇宙中别处有生命”(19)。 到19世纪末,“美国社会的每一个阶层都暴露在”这种信念之下(43)。 例如,伊曼纽尔·瑞典堡教导说,宇宙中充满着带有上帝形象的人类,并声称与他们进行了交谈。

他的美国追随者人数从未超过几千人,然而他的想法却横跨了年轻的国家;海伦·凯勒也抱着他们,约翰·查普曼(英语:Johnny Appleseed)也是如此. 如果我们不认真对待外星生命的可能性,

美国精神主义之父安德鲁·杰克逊·戴维斯(Andrew Jackson Davis)同样受到启发,他坚信“如果在其他星球上找到生命,那就是人的生命。” 他将外星人类安排在“从较少的学位发展到更精神的学位”(64)。 后来约瑟夫·史密斯把事情更进一步.

末日圣徒(摩门教徒)采取了一种“侵略性的地外宇宙学立场,将所有的世界在一个管理结构下联系起来(79)。 上帝创造了许多有人居住的世界,这些世界是以“一些世界统治其他世界的等级”安排的(89)。 在许多世界中,地球拥有最不可取的“最邪恶因而最需要救世主”的称号(86)。

articles.title: Young Adults Are Hungry. Here Are 3 Ways to Feed Them.
articles.summary: Gen Z’s hunger for food, people, and the Word gives the church a magnificent opportunity in this moment.
articles.summary_zh: Gen Z对食物的渴望, 人们,
articles.title_zh: 年轻的成年人是饿了。 这里有3种喂食方法。
articles.content: When we opened the century-old church doors on the corner of Whaley Street and Wayne Street, we figured we’d have about 50 folks step through them that night. It was a Bible class for Gen Z, after all. How many Gen Zers actually want to learn about the Bible? Apparently, more than 50. We had to scramble for more chairs. It quickly became obvious that this generation—my generation—is hungry for the Bible, and we’ll starve if we don’t get fed. How are you feeding the hungry young adults in your context? My church has learned key lessons about feeding college students and young adults. These aren’t novel, but I hope they can help your people as much as they’ve helped ours. 1. Food (Like, Actual Food) I was sitting across from a leader at a major university recently and asked him how we could influence the students on that campus. He looked at me and said the plainest thing: “Food wins.” To win the heart of a man, you go through the stomach. If you want to feed people the gospel, consider first feeding them a sandwich. This is why my brother (“Chef Chunk” as they call him) has been serving an incredible amount of pancake batter out of a four-foot plastic storage container, complete with chocolate chips, blueberries, and a few other cheap toppings. We start pancake-flipping before 7 p.m. and don’t stop until we start class at 8:03 p.m., to keep up with the demand. Apparently breakfast for dinner is a fan favorite. Eating meals with others is one of the greatest indicators of personal well-being—the more we eat with our families (whether spiritual or biological), the more likely we are to be satisfied with our lives and filled with love, joy, and peace. Yet we’re eating fewer meals together than ever. What if the church was one of the great combatants of this damaging trend? 2. Friends (Like, Actual Friends) Speaking of loneliness, our culture is increasingly lacking “third spaces” where lonely people can find and build community. Robert Putnam described and predicted this decades ago in Bowling Alone —but these days we don’t just bowl alone. We shop alone, eat alone, entertain alone. We even tend to date or do friendship “alone,” as in virtually rather than in person. What few third spaces remain—the gym, sports environments, coffee shops—aren’t ideal for making meaningful connections. In gyms, we have our headphones on; at sports games, the music is so loud you get hoarse when you speak; and coffee shops are great but usually filled with headphones-on, screened-off people (and $7 lattes). Fresh-out-of-college Jimmy has nowhere to meet potential-best-friend Johnny or potential-love-of-his-life Jessica. That leaves Jimmy feeling hopeless in one of the most foundational needs of life: relationships. Our culture is increasingly lacking ‘third spaces’ where lonely people can find and build community. Yet this is a hole best filled by the new humanity God created called the church. Amid a growing cultural hunger for embodied friendships, maybe one of the major ways our church can “seek the welfare” of our cities (Jer. 29:7) is to build environments where a wide variety of folks can congregate. Maybe that looks like creating spaces for line-dancing, pick-up basketball, or weekly pickleball nights. But I have a hunch that one of the most interesting third spaces we can create might not need to be about entertainment. 3. Knowledge (Like, Spiritual Knowledge) “Do you know what Christmas is about?” “Um—not sure. What do you mean?” “Like, do you know the story behind it?” “Hmm. I feel like it’s about a guy . . .” “YES! Do you know his name?” “Mmm. Nah man.” “Jesus. His name is Jesus.” This is a real conversation I had with an average high school student in the South, the heart of the so-called Bible Belt. I could tell you of dozens of other conversations just like it. Here’s the truth: The Bible is the most interesting story in the world, and no one knows it anymore. articles.content: Several times now, I have been out in creation with unbelievers, speaking to them of eternal matters, and, passing by a dying branch at the base of a tree, I have picked it up and said, “This is your life apart from Christ.” Speaking about their souls, Jesus’s illustration is irresistible. The conversation goes something like this: Jesus gives us this illustration. He looks you in the eye and says that he is the tree (to augment the illustration slightly), and you are the branch. Look up and see the branches above us, beautiful leaves waving, healthy in their vibrant greens, bearing evidence of life. And then there is this branch. Dry. Leafless. Withered. Why? Because it is detached from the source of its life. Cut off from the one it was made to have communion with. And so, it lies here, detached from its purpose and severed from the only thing that can make it flourish. Jesus claims to be man’s source. He claims to be the Tree to whom you belong. In relationship with him, you have life. Apart from him, he teaches, you spend life withering. I usually pause to let the claim have its proper space. I ask what they think of such an assertion. I give them an opportunity to respond. I have often expected indifference or offense, but I have consistently been met with quiet consideration or outright acknowledgment that such an illustration made sense to them. Or at least they would like to hear more. So I go on to wonder aloud with them. What is it like to be a branch fallen from the tree that is, as Jesus says, withering ? Don’t you know? Need we ask? The restlessness, the fatal dryness, the looming death. The reaching out to anything and everything for life — except for the tree standing beside and over us. Him we do not want. Him we can do without. We can make it our own way. The adverb is different, but the end is the same — restless withering, drunken withering, religious, secular, or thoughtless withering . Some overdose on pleasure. Others get high on their own morality. Still others distract themselves from death’s shadow creeping over them with fantasy football and rounds of golf. But for all that, withering. But Jesus himself asserts that he is the Tree. He is the one we were made for; in him alone can we find the life that haunts us in still and sober moments. Be grafted to him through repentance and faith, be attached to him by the Spirit of the living God, have his words live in you, direct you, amaze you, and dead things will come to life. And what will it be on that day, I am compelled to continue, for those dry and fruitless branches who refused life in him? They will be gathered and thrown into the fire and burned as useless things. But Jesus came that you might have otherwise. He told us his mission was to bring life — life abundantly . Imagine the branch grafted to the tree, suddenly infused with life and purpose and the vital sap of God’s own Spirit. We are as branches; the Father, Son, and Spirit are the source of everlasting life. With him, we flourish though all may seem to go poorly. Without him, only sapped wood remains. Would you like to know more about this Jesus? Now, I tell you this to highlight one of many places where the Bible addresses the interiority of man and its solution: God. I want you to see how dangerous the alternative answers found in modern therapeutic culture are to our souls and our churches. It is a scourge, especially to this inward age, not because a therapeutic culture takes distresses of the heart seriously, but because it too often sends branches reaching out for anything but the Tree. Ingrown Toenails The problem comes not from a focus on the inner man. Anyone who says the Bible has little to say about internal battles, demons, depressions, anxieties, doubts, and the despairs of human life should not air his ignorance. The Scriptures abound with stories of the faithful brought into all the perplexities and pains of life in a fallen world. The Psalms, as one profound example, give u

他是我们被造出来的人;只有他我们才能找到在静静和清醒的时刻困扰我们的生活。 通过忏悔和信仰而受他宠爱,被活神的灵附在他身上,让他的言语活在你身上,引导你,惊叹你,死去的东西将复活.

那天我不得不继续 对那些拒绝他生命的干枯和无果树枝 他们将被集合并投入火中,被烧成无用的东西. 但耶稣来了,你也许有 否则。 他告诉我们,他的使命是带来生命——充满生命。

想象一下树上的树枝, 突然注入生命和目的, 我们如枝条一样;父、子、精神是永恒生命的源泉。 和他在一起,我们蓬勃发展,尽管一切似乎都不好。 没有他,只有树枝残骸。 你想知道更多关于这个耶稣的事吗?

现在,我告诉你,这要强调 圣经涉及人类的内在性及其解决方案的许多地方之一:上帝。 我想让你们看看现代治疗文化中找到的替代答案对我们的灵魂和教会有多危险.

articles.title: Fulani Militants Kill 14 Christians in Plateau State, Nigeria
articles.summary: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure
articles.summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
articles.title_zh: 富拉尼武装分子在尼日利亚高原州杀害14名基督徒
articles.content: At least 14 Christians have been killed in fresh attacks across four local government areas of Plateau state, Nigeria, days after President Bola Ahmed Tinubu appealed for forgiveness over his failure to visit violence-affected communities during an earlier trip to the state and promised to rebuild destroyed communities and return internally displaced persons (IDPs) to their ancestral homes. The killings occurred between Sunday, Nov. 15, and Monday, Nov. 16, in Mangu, Riyom, Barkin Ladi and Bokkos local government areas, according to community sources and local security groups. Armed attackers reportedly targeted rural settlements and ambushed residents traveling between communities. The latest violence followed Tinubu’s visit to Jos on Saturday, Nov. 14, for an All Progressives Congress (APC) political rally at Zaria Road Stadium, where he acknowledged the suffering of communities affected by recurring attacks and displacement. Addressing residents and party supporters, Tinubu asked Plateau residents to forgive him for not visiting affected communities during his previous trip to the state in April. “When I last visited the other time, I was limited to the airport,” he said. “Forgive me if you didn’t see me in the hinterland, but I saw the devastation. I got the report from the governor. I saw horror in the faces of our people.” The president promised to rebuild communities destroyed by violence and facilitate the return of displaced residents. “We will rebuild your communities, and we will bring you back to your communities,” Tinbu added. “I have directed all the security agencies to take decisive action and sustain peace and stability on the Plateau.” He also commended the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs and Poverty Reduction, Dr. Bernard Doro, for identifying vulnerable populations and coordinating humanitarian assistance. Tinubu announced that 1,000 forest guards were undergoing training and that surveillance cameras promised to Plateau state had been procured to strengthen security monitoring and early warning operations. However, fresh attacks were reported within hours of the president’s departure from the state. In Mangu Local Government Area, armed attackers invaded Zwagal community in Jipal District at about 9 p.m. on Sunday, killing nine people. Other residents were reportedly missing following the attack. Silas Nanfwang, a resident who confirmed the incident to journalists, called on security agencies to intensify efforts to locate the attackers and bring those responsible to justice. In Barkin Ladi, 79-year-old Da Ishaku Pam Vwos was killed when armed men invaded Sho village at about 5:20 p.m. on Sunday, according to the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM). The association’s National Publicity Secretary, Rwang Tengwong, also reported the killing of 42-year-old Dauda John Davou during an attack on the Sambak community in Hoss District, Riyom LGA, at about 2 a.m. on Sunday. Another attack was reported in the Jol community around 12:10 a.m. on Sunday. According to BYM, local vigilantes responded to the attackers, preventing further casualties. The association said the incidents followed the shooting of Joshua Doro Dafwel in Jol on Wednesday. He is currently receiving medical attention. BYM also reported that Ina Arin was killed when armed men ambushed him and his friend, Abok Gyang, as they returned to Dorong village in Foron District. Gyang survived the attack. In Bokkos Local Government Area, two people, including a unit commander of the Plateau state-owned security outfit, Operation Rainbow, were killed in an ambush on Monday afternoon. The victims, identified as Gambo and his companion, were traveling on a motorcycle from Hurti village to Tadai in Manguna District when armed men attacked them at about 1:30 p.m. They had reportedly visited Hurti for a condolence visit and died at the scene. Gambo had recently completed a refresher training program for Operation Rainbow unit commanders in Jos and was known amon

在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统呼吁原谅他在早些时候访问受暴力影响的社区,并承诺重建被摧毁的社区并让境内流离失所者返回其祖传家园几天后,在尼日利亚高原州四个地方政府地区,至少有14名基督徒被杀死。

据社区人士和地方安全团体称,这些杀戮发生在11月15日星期日至16日星期一的Mangu、Riyom、Barkin Ladi和Bokkos地方政府地区。 据报告,武装袭击者以农村定居点为目标,并伏击社区之间的居民。 在Tinubu于11月星期六访问Jos后,

14,在Zaria Road体育场举行全体进步人士大会(APC)政治集会,他承认一再受攻击和流离失所影响的社区遭受苦难。 蒂努布针对居民和政党支持者,要求高原居民原谅他4月前去该州旅行期间没有访问受影响的社区.

他说,“上次访问时,我仅限于机场。” “对不起,如果你没有在内地看到我,但我看到了灾难。 我收到州长的报告了 我在我国人民的脸上看到了恐怖。” 总统承诺重建被暴力摧毁的社区并便利流离失所居民回返。

Tinbu补充说,“我们将重建你们的社区,并将你们带回你们的社区。” “我已指示所有安全机构采取果断行动,并维持高原的和平与稳定。” 他还赞扬人道主义事务和减贫部长贝尔纳·多罗博士确定弱势人口和协调人道主义援助。

蒂努布宣布有1000名森林警卫正在接受训练,并且已经采购了向高原州承诺的监视相机,以加强安全监测和预警行动. 然而,据报道,总统离开国家后的数小时内又有新的袭击.

在Mangu地方政府地区,武装袭击者于星期日下午9时左右入侵Jipal区的Zwagal社区,造成9人死亡。 据报告,其他居民在袭击后失踪。 向记者证实此事的居民Silas Nanfwang呼吁安全机构加紧努力找到袭击者,并将责任人绳之以法。

在Barkin Ladi,79岁的Da Ishaku Pam Vwos被武装分子于星期日下午5:20左右入侵Sho村而死,据Berom青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)称. 该协会的全国宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong还报道了42岁的Dauda John Davou星期天凌晨2时左右在Riyom LGA的Hoss区被Sambak社区袭击时被杀死的事件。

据报道,乔尔社区在星期日12:10左右又发生了一起袭击事件. 据BYM称,当地民团对袭击者作出反应,防止了进一步的伤亡. 该协会说,事件发生在周三Joshua Doro Dafwel被枪击后。 他目前正在接受治疗。

BYM还报告说,Ina Arin被武装分子伏击并被其朋友Abok Gyang杀死,当时他们返回了Foron区的多龙村。 克阳幸免于袭. 在博克科斯地方政府地区,包括高原国有保安装备"彩虹行动"的一名分队指挥官在内的两人于星期一下午被伏击而身亡.

受害者被确认为Gambo和他的同伴,他们乘坐摩托车从Hurti村前往Manguna区的Tadai,武装人员于下午1时30分左右袭击他们。 据报告,他们前往Hurti慰问,并在现场死亡。 甘博最近完成了 " 彩虹行动 " 部队指挥官在乔斯的进修培训方案,并被称作 " 阿蒙 "

articles.title: Hindu Nationalists Target Christians in West Bengal, India
articles.summary: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiy
articles.summary_zh: 据记录，5月至11月期间，印度西孟加拉邦发生了至少48至65起针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和针对基督徒社区的暴力行为。
articles.title_zh: 印度西孟加拉邦的印度教民族主义者将矛头对准基督徒
articles.content: At least 48 to 65 incidents of targeted harassment, church vandalism, and physical violence against Christian communities in West Bengal, India, have been recorded between May and November. The Bangiya Christiya Pariseba, a Christian organization working for the welfare of the state’s Christian community, compiled this data. The right-wing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) came to power in West Bengal following the April 2026 Legislative Assembly elections. Independent tracking by the research group India Hate Lab verified 60 hate crime incidents explicitly targeting Christian individuals, domestic fellowships, and institutional properties within West Bengal during the same period, confirming the widespread geographic footprint of the escalation of attacks on Christians. According to reports, the latest attack occurred on Nov. 9, when vandals desecrated a sacred shrine and Marian grotto of a church in an overnight attack in Khari Bamuner Chak, located within the Raidighi and Baruipur pastoral region of West Bengal’s South Parganas. A week earlier, a heavily organized contingent of about 40 men attacked a house prayer fellowship in Rayan village of the Bardhaman area. The assailants stormed the private residence during a morning service, violently assaulting the officiating pastor and worshippers. Surge of Attacks The surge in targeted violence, intimidation, and vandalism against Christian communities, churches, and home prayer fellowships in West Bengal is proving that Hindu nationalists have found West Bengal to be the new hunting ground with tacit support of the authorities. The state is currently experiencing a rapid breakdown in local law enforcement deterrence. This erosion directly threatens the constitutional guarantees enshrined in Article 25 of the Indian Constitution, which ensures freedom of conscience and the right to freely profess, practice, and propagate religion. The emergence of organized Hindutva networks operating with near-total impunity represents not merely localized social friction, but a systemic challenge to the rule of law and civil stability across the state. Faith Space Shrinking Across rural and semi-urban districts of West Bengal, Hindu nationalists increasingly employ physical blockades, structural desecration, and coordinated mob actions to shrink the space for religious minority assemblies. By weaponizing social intimidation and exploiting police inertia, these actors seek to criminalize ordinary acts of devotion, transforming private exercise of faith into contested public security triggers. Detailed documentation by human rights organizations and community defense networks attributes the vast majority of these incursions to organized Hindutva-affiliated groups. Investigations specifically point to operational coordination by local cadres associated with the Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) and the Bajrang Dal, the RSS’s militant arm. Assailants consistently deploy dual narratives of illegal “unlawful religious conversions” and fabricated “honey traps.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post Hindu Nationalists Target Christians in West Bengal, India first appeared on International Christian Concern .
articles.content_zh:
5月至11月期间,印度西孟加拉邦至少有48至65起针对基督教社区的有针对性骚扰、破坏教堂和人身暴力事件。 Bangiya Christiya Pariseba是一个致力于国家基督教团体福利的基督教组织,

右翼印度民族主义者Bharatiya Janata党(BJP)于2026年4月立法议会选举后在西孟加拉邦上台.

研究小组印度仇恨实验室的独立跟踪核实了同期60起仇恨犯罪事件,明确针对西孟加拉邦的基督教个人、家庭奖学金和机构财产,证实了对基督教徒袭击升级造成的广泛地域影响。 据报道,最近一次袭击发生在11月.

9日,在位于西孟加拉邦南帕尔干纳斯的Raigighi和Baruipur牧区Khari Bamuner Chak的一起夜间袭击中,被破坏者亵渎了一座圣地和一座教堂的Marian地道。 一周前,一支由约40名男子组成的组织严密的特遣队袭击了Bardhaman地区Rayan村的一个家庭祈祷研究金。

袭击者在上午礼拜时冲入了私人住宅,暴力袭击了牧师和礼拜者。

袭击的激增 西孟加拉邦针对基督教社区、教堂和家庭祈祷研究金的有针对性暴力、恐吓和破坏行为激增,证明印度教民族主义者在当局的默许下发现西孟加拉邦是新的狩猎地。 目前,该国地方执法威慑迅速崩溃。

这种削弱直接威胁到《印度宪法》第25条所载的宪法保障,该条确保良心自由和自由信奉、实践和传播宗教的权利。

有组织的印度人网络的出现几乎完全不受惩罚,这不仅是局部性的社会摩擦,而且是对全国法治和国内稳定的系统性挑战。

印度民族主义者在西孟加拉邦的农村和半城市地区越来越多地采取实际封锁、结构性亵渎、协调暴徒行动来缩小宗教少数群体集会的空间。

通过将社会恐吓武器化和利用警察惯性,这些行为者试图将普通的献身行为定为刑事犯罪,将个人信仰的行使转变为有争议的公共安全触发因素。 人权组织和社区防卫网络的详细文件将绝大多数入侵归因于有组织的印度教附属团体。

调查特别指向与印度印度人理事会(VHP)和RSS好战武装Bajrang Dal有关的当地干部的业务协调。 仆从们一贯使用非法的“非法宗教皈依”和捏造的“甜蜜陷阱”的双重说法。 更多新闻报导, 采访,请通过电子邮件。

支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 印度西孟加拉邦后印度民族主义者以基督徒为目标,

articles.title: What We Get Wrong About the Tears of Jesus
articles.summary: Was Jesus’s grief at Lazarus’s tomb over his friend’s death or the response of the mourners? Pastor John explains how Jesus’s perfect emotions captured his indignation over unbelief. Listen Now
articles.summary_zh: 耶稣在拉撒路的坟墓前悲伤是因为朋友的离世，还是因为哀悼者的反应？约翰牧师解释了耶稣完美的情感如何表达了他对不信的愤慨。立即聆听
articles.title_zh: 我们对耶稣的眼泪有什么误解
articles.content: Audio Transcript “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). It’s the shortest verse in the Bible. We read it together in the Navigators Bible Reading Plan yesterday. But it’s so brief we can pass it too quickly. Maybe we pass over it because we think we know what it means. Jesus’s friend Lazarus died. Jesus wept because his friend was gone. But what if we got that wrong? Or, what if we mistakenly thought his emotions were simple when they were complex? What if Jesus wept not simply in the loss of death but from a frustration with the living? Today on Ask Pastor John: what we get wrong about the tears of Jesus. Henry, a listener, writes in with a timely question on John 11:35. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question today. I’d like to ask you about John 11:35. Why do you think Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus? One way to read this account is that he’s simply sharing in Mary and Martha’s sorrows over his death. But I wonder if something deeper is going on here. Jesus already planned to raise Lazarus, and he even told his disciples he was going to do it in John 11:11–15. “So, my questions are these two: First, why does Jesus ask, ‘Where have you laid him?’ Was he simply asking to be taken to the tomb? When they answer, ‘Lord, come and see,’ it’s almost like they still don’t appreciate who he is as the Messiah. And that is my second question: This whole event leaves me wondering if this weeping is more like Jesus’s weeping over Jerusalem in Luke 19:41 — weeping because he is heartbroken over the city’s unbelief. Is it a stretch to connect these two moments? Is Jesus grieving the dead Lazarus? Or is he grieving the unbelief of the living?” I doubt that any of Jesus’s emotions were simple. I think they were always complex. We finite creatures have emotions that respond to one or two, maybe three, happy or painful aspects of a situation. So, we may feel sorrow and joy mingled because, say, a very old saint has just gone to be with the Lord, and we will miss him, and yet we’re so happy for him. But Jesus could see every angle, every imaginable aspect of a situation, some of which called for very different emotions. So, I doubt that he ever had a simple emotion. For example, in Mark 3:1–5, there’s this man with a withered hand in the synagogue, and the people are watching to see if Jesus would heal him so that they could accuse Jesus. Can you imagine? They don’t give a hoot about this man’s pain. All they want is to accuse Jesus if he heals him. And in verse 5, it says, “He looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart.” And that’s what I mean by complex emotions: anger and grief perfectly mingled in the sinless heart of Jesus. Another example would be that he looked on unbelieving Jerusalem and wept: “Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes” (Luke 19:42). But in Luke 10:21, it says Jesus “rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, ‘I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.’” He could weep and rejoice over the wise and bitter providence of God. So, we come to John 11 and the death of Lazarus. And I think Henry, who’s sending us this question, is right when he says Jesus’s tears in John 11 aren’t just about sharing our human grief — that maybe he is genuinely mourning their spiritual blindness. Yes, and I’m going to say not just mourning — he’s indignant. The story begins in John 11:1–6 with Mary and Martha sending words to Jesus that their brother Lazarus is very sick. Jesus waits two more days before going and intentionally lets Lazarus die. He says in John 11:14–15, “Lazarus has died, and for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe.” That’s an amazing statement: “I let him die for the sake of your faith.” “They needed to see the glory of Jesus more than they needed the
articles.content_zh:
" 耶稣哭泣 " (John 11:35)。 这是圣经中最短的一首诗。 我们昨天一起在《航海家圣经阅读计划》上读到的。 但时间太短了, 也许我们通过它,因为我们认为 我们知道它意味着什么。 耶稣的朋友拉扎鲁斯去世. 耶稣因为朋友不在而哭泣. 但如果我们搞错了呢?

或者,如果我们错误地认为 他的情绪是简单的 当它们是复杂的? 如果耶稣不仅在死亡中哭泣,而且在对活人的挫折中哭泣呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"(Pastor John):我们对于耶稣的眼泪有什么错误. 亨利是一位听众,他及时写下约翰11:35的问题. “约翰神父,谢谢你今天接受我的问题。

我想问你约翰11点35分的事。 你觉得耶稣为什么在拉扎鲁斯的坟墓上哭泣? 他只是分享玛丽和玛莎对死亡的悲伤。 但我想知道这里是否发生了更深层的事情。 耶稣已经计划要抚养拉撒路人,他甚至告诉门徒他要在约翰11:11–15中完成.

我问的是这两个问题:首先,耶稣为什么问:你们把他放哪儿了? 他只是要求被带去坟墓吗? 当他们回答“主啊,快来看”时,

这是我第二个问题: 这整起事件让我怀疑这起哭泣事件是否更像是耶稣在路加19:41为耶路撒冷所哭泣, 连接这两个瞬间是不是很长一段时间? 耶稣在哀悼死去的拉撒路吗? 还是他痛恨众生的不信呢?” 我怀疑耶稣的任何情绪都很简单。

我觉得他们总是很复杂 我们有限的生物的情绪 反应了一两个, 也许三个,快乐或痛苦的方面 一个情况。 因此,我们可能感到悲伤和欢乐,因为,比如说,一个非常老的圣人刚刚与上帝在一起,我们将怀念他,然而,我们为他感到如此的高兴。

但是,耶稣可以看到每个角度,一个局势的每一个可想象的方面,有些需要非常不同的情绪. 所以我怀疑他有没有过简单的情绪 例如,在Mark 3:1–5中,有一个人手在犹太会堂里枯萎了,人们正在观察耶稣能否治愈他,以便他们指控耶稣。 你能想象吗?

他们不关心这个人的痛苦。 他们只想指控耶稣 如果他治愈他。 在第5节中,他说:他愤怒地注视着他们,他们为自己的坚硬而悲伤。 这就是复杂的情感的含义:愤怒和悲伤完全混入了耶稣的无罪之心。

另一个例子是,他注视着不信的耶路撒冷并哭道:"但愿你,甚至你,在今天知道什么是和平的! 但是现在它们被隐藏在你的眼睛之外”(19:42)。

但在"路加福音"第10:21节中说:"耶稣在圣灵中欢喜,并且说:我感谢你,天地之主,你把这些东西隐藏在智者与明者之间,并把它启示给小孩子;是的,神父,这是你的仁慈的意志". 他可以为上帝的睿智和痛苦的上帝而哭泣和欢乐。 所以,我们来到约翰11号 和拉撒路的死亡。

我认为亨利(Henry)向我们提出这个问题, 他说耶稣在约翰十一世的眼泪并不只是分享人类的悲痛, 我不仅要表示哀悼, 故事从约翰11:1–6开始,由玛丽和玛莎向耶稣发送了他们的兄弟拉扎鲁斯病得很重的话.

耶稣再等两天,然后故意让拉撒路死去. 他在"约翰·11:14-15"一文中说:"拉撒路已经去世了,为了你,我很高兴我没有在场,以便你相信". 这是一个惊人的说法:“我让他为了你的信仰而死。 ” 他们需要看到耶稣的光荣 而不是他们需要的

articles.title: He survived the killing fields. Then he baptised the man who ran a death camp
articles.summary: 🇰🇭Cambodia· 1980s-1990s
articles.title_zh: 他从“杀戮之地”幸存下来。后来，他为一名曾经营死亡集中营的人施洗。
articles.content: Christopher LaPel grew up near the royal palace in Cambodia and wore a small ivory cross as a boy, though his father disapproved. Then the Khmer Rouge came. In 1975 he was driven into the labour camps, working sixteen-hour days in the fields. He lost both parents, a brother, and a sister to execution and starvation. He nearly died himself. When he was too sick to work for three days, soldiers came to execute him, and one of them looked at him and said he really looks sick, and walked away. He survived into a refugee camp in Thailand, empty and grieving. There a missionary told him that Jesus Christ had died on the cross for his sins. "This is the answer I've been waiting for," LaPel said, and he gave Jesus his life. The general who said, my sin is so deep LaPel became a pastor and went back to teach his own people. In 1995 a quiet man calling himself Hang Pin came to one of his leadership trainings. He gave his life to Christ, was baptised the next day, and began leading a house church. Only later did the world learn who he really was. Kang Kek Iew, known as Comrade Duch, had run S-21, the prison where around twelve thousand people were tortured and killed. He came to LaPel and said, "My sin is so deep." Duch surrendered to the authorities and was sentenced to life in prison, where he wore out the Bibles LaPel kept sending him. The man who survived the killing fields carried the grace of Jesus back to one of the men who built them. No sin is too deep for the blood of Jesus. Not the worst thing done to you. Not the worst thing you have done.
articles.content_zh:
克里斯托弗·拉佩尔(Christopher LaPel)在柬埔寨的皇家宫殿附近长大并作为一个男孩穿小象牙十字架,尽管他的父亲不赞成. 后来红色高棉来了. 1975年,他被驱入劳改营,在田地工作了16小时. 他的父母、兄弟和姐妹都死于处决和饥饿。 他差点死了

当他生病了三天不能工作时,士兵们来处决他,其中一人看着他,说他真的病了,走了. 他活了下来,进入了泰国的一个难民营,空虚而悲伤. 有一个传教士告诉他,耶稣基督因他的罪而死于十字架上. 拉佩尔说:"这就是我一直在等待的答案",他给了耶稣一命.

将军说,我的罪恶是如此之深拉佩尔成为牧师,回去教自己的人. 1995年,一个叫作"杭平"的安静人来到了自己的领导训练之一. 他把生命献给基督,第二天被洗礼,并开始领导一所房屋教堂. 直到后来,世界才知道他的真实身份.

姜克毅被称作"杜克同志",曾经营过S-21监狱,当时大约有一万二千人被拷打并杀害. 他来到拉佩尔说:"我的罪恶是如此之深". 杜克向当局自首并被判处终身监禁,在那里他穿了"圣经"LaPel继续送去.

在杀戮地中幸存下来的人将耶稣的恩典带回了建造他们的人之一. 没有罪过是太深 对于耶稣的血。 不是对你最坏的事 不是你做过的最坏的事

articles.title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
articles.summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s
articles.summary_zh: 🇨🇬刚果民主共和国·21世纪10年代
articles.title_zh: 巫医有一台太阳能收音机。它被调到了真相频道
articles.content: Mbutu was a witch doctor in a remote village in the Democratic Republic of Congo. For years he cast spells, claimed power over the natural world, and sold cures to sick villagers who had nowhere else to turn. People feared him. He made his living off that fear. Then he was given a small solar-powered radio. It was fixed to one station, a local Christian broadcast, and handed out to villagers who had no other way to hear anything. Tuned to the truth So Mbutu listened. Day after day the good news came through that little speaker. He learned of the One who really controls the universe, and more than that, he learned about the love of Jesus and His offer of forgiveness. The man who had traded in fear laid his witchcraft down and gave his life to Christ. He did not keep it to himself. Mbutu now walks from village to village, finding other witch doctors and telling them what he found. Some of them have become believers. Some have become pastors, planting churches where there were none. A cheap radio and the name of Jesus were enough to turn the most feared man in the village into its brightest light. No one is beyond the reach of that name. Not the person others are afraid of. Not you.
articles.content_zh:

articles.title: Who or What? A Continuum for Using AI Wisely
articles.summary: From AI as god to AI as assistant. Here is a continuum of nine roles that can help Christians tell legitimate uses of AI from illegitimate ones, and wise from unwise. See Also A Christian’s Guide to AI Technology is Fast, Sanctification Is Slow, and Claude Can’t Do It For You A La Carte (October 16)
articles.summary_zh: 从AI为神到AI为助手。这里有九个角色的连续体，可以帮助基督徒区分人工智能的合法使用和非法使用，以及明智和不明智的使用。另请参阅基督徒的人工智能指南：人工智能技术快，成圣慢，克劳德无法为你点菜（10 月 16 日）
articles.title_zh: 谁或什么？明智使用人工智能的连续体
articles.content: It is sometimes hard to believe that it has been only four years since AI became widely available. Few technologies have made so massive and rapid a leap into our daily lives, to the extent that AI now exists in the background of all of our lives and, for many of us, in the foreground as well. Few technologies have evolved as quickly, so that the latest ChatGPT model bears about as much resemblance to its debut as the latest MacBook does to a Commodore 64. If all this has happened in just four years, imagine what the next four—or the next fourteen—might hold. As AI’s capabilities have increased, so too have the ways we can use it in our homes, churches, and workplaces. It seems like every month or two we read of a feature that can make a difference to our lives by adding a new ability or taking on work that used to be done by a person. The latest trend is the rise of agents—AI tools like Meta’s Muse or xAI’s Grok Bot that can carry out tasks, routines, and duties on an ongoing basis. With all of the tools available to us and all of their capabilities, it can be difficult to know which uses are legitimate and which are not. We all know that just because AI can do a task doesn’t mean that it should . So how can we determine the legitimate roles AI can play in our lives? I think sketching out a continuum of some of AI’s potential roles can help us. At the beginning are roles that most of us would agree are illegitimate, and at the end roles that most of us would agree are legitimate. Between them are roles that may be illegitimate in some cases and perfectly fine in others. These demand that we approach them thoughtfully to determine whether integrating them into our lives would be an act of wisdom or folly. As you will see, illegitimate roles tend to be those that require a who whereas legitimate roles tend to be those that require a mere what . The Continuum AI as God . There are some people, most of them deeply engaged in the tech industry, who ascribe to AI god-like qualities and who relate to it accordingly. They may believe it is an evil god that is likely to destroy humanity or a benevolent god that is likely to redeem humanity, but in either case, they treat AI as something far more than software. These people go too far and commit idolatry as they attribute to tech what rightly belongs to God. AI as Friend . There are some people who relate to AI as a friend, and even a few troubled people who relate to it as a lover. While AI is capable of mimicking the kind of relationship one might enjoy with a fellow human being, it can only ever mimic it. To relate to AI as a friend is to anthropomorphize a mere technology and worse, to deprive oneself of actual friendship. Though AI can imitate friendship, it cannot be a friend in any legitimate sense of the word, for friendship depends upon personhood. Not only that, but friendship depends upon mutuality and both the blessings and risks that come with relationship. You cannot be friends with AI any more than you can be friends with a tree, a PlayStation, or any other non-being. AI as Counselor . Many people today relate to AI as a counselor—a confidant who will listen patiently and counsel them with a trusted voice. Yet because AI is a what , not a who , it cannot offer answers based on a true understanding of their circumstances, true wisdom that comes from learning and experience, or true compassion that comes from sharing their humanity. It cannot empathize with them, pray for them, or plead with the Holy Spirit for wisdom in helping them. AI is capable of advising in many ways, but not of counseling, for counseling is inherently personal. AI as Pastor . Increasingly, people bring to AI the matters of spiritual health, growth, and well-being that in the past would have been addressed to a pastor. Every Christian needs to be under the loving oversight of a pastor who will care for their soul, and such crucial matters must be entrusted not to AI, but to a pastor who is called and
articles.content_zh:
有时很难相信,自AI广泛提供至今才四年。 很少有技术使我们的日常生活如此巨大和迅速地跃入,以至于AI现在存在于我们所有生活的背景中,对我们许多人来说,也存在于前景中。

很少有技术发展得这么快,因此最新的ChatGPT模型与其首发版的相近程度与最新的MacBook对准将64的相近程度相同. 如果这一切在短短的四年内就发生了,想象下四年,或下十四年可能发生的情况。 随着AI能力的增强,我们在家里、教堂和工作场所使用它的方式也一样。

我们似乎每个月或两个月都读到一个特点,通过增加新的能力或从事过去由一个人完成的工作,可以改变我们的生活。 最近的趋势是,诸如Meta的Muse或xAI的Grok Bot等能够持续执行任务、例行公事和职责的代理-AI工具的兴起。

有了我们可以利用的所有工具及其所有能力,就很难知道哪些用途是合法的,哪些用途不是。 我们都知道, 我们如何确定AI在生活中可以扮演的合法角色? 我认为勾画出AI的一些潜在角色可以帮助我们。

开始时,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是非法的,最后,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是合法的。 两者之间是在某些情况下可能是非法的,而在另一些情况下则完全正确。 这些要求我们深思熟虑地对待他们,以确定将他们融入我们的生活是明智还是愚蠢。

你会看到,非法角色往往是那些需要谁的角色,而合法角色往往是那些只需要什么的角色。 连续AI作为上帝。 有一些人,其中大多数人深入从事技术产业,他们把AI的神性描述为"类似"的特质,并与之相应相通.

他们可能相信是邪恶的神有可能毁灭人性或者仁慈的神有可能赎回人性,但无论在哪种情况下,他们都把AI视为远远超出软件的东西. 这些人太过分了 以偶像为神 因为他们把属于上帝的东西归为技术 作为朋友的AI.

有些人以朋友身份与AI有关,甚至有少数人以恋人身份与之有关系. 虽然AI能够模仿人们可能享受的那种与人类同胞的关系,但它只能模仿它. 作为朋友与AI的关系就是人类化,将一种简单的技术变成更糟糕的技术,剥夺了自己的实际友谊。

虽然大赦国际可以模仿友谊,但它不能是任何合法意义上的朋友,因为友谊取决于人性。 不仅如此,友谊还取决于相互以及关系带来的幸福和风险。 你不可能成为AI的朋友 也不可能成为树上的朋友,PlayStation,或者其他的不幸福. 作为律师的AI.

今天,许多人都把大赦国际当作一个顾问——一个会耐心地倾听他们的意见并以一个值得信赖的声音给他们提供建议的告密者。 然而,由于大赦国际是一个什么人,而不是谁,它不能根据对他们情况的真正理解、来自学习和经验的真正智慧或来自分享其人性的真正同情来提供答案。

它不能同情他们,不能为他们祈祷,也不能恳求圣灵的智慧帮助他们。 大赦国际能够在许多方面提供咨询,但不能提供咨询,因为咨询本质上是针对个人的。 作为牧师的AI. 人们越来越多地将精神健康、成长和福祉等问题带到大赦国际,这些问题过去本来是交给牧师的。

每个基督徒都需要接受一位会关心自己灵魂的牧师的慈爱监督,这种关键事项必须不委托给大赦国际,而委托给一位被叫作"和"和"的牧师".

articles.title_zh: 也门记者访问以色列，观点发生戏剧性变化
articles.content: By Charles Gardner — Luai Ahmed speaking at UN (screenshot YouTube) A brave Yemeni journalist has stunned the United Nations with an account of how his view of Israel has dramatically changed following a visit there. And he was led to the conclusion that everything he has been taught to believe about the Jews is a lie. Luai Ahmed was invited to address the assembly by UN Watch, a non-governmental organisation monitoring the international body’s performance, as the UN Human Rights Council gathered to debate racism. He said: “I grew up in Yemen, where the word that we used for black people is ‘abeed’, which quite literally means ‘slaves’. Racism towards black people in my country is horrifying, but it’s not even the most toxic hatred that I was taught. “The first time I ever heard the word ‘Jew’ was in my local mosque when I was nine years old. At the end of Friday prayers, the Imam said: ‘May Allah kill the Jews and the Zionists’. And I responded alongside thousands of Muslims praying beside me: ‘Ameen’.” Luai then continued: “I was taught that Zionism meant killing Arabs, stealing our land, and destroying Islam. Then October 7th came. Hamas terrorists ‘freed Palestine’ by slaughtering 1,200 Israelis and kidnapping more than 200 people, including a one-year-old child. “Almost everyone in my Arab-Muslim circle celebrated. I didn’t. Instead, as a journalist, I decided to visit the so-called Zionist entity, and I was completely shocked to the core by the lack of apartheid and racism that I experienced. “One day, I got an eye infection. At the hospital, the nurses in reception were Jewish. The doctor treating me was Arab. Is there racism in Israel? Of course. There’s racism everywhere. “But Arabs in Israel aren’t called ‘slaves’. They are doctors, engineers, and party leaders. My experience helped me realise that Zionism really just means the Jewish people’s right to a tiny country. Everything I was taught was a lie.” Quite apart from tipping over the tables of woke left-wing ideology spreading its poisonous antisemitic tentacles across the globe, Luai’s testimony also knocks holes into the escalating pressure on the UK to make reparations for the slave trade, which saw plenty of collaborators in the host countries of those who suffered. And of course, the truth that dare not speak its name – that it was Christians like William Wilberforce who put an end to it! Luai is a great inspiration to fellow journalists like me who long for more of our colleagues to stand up and be counted. Thanks also to David Soakell of Christian Friends of Israel’s Watching Over Zion newsletter, November 5, 2026. The post Yemeni journalist visits Israel, dramatically changes views first appeared on God Reports .
articles.content_zh:
一位勇敢的也门记者在联合国(YouTube)讲话时, 而他由此得出了这样的结论:他所学的关于犹太人的一切信仰都是谎言.

Luai Ahmed被联合国观察组织邀请在大会上讲话,该组织是监测国际机构业绩的非政府组织,在联合国人权理事会聚集一堂讨论种族主义问题。 他说:“我成长于也门, 我们用来形容黑人的字眼是“有病”的,

对我国黑人的种族主义令人恐惧, “当我九岁时,我第一次听到`犹太人'这个词是在我的地方清真寺。 星期五祷告结束时,教母说:愿真主杀害犹太教徒和犹太复国主义者。

我与数千名穆斯林一同祈祷: 卢艾接着说:“我被告知犹太复国主义意味着杀害阿拉伯人、偷窃我们的土地并摧毁伊斯兰教。 后于十月七日来. 哈马斯恐怖分子屠杀了1 200名以色列人并绑架了200多人,包括一名一岁儿童,从而“解放了巴勒斯坦”。 “我的阿拉伯-穆斯林圈子里几乎每个人都庆祝。

我没有。 相反,作为一名记者,我决定访问所谓的犹太复国主义实体,我对缺乏种族隔离和种族主义感到完全震惊。 “有一天,我眼睛受到感染。 在医院接待的护士是犹太人. 治疗我的医生是阿拉伯人。 以色列是否存在种族主义? 当然 到处都有种族主义。

“但以色列的阿拉伯人并不被称为奴隶。 他们是医生、工程师和党领袖。 我的经验帮助我意识到犹太复国主义只是意味着犹太人民对一个小国的权利。

我所学的一切都是谎言。” 卢艾的证言不仅在醒目的左翼意识形态席上倾出,在全球散布出有毒的反酋长触角,还打入了英国为奴隶贸易提供赔偿的不断升级的压力的洞口,在那些受苦受难者所在的东道国中,有许多合作者。

当然,那个不敢说出自己名字的真理——是威廉·威尔伯福斯这样的基督徒终结了它! 吕艾对像我这样的记者同事来说是一个巨大的灵感,他们渴望有更多的同事站起起来被统计. 也感谢以色列基督教之友的David Soakell,

articles.title_zh: 我们的刑事司法制度在哪些方面存在缺陷（与Matt Martens合著）
articles.content: When you really want to dive into the details of big questions about public policy—how we can live better together—you run into two problems: The experts and other stakeholders don’t want to consider Christian arguments, and Christians don’t want to engage in the details. That combination of a Christian argument from a legal expert was rare when Matt Martens’s book Reforming Criminal Justice: A Christian Proposal came out in 2023 from Crossway. And it’s still rare today. Matt is a trial lawyer and partner at an international law firm in Washington, DC. He and his wife are members at Capitol Hill Baptist Church, and they have two sons and a daughter. I read this book when it came out, and it’s stuck with me. Just the other day, I was thinking about the book when talking to one of my pastors, who was preparing to preach from 1 Peter on justice and obeying authorities. I thought about how I’d want to see the criminal justice system reformed if there were a good shot I’d be either a victim or criminal defendant. Isn’t that the law summed up in loving our neighbors as ourselves? From the death penalty to AI to the decline of violent crime—Matt and I covered a great deal. articles.title: The Cumulative Effect of Thousands of Family Bible Times
articles.summary: When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost.
articles.summary_zh: 当您的孩子注意力不集中或行为扰乱时，不要过于沮丧。如果牛奶洒了，如果发生了争吵，一切都还没完。
articles.title_zh: 数千次家庭查经的累积效应
articles.content: The alarm goes off, and another busy day begins. Getting kids up and ready for school, meal prep, work, after-school activities. Before you know it, the day is racing to its close. And you’re exhausted again. As Christian parents, we want our lives to count for Christ. We sincerely want our children to live their lives for Christ too. We want them to be changed by the same amazing grace that has transformed us. But how does this happen? How can we find the time and energy to effectively disciple our kids? Where will we find the creativity and passion to teach them what matters most? If you’re discouraged by your limited time and ability to shepherd your children, consider the cumulative effects of thousands of family Bible readings over the course of many years. Think Small What if a brief Bible reading today, a couple more later this week, and a few more next week eventually became a pattern, a deeply rooted habit for your family? Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over a couple decades. Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over the span of a couple decades. Years ago, Trevin Wax wrote an article titled “ 1000 Sermons Will Change Your Life .” What he says to pastors about preaching also applies to parents who lead their kids in family Bible reading: Pastors, don’t underestimate the cumulative effect of your preaching. You are not dumping information into brains. You are forming the habits of your people, teaching them how to read and understand and apply the Bible for themselves. Similarly in family life, our discipleship has cumulative effects that may not come to fruition for years. As parents, we’re in this for the long haul. If your children live in your home from birth to age 18, that’s 6,570 days. If you read the Bible together on average every third day, that’s 2,190 Bible readings over the course of your sons’ and daughters’ childhood and teenage years. Keep that big picture in mind when you feel defeated after a couple days on the go, when those family discipleship moments have eluded you. Think of Timothy, who was acquainted with the sacred writings from childhood because of his mother’s and grandmother’s faithful witness (2 Tim. 1:5; 3:14–15). May we be influential parents like them, who little by little and day by day pass on our life of faith to the next generation. Be Consistent, Establish a Habit With the long view in mind, think small in terms of your goals for this week, month, or year. Aim for consistency, for establishing a habit that you can pray will take root in your kids’ lives. Joe Carter recently shared the results of a sociological study of how faith moves across generations. He summarized the findings: The behaviors that most strongly predict lasting faith are active and verbal: praying together as a family, saying grace, embedding faith in the rhythm of the week rather than reserving it for Sunday, and, above all, talking about it. Children raised in homes where faith was discussed at least several times a week were more than twice as likely to attend church, pray daily, and rate religion as very important in young adulthood. The simplest way to put this truth into practice in your home is by creating a rhythm of opening the Bible regularly, reading some verses, and discussing them. You may never have a sense that one particular devotional was transformative. But keep at it. When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost. Resist the temptation to quit. Come back to the reading the next day, or the day after that. Keep finding times to open the Bible with your family. Let the Word Do the Heavy Lifting Another deterrent that may get in the way of family discipleship is “the intimidation factor.” If you feel ill-equipped to teach the Bible to your kids, you may be inclined to leave that task to Sunday school teachers and youth pastors. But you don’t h
articles.content_zh:

articles.content: “Hey, honey, you’re not going to be able to sleep tonight if you don’t start shutting things down soon!” After 36 years of marriage, my husband knows me well. He’s absolutely right, but I still sometimes want to keep pushing until bedtime. The way of wisdom is to stop consciously, set the work aside, and engage in the repetitive, mundane wind-down of the day. The work will still be there tomorrow, and I can trust God for new mercies to finish when morning comes (Lamentations 3:22–23). Our habits of rest reveal what we trust. While our need for sleep, recreation, and downtime weighs on our very physical, very finite bodies, we often resist submitting to our limitations. Substituting entertainment for true rest, we become passive consumers of endlessly streaming content that devours our time. Paradoxically, we crave rest and engage in ceaseless striving after things we hope will satisfy the desires of our heart. This is an ongoing battle for me, and I know I’m not alone. Our society values activity and busyness. We spend our hours and days going and doing, always with one eye on the clock. We reward tireless resilience with job promotions and earnest admiration. In our fervor for achievement, we may forget that rest is necessary for quality work to continue — and that rest can teach our hearts to trust God. Rest Reveals the Heart Psalm 127:1–2 is a reminder for our caffeinated and sleep-deprived souls that progress depends not solely on the work of our own hands but on God’s gracious provision: Unless the L ORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain. Unless the L ORD watches over the city, the watchman stays awake in vain. It is in vain that you rise up early and go late to rest, eating the bread of anxious toil; for he gives to his beloved sleep. Note that the psalmist illustrates a right and a wrong way to work. He makes three important points for the restless. 1. The Lord builds the house. God builds the ministry, the family, and the career. We work in cooperation with the Lord, and he watches over us and our work. The point is not that we shouldn’t work heartily at whatever we do (Colossians 3:23). Rather, our security is found in God, not in our efforts. Knowing our frame, remembering that we are dust, God commands us to observe regular patterns of rest, not only for our physical health but also as an acknowledgment of our dependence upon him (Psalm 103:14). 2. The Lord watches over the city. Whether we’re closing our eyes or closing our laptop and office door at the end of the day, when we leave the results of our work in God’s hands, we demonstrate trust in him. “He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep,” the psalmist writes (Psalm 121:4). God is your keeper, too. Entrusting our work to the Lord prevents it from becoming an idol. In our glad contemplation of work well done, we remember that he is both giver and gift. Our work is evidence of his power and goodness. 3. The Lord gives sleep to his beloved. Anyone who has spent a night sleepless from worry knows our bodies are not designed to run on anxious adrenaline. Insomnia has many causes and may not indicate a spiritual problem, but God often uses physical symptoms to reveal our spiritual condition. A steady diet of “the bread of anxious toil” (Psalm 127:2) starves us of what we need most: the ability to rest in God. When we rest, we accept our God-given limits. We hand the controls over to him. We lay aside our disordered loves, and we choose to believe the Father’s delight in Christ is also for us, his treasured children: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased” (Matthew 3:17). Because it can feel entirely unnatural, we may need to approach rest as a learned behavior, a habit of holiness, a spiritual discipline that we “put on” in the same way Paul exhorted the Colossians to clothe themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience (Colossians 3:12). articles.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now
