articles.title: El papa León XIV ya está en Argentina y el campo tuvo protagonismo en su primer discurso
articles.summary: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país
articles.summary_zh: 在访问乌拉圭之后，教宗利奥十四世于本周日开启了为期四天的历史性阿根廷之行，这是全球天主教会领袖首次踏上我国的土地。
articles.title_zh: 教宗方济各已抵达阿根廷，他在首场讲话中重点谈及乡村问题。
articles.content: Tras pasar por Uruguay, el papa León XIV inició este domingo su histórica gira de cuatro días por Argentina, que constituye la primera llegada de un líder de la Iglesia Católica mundial a nuestro país desde Juan Pablo II en 1987. En ese marco, la primera actividad del Sumo Pontífice fue un discurso en el Palacio Libertad de la Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires (CABA), frente al presidente de la Nación, Javier Milei. Y aunque sus palabras lógicamente estuvieron apuntadas hacia toda la sociedad, hubo numerosos pasajes que encontraron especial sintonía con el mundo agropecuario. Esto, en la previa de la reunión que León XIV mantendrá el lunes con representantes empresariales, sindicales y de organizaciones sociales, entre los que estarán los presidentes de las cuatro entidades de la Mesa de Enlace. EL PAPA LEÓN XIV EN ARGENTINA Puntualmente, el jefe mayor del Vaticano destacó el valor del esfuerzo cotidiano de los argentinos, con una mención expresa a quienes trabajan en el campo, y reivindicó la importancia de generar oportunidades, estimular la iniciativa privada y aprovechar responsablemente los recursos naturales. “Esta tierra conoce bien el valor del esfuerzo de quienes se ganan la vida en el campo y en las ciudades”, expresó León XIV, al destacar también el papel de los emprendedores y de las familias que sostienen sus hogares a través del trabajo. Asimismo, el Papa reconoció el enorme potencial productivo del país, al señalar que la Argentina cuenta con una extraordinaria riqueza natural, desde sus campos y reservas de agua hasta sus fuentes de energía, minerales y biodiversidad. Así, su mensaje combinó la posibilidad de aprovechar esos recursos para generar desarrollo y bienestar con la responsabilidad de preservar el ambiente y las condiciones de vida de las futuras generaciones. También dedicó un espacio a la innovación, la investigación y las nuevas tecnologías, incluida la inteligencia artificial, destacando su capacidad para transformar la producción y mejorar la vida de las personas. Por otro lado, al expresar una mirada sobre América del Sur, mencionó además a los alimentos, la energía y el conocimiento como elementos que vinculan a los países y abren oportunidades para fortalecer la cooperación regional. LEON XIV, EL MARTÍN FIERO Y EL MATE Asimismo, León XIV ofreció referencias cargadas de simbolismo para la identidad argentina. Por ejemplo, mencionó al Martín Fierro de José Hernández, a Jorge Luis Borges, al tango y a las tradiciones del interior del país. Y no faltó una de las costumbres más arraigadas entre los argentinos: el mate compartido, al que presentó como un gesto cotidiano que favorece la conversación y la cercanía. Por último, hacia el final de su intervención, León XIV evocó a Nuestra Señora de Luján, patrona de la Argentina y figura de especial significado para las comunidades rurales y para generaciones de familias de todo el país. También recordó al papa Francisco, citó a Carlos Gardel y alentó a los argentinos a valorar el patrimonio recibido de las generaciones anteriores y trabajar para dejar un país mejor a quienes vendrán. De esta manera, sin ser un discurso específicamente dirigido al agro, las palabras de León XIV dejaron un reconocimiento al trabajo rural, a la producción, a la iniciativa emprendedora y a las tradiciones que forman parte de la identidad argentina. articles.content: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólica en Paraguay comunicó el sábado 7 de noviembre que el santo padre aceptó la renuncia de Robledo y designó en su reemplazo a monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville, quien se desempeñaba como obispo de San Pedro y es el actual presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya (CEP). La decisión fue anunciada por la CEP, conforme a lo establecido en el Código de Derecho Canónico, que contempla la renuncia de los obispos al alcanzar los 75 años de edad. No obstante, monseñor Robledo continuará al frente de la diócesis como administrador apostólico hasta la toma de posesión canónica de su sucesor. La Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya agradeció a monseñor Robledo por su servicio pastoral y dedicación a la Iglesia, al tiempo que encomendó en oración al nuevo obispo, deseándole un fecundo ministerio episcopal en su nueva misión. El nuevo obispo Monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville nació el 5 de agosto de 1960 en Ottawa, Canadá. Tras algunas experiencias laborales, ingresó en la Congregación del Espíritu Santo y estudió Teología en la Universidad de Montreal. Emitió los votos solemnes en 1988 y fue ordenado presbítero el 17 de setiembre de 1988. Tras algunas experiencias misioneras en África, realizó estudios académicos en Montreal y París. Llegó a Paraguay en 1991, desarrolló diversas tareas pastorales y formativas; entre ellas, se desempeñó en la pastoral indígena de la parroquia San José Obrero, en la Diócesis de San Pedro; fue párroco de San Francisco de Asís y formador de la Congregación del Espíritu Santo en Asunción. En 2013 fue nombrado obispo de San Pedro y recibió la ordenación episcopal el 21 de diciembre de ese mismo año. Además, ejerció la vicepresidencia de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya entre 2018 y 2024 y, desde noviembre de 2024, ocupa la presidencia de dicha institución. La Diócesis de San Lorenzo comprende varias localidades del departamento Central, entre ellas Capiatá, San Lorenzo, Ñemby, Itá, Ypané, Guarambaré, Villeta, Nueva Italia, San Antonio, J. Augusto Saldívar, Ypacaraí y Thompson.

articles.title: Why Did Prosecutors Agree To Omit References to Katy Perry From the Opening Statements at Trial ?
articles.summary: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November
articles.summary_zh: 在拉塞尔·布兰德的伦敦强奸案庭审中，经其律师提出异议，检方同意从开庭陈述中删除提及凯蒂·佩里的内容。该决定于11月5日星期四公布。
articles.title_zh: 为什么检察官同意在庭审开场陈述中省略对凯蒂·佩里的提及？
articles.content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

articles.content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. articles.content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.

articles.title_zh: 世界各地的地标建筑将在2026年红色周期间亮灯
articles.content: About 130 cathedrals, thousands of churches, and over 125,000 people around the world are expected to take part in Red Week this month, with the European Parliament in Strasbourg, France, honoring the occasion by lighting up in red on Nov. 23. Red Week 2026 will take place from Nov. 15–22, with Red Wednesday falling on Nov. 18 in most regions, although it will be observed on Nov. 25 in the Philippines. The observance began in 2016 by Aid to the Church in Need (ACN), an international Catholic aid organization and Pontifical Foundation of the Church that supports Christians who are persecuted, oppressed, or in material need. The week includes illuminating monuments in red, prayer vigils, testimonies, and seminars on Christian persecution around the world. Designed to raise awareness of the ongoing Christian persecution in countries particularly in Africa and Asia, Red Week brings together those who are persecuted and those who are working to end violence and hatred against people of faith. At various events, testimonials from survivors of religious persecution will provide powerful moments of reflection about the suffering and human rights violations happening around us that go unnoticed. According to the latest figures provided by ACN, 413 million Christians live in countries where serious violations of religious freedom occur, and around 220 million Christians worldwide are directly exposed to persecution. "Faced with this reality, the pontifical foundation is once again promoting the Red Week this November, an international mobilization of prayer, witness, and awareness-raising to draw attention to the deterioration of religious freedom and remember the millions of Christians who suffer discrimination and persecution because of their faith," said Regina Lynch, executive president of ACN International. Red is more than a color According to ACN's "Religious Freedom in the World Report 2025," more than 5.4 billion people — almost two-thirds of humanity — live in countries where religious freedom is not fully guaranteed. The color red is used to symbolize the blood of martyrs and all those who suffer for their faith. In 33 countries Christians have been forced to leave their homes because of their faith while in 57 countries Christians suffer physical violence or even detention because of their faith. Each church and monument taking part in Red Week serves as a reminder of Christians who cannot freely practice their religion. In line with article 18 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, every individual has the freedom of thought, religion, and conscience with the right to practice their beliefs, free from persecution and violence. Through this weeklong initiative, ACN aims to promote one shared goal of making visible the shared suffering of the Christian people and defend everyone's fundamental rights to religious freedom.

articles.content: É a maior comunidade religiosa, mas também a mais perseguida do mundo. Os cristãos são notícia quase diariamente por serem alvo de ataques ou assassínios; ou por as suas instalações e símbolos terem sido danificados. Só em setembro, o Observatory on Intolerance and Discrimination against Christians dá conta de 30 casos na Europa, entre atos de vandalismo a igrejas, cemitérios, ataques a sacerdotes - um foi assassinado - ou mesmo a discriminação profissional por se ser cristão. Se a Nigéria é considerada o país mais perigoso para os católicos, o México é o inferno para padres, pois é aí que mais são assassinados. O Nascer do SOL entrevista Félix Lungu, um romeno a viver em Portugal há 31 anos, porta-voz, em Portugal, da fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre (AIS). Esta organização faz relatórios sobre a liberdade religiosa no mundo, e tenta explicar onde as religiões são mais perseguidas e quais os desafios que enfrentam, com especial ênfase na Igreja Católica. Félix Langu, à semelhança dos seus chefes - a organização tem sede na Alemanha -, procura não alimentar divisões, mas é impossível fugir a factos: no Paquistão, só muito recentemente é que os empresários do lixo deixaram de recrutar obrigatoriamente cristãos; não faltam países fundamentalistas onde meninas de 10 anos são violadas e obrigadas a casar, ‘adquirindo’ automaticamente a religião islâmica; e são ainda muitas as nações onde os católicos não podem desempenhar cargos na função pública. O Vaticano calcula que, anualmente, são mortos cerca de cinco mil cristãos, mas a liberdade religiosa afeta também os muçulmanos moderados, que são alvo da ira dos fundamentalistas, acabando muitos deles assassinados. Qual o papel da Fundação Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre? A Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre, fundação Pontifícia, é uma organização que tem quase 80 anos e foi criada na Alemanha. Nasceu no final da Segunda Guerra Mundial para ajudar os refugiados alemães que se deslocavam pela Europa. Depois, pouco a pouco, ajudou cristãos dos países do Leste, por causa do comunismo, do ateísmo, de toda essa situação. Ou seja, não somos como a Cáritas, ou outras ONGs, no sentido de dar ajuda social, ou educação, ou saúde. Também chegamos a estas áreas, o foco, contudo, é a ajuda pastoral, ajudar a Igreja, ajudar sacerdotes, construir igrejas, formação de seminaristas, ajudar nas missões os missionários, com carros, com rádios, televisões, bíblias, o que é necessário para fazer a evangelização. Basicamente é isso e estamos em 24 países. A sede é na Alemanha, onde se faz a gestão de tudo isso. E nos outros 24 secretariados fazemos a angariação de fundos. Para fazer a angariação de fundos é preciso saber por que se pede dinheiro, por que se pede esta ajuda. Temos três pilares, digamos assim, da nossa missão: informar, rezar e ajudar. Informar é tentar dizer qual é a situação no mundo, sobretudo onde há carências, que tipo de carências, sempre com foco nesta dimensão pastoral ou de evangelização. Nos últimos anos, a Ajuda à Igreja que Sofre dedica-se ao estudo ou análise da situação da liberdade religiosa no mundo. Porque se nós somos uma organização da Igreja, e se temos parceiros em todo o mundo, em 186 países, é importante saber onde há carências, que tipo de carências são. E temos percebido que, por exemplo, no Médio Oriente, junto com as carências materiais, falta de escola, de saúde, da alimentação, há também esta dimensão da perseguição. Falta algo que valorizamos muito, que é a questão da liberdade religiosa, dos direitos, que estão valorizados no ocidente. O que fazem nesses países onde os cristão são perseguidos? Na Arábia Saudita, por exemplo, não há hipótese de haver uma igreja? Não, na Arábia Saudita não temos uma presença. A única presença nesses países é através da representação consular. É na capela de uma embaixada, por exemplo, de França ou de Itália, que se pode celebrar a missa, porque não há possibilidade de ter uma igreja na Arábia Saudita. Considerado o país do profeta, terra sagrada

articles.summary: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă

articles.title_zh: Calendar creștin ortodox joi, 22 octombrie 2026. Rugăciunea către Sfinźii șapte tineri din Efes, rstită pentru liniște sufletească și somn odihnitor
articles.content: Calendarul creștin ortodox pentru joi, 22 octombrie 2026, îi pomenește pe Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cunoscuți și sub numele de „cei șapte adormiți”. Aceștia sunt sărbătoriți de Biserica Ortodoxă de două ori pe an, pe 22 octombrie și pe 4 august. Povestea lor este legată de o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde, potrivit tradiției creștine, au dormit vreme de mai multe sute de ani. Credincioșii se pot ruga către aceștia pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă. Cine sunt Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes sunt Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan și Constantin. Potrivit tradiției creștine, aceștia au trăit în vremea împăratului Deciu, când creștinii erau persecutați pentru credința lor. Pentru a se adăposti de prigoană, cei șapte tineri s-au retras într-o peșteră din Muntele Ohlonului, unde au adormit pentru mai multe sute de ani. Tot joi, 22 octombrie, Biserica Ortodoxă îl pomenește și pe Sfântul Averchie, episcopul cetății Ierapole din Frigia. În aceeași zi mai sunt pomeniți Sfântul Kukșa din Odesa, Sfântul Mucenic Alexandru episcopul, Mucenicul Iraclie, Anna, Elisaveta, Teodota și Glicheria, Sfântul Mucenic Zaharia, Sfântul Ruf și Cuviosul Lot. Rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, pentru liniște sufletească și odihnă Credincioșii care se confruntă cu griji și lipsa somnului pot rosti rugăciunea către Sfinții șapte tineri din Efes, cerând ajutor pentru dobândirea păcii sufletești. „Sfinților 7 tineri din Efes, care bine v-ați nevoit și cununa Împăratului Hristos ați dobândit, ne rugăm vouă, ca unii care multă îndrăzneală înaintea Domnului ați câștigat. Sfinților Maximilian, Exacustodian, Iamvlih, Martinian, Dionisie, Ioan şi Constantin, izbăviți-ne de lipsa somnului și puținătatea sufletului. Citește și: Carmen Harra, mesaj pentru populație! Ce s-ar putea întâmpla în 2027: “Nimeni nu spune adevărul!” Citește si: Andreea Pirui a fost prinsă de oamenii legii! Unde a fost găsită Voi, care în vremea împăratului Deciu, prigonitorul, ați fost pregătiți să luați cununa muceniciei, mărturisind dreapta credință și împotrivindu-vă tiranului celui fără de omenie, însă, din rânduială dumnezeiască, peștera în care v-ați adăpostit nu v-a fost vouă mormânt, ci s-a făcut vouă sân al lui Avraam, în care ați dormit somn adânc mai multe sute de ani şi, ca nişte prunci ce se încălzesc la sânul maicii lor, nu ați suferit nicio stricăciune. Iar în vremea binecredinciosului împărat Teodosie, din încredințarea Mântuitorului și pentru adeverirea Învierii celei de obște, v-ați trezit și v-ați arătat oamenilor, dând mărturie despre puterea lui Dumnezeu, apoi ați adormit cu adevărat întru odihna cea veșnică. O, preaslăvită minune, încât pretutindeni oamenii o au cunoscut. Deci, și acum, când gânduri negre vin asupra noastră, văzând cum slăbim cu duhul și cum ne descurajăm din lipsa somnului, acestea ne rod și ne macină sufletește, ca un vierme neadormit. Grijile cele apăsătoare, ca niște ulii la pradă, ne covârșesc și nu mai știm ce sunt pacea și odihna încrederii în Dumnezeu. Știm că toate acestea pentru păcatele noastre sunt. Știm că, pentru puțina noastră iubire de Dumnezeu și de aproapele, în astfel de mâhniri se afundă sufletul nostru. Cu pocăință ne rugăm și cerem ajutorul vostru, Sfinților din Efes, somn binecuvântat și mângâietor, spre pacea sufletului și odihna cea trupească, dăruiți-ne. Izbăviți-ne din gândurile cele rele, iar cu cele bune ne insuflați. Scoateți-ne din grijile cele multe care ne macină și de singură grija mântuirii învățați-ne să ne ținem. Așadar, Sfinților ai lui Dumnezeu, prin ajutorul vostru, luminare și împăcare întru Hristos să găsim și cerul să îl dobândim. Amin.”

articles.title_zh: 十字架：所有基督徒被称为的苦难
articles.content: By Bradlee Dean October 21, 2026 “For unto you it is given on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in Him, but also to suffer for His sake…”-Philippians 1:29 When it comes to suffering, there is not a genuine Christian who is not appointed to it. Why? For His sake. “For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus’ sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ. But we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellency of the power may be of God, and not of us. We are troubled on every side, yet not distressed; we are perplexed, but not in despair; Persecuted, but not forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed; Always bearing about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our body. For we which live are always delivered unto death for Jesus’ sake, that the life also of Jesus might be made manifest in our mortal flesh. So then death worketh in us, but life in you. We having the same spirit of faith, according as it is written, I believed, and therefore have I spoken; we also believe, and therefore speak; Knowing that he which raised up the Lord Jesus shall raise up us also by Jesus, and shall present us with you. For all things are for your sakes, that the abundant grace might through the thanksgiving of many redound to the glory of God.” –2 Corinthians 4:5-15 I also realize that no one spoke of, or endured, suffering more than Christ, though ours are light in comparison (Isaiah 53), who told us before His ascension that as the Father sent Him, so He would send us (John 20:21). I have personally suffered, including fellowship with His sufferings, afflictions, trials, and testings, so that I might learn and grow from the lessons the Lord gives in the process (Psalm 119:71). Oftentimes we think we are in control of our own world; we may even deceive ourselves into believing we are trusting the Lord and are being led by His Spirit (Romans 8:14) when we are not, only to find that in the end we were all the while limiting Him through our means of control. For example, we can pray, Lord, increase our faith, or, Lord, oh, that I would grow in grace more so I might be just like you, and then, when He brings us through the process to learn the lessons, we lose control, and there it is: we find out who it is that we really are, and who it is that we really trust (John 3:6). We have heard some say that the Lord will never give us more than we can handle, and I have to say, this is not true whatsoever, because in many cases He brings us to the place of more than we can handle to show us what we cannot handle, to show us what it is that He can handle, and this with ease. This is done so that we trust not in ourselves (2 Corinthians 1: 5-10). In other words, our extremity is the Lord’s opportunity. You see, the root of fear is control, and throughout our lives we are taught to control every aspect of our lives so that we do not have to trust in the Lord (avoid suffering) that we may grow, though we claim that we are doing so. Then, when we lose that control, we have to trust the Lord in ways that we never have before, this where we suffer through our unbelief (though we hold to His Word) until we transition (by the Holy Ghost – Titus 3:5) into what it is that He means for us to be, and to see outside of our own limited controls in order to bring us into a larger place (Psalm 4:1). Isaiah 55:8-9 says, “For my thoughts are not your thoughts, neither are your ways my ways, saith the LORD. For as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways, and my thoughts than your thoughts.” In conclusion: Through suffering, the Lord introduces us to His workings, so that we might see His faithfulness, to see His wonderful works which are His righteous operations in and through Christ, as we are confo
articles.content_zh:
2026年10月21日 布莱德利·迪恩 “为了你们,不仅为了信仰基督,而且为了他而受苦受难。” 关于受苦,没有一个真正的基督徒没有被任命。 为什么? 为他故. " 我们不是为自己而传教,而是为主而传教;我们是你们的仆人;

因为上帝命令光从黑暗中闪出,已经照亮了我们的心,在耶稣基督面前赋予了上帝的荣耀知识之光. 但我们有这个宝藏在地上, 权力的卓越可能来自上帝,而不是我们。 我们每边都忧心忡忡,却不忧愁;我们感到困惑,但不是绝望;我们受到迫害,但不是被遗弃;

我们有着同样的信仰精神,按照它所写的,我相信,因此我说过话;我们也相信,因而也说出话来;我们知道,复活主耶稣的人,也要由耶稣来养育我们,并将我们与你一同呈现.

万事都是为你着想的,丰厚的恩典,可以通过许多为上帝所荣耀而赞颂的恩惠来达到。” ——2 科林斯人4:5-15 我也意识到,没有人会说出或忍受比基督更痛苦的事,尽管我们的比喻是轻的(以赛亚53),在他升天之前,他告诉我们,正如父亲派遣他那样,他将派遣我们(约翰20:21)。

我个人遭受了痛苦,包括同他的痛苦、苦难、考验和试验的友谊,以便我能够从上帝在这一过程中提供的经验教训(第119:71段)中吸取并成长。 我们常常认为我们控制着自己的世界;

我们甚至可以欺骗自己,使我们相信我们信任主,并且正被他的精神所引导,而我们不是那样的,我们只是发现,我们最终通过我们的控制而限制他。

例如,我们可以祈祷,主,增加我们的信仰,或者,主, 哦,我将会在恩典中成长得更多,这样我或许就和你一样,然后,当他带我们走进吸取教训的过程时,我们失去控制,这就是:我们发现我们真正是谁,我们真正信任谁(John 3:6)。

我们听到有人说,上帝永远不会给我们 超过我们所能处理, 我必须说,这不是真的,因为在许多情况下, 他带我们到我们无法处理的地方 向我们展示我们无法处理的事 向我们展示他能处理的事 以及轻松处理的事 这样做是为了让我们不信任自己(2个哥林多1:5-10).

换句话说,我们的极限是上帝的机会。 你看,恐惧的根源是控制,在我们一生中,我们被教导要控制我们生活的方方面面,这样我们不必相信主(避免痛苦),以便我们成长,尽管我们声称我们这样做了.

然后,当我们失去这种控制时,我们必须以我们以前从未有过的方式信任上帝,这是我们通过不信而受苦的地方(尽管我们坚持他的话),直到我们(由圣灵-提图斯3:5)过渡到他对我们意味着什么,并且看到我们自己有限的控制之外,以便把我们带入更大的地方(Psalm 4:1).

以赛亚55:8-9说:"耶和华说,我的想法不是你们的,你们的道路也不是我的。

因为天比地高,我的道路也比地高;我的思想也比地高。” 最后:主通过苦难向我们介绍他的工作,以便我们看见他的忠诚,看到他的出色的作品,这是他在基督中和通过基督的正义行动,就像我们聚集在一起一样。

articles.title: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma : cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
articles.summary: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia.
articles.summary_zh: “我有一个梦想” ， decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia。
articles.title_zh: De la pesadilla de Gaza al sueño de Fatma: cómo podemos seguir creyendo en la humanidad en medio del horror
articles.content: “I have a dream”, decía Martin Luther King en 1963, cuando agitaba las conciencias desde las escalinatas del monumento a Lincoln en Washington, en uno de los discursos más emblemáticos de la historia. Hoy, sin embargo, sólo siento ganas de decir: I have a nightmare. O mejor dicho: We have a nightmare, porque la pesadilla no sólo afecta a los palestinos, sino a todos nosotros, a cualquiera que cree que la “justicia” no es una palabra vacía. La vida de los palestinos es una pesadilla interminable. En Gaza oyes el ruido de los aviones, sientes el miedo de los bombardeos, el acecho de los drones –cada vez más traicioneros y sofisticados– que te siguen, te espían, te ensordecen y disparan. La vida cotidiana consiste en sobrevivir en tiendas de campaña desgarradas por el viento y llenas de barro. Compartir un baño con tanta gente que usarlo se vuelve imposible. Volver a una casa medio destruida por las bombas con el riesgo de que el techo se derrumbe y mate a tu familia. Afrontar el rigor del invierno –ya es el tercero desde que comenzó el genocidio–, sin ni siquiera unos libros que poder quemar para mantener a tus seres queridos, al menos a los niños y ancianos, en un lugar cálido y seguro. Sólo tiendas, frías en invierno, sofocantes en los tórridos veranos. Cuántos muertos, desplazados, huérfanos, heridos, mutilados… Y los que aún no han sucumbido al asedio total que impera desde hace más de dos años están condenados a sufrir hambre y sed, a no tener derecho a una asistencia sanitaria y a una supervivencia digna. En Cisjordania y en Jerusalén Este, los palestinos viven con el terror de despertarse en plena noche con un soldado que los apunta con un fusil a la cara, que destruye sus casas, que los amenaza, los humilla delante de sus hijos o se los lleva consigo, con sus pijamas manchados de pipí porque se han orinado encima de miedo. Mientras tanto, los colonos están cada vez más furiosos: los ataques a los pueblos, comunidades rurales, tierras, coches, ganado, están a la orden del día. Incluso en las cárceles hay casos documentados en los que se ha autorizado a periodistas y civiles israelíes a presenciar –e incluso a grabar con sus teléfonos móviles– los abusos infligidos a prisioneros palestinos, a quienes deberíamos llamar “rehenes”, dada la falta de garantías mínimas legales que caracteriza las detenciones israelíes en el territorio palestino ocupado. Esta fragmentación territorial, legal y política es la institucionalización de la excepción; es la transformación de la precariedad en condiciones permanentes; es un sistema en el que la ocupación militar y la colonización ya no son sucesos aislados, sino un régimen consolidado en el que el control no sólo se ejerce con las armas sino también mediante la planificación urbanística, la burocracia, la segmentación administrativa, con la creación de categorías jurídicas diferenciadas para personas que viven en el mismo espacio pero no bajo los mismos derechos. Y después de décadas, la violencia de esta época nos indica que hemos llegado a la fase final: la del genocidio, la de la guerra de Israel contra un pueblo que hasta ahora ha resistido como ha podido. La mujer que amasa el pan bajo los drones, el maestro que sigue enseñando bajo las tiendas, la familia que planta un limonero donde el día antes había una casa, las parejas que siguen casándose y –también en el infierno de Gaza– trayendo hijos al mundo. articles.title: Revd Beilieü Shüya : The Pioneer of Christian Revival Church in Arunachal Pradesh
articles.summary: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary
articles.content: Revd Beilieü Shüya (15.8.1928 to 18.9.2026), remembered as the first CRC woman to be ordained, passed away at the age of 98 in Kohima, leaving behind a remarkable legacy of Christian faith, missionary commitment, education, and service. Her life was a testimony to perseverance, spiritual conviction, and obedience to the call of GOD, extending her influence beyond Nagaland into Arunachal Pradesh. The eldest of ten children of Lhousuohie Shüya and Zeno Dolie Shüya of Meriema village, she belonged to a family closely connected with the region’s Christian history. Her maternal grandfather was reportedly the second person from Khonoma village to embrace Christianity. Her mother was also the sister of Angami Zapu Phizo, the legendary Naga nationalist leader. An Exceptional Educational Journey Revd Shüya received her early education at Mission School, Kohima, before continuing her studies at Mission School, Golaghat, Government High School, Kohima, and Cotton College, Guwahati. She completed the first two years of her Bachelor of Arts degree at Scottish Church College, Calcutta, and her final year at Tribhuvan University, Nepal. Her academic achievements extended across several disciplines. She obtained a diploma from the International Montessori Association, Kolkata, completed a Perspective Course in Education at William Carey University, California, earned a Bachelor of Education degree from Utkal University, Bhubaneswar, and pursued a Master of Theology at Los Angeles University. She also earned a Master of Arts in Tenyidie from Ura Academy. Her educational background reflected a lifelong commitment to learning, teaching, and the development of people through knowledge and faith. A Life Transformed By The Holy Spirit A defining moment in her spiritual journey came in 1946, when she experienced what she described as the filling of the Holy Spirit. From then on, her life became increasingly devoted to Christian ministry rather than earthly popularity or recognition. In 1978, she was ordained at the World Mission Conference in Chennai, becoming the first CRC woman to receive ordination, according to accounts of her life. Her ordination represented a significant milestone for CRC women in Christian ministry and demonstrated her determination to serve despite the social and institutional challenges of her time. Her Christian convictions also brought hardship. She was imprisoned for her faith and reportedly imprisoned again in 1956 because of her family connection with A. Z. Phizo. During periods of imprisonment in Kohima, Nagaon, and Guwahati, she translated numerous passages of the Bible. Even confinement could not silence her commitment to GOD’S Word. Bringing The Revival Movement To Arunachal Pradesh Among her most significant contributions was her involvement in introducing the Christian revival movement to Arunachal Pradesh. Along with a few fellow believers and missionary friends, she helped bring a new spiritual impetus to Christian communities in the state. According to personal recollections, the early team undertook three days of fasting in a forest, seeking GOD’S guidance and spiritual empowerment. This pioneering work contributed to the establishment of the Christian Revival Church in Arunachal Pradesh. Her missionary journeys were not without opposition. There were occasions when the police reportedly attempted to arrest her for preaching the gospel in the state. Nevertheless, she continued her mission, demonstrating courage and perseverance in the face of persecution. I still vividly remember the excitement surrounding the visits of Miss Beilieü Shüya and Miss Rose, a missionary from Goa, to Jipu. People would say that GOD was going to perform signs, wonders, and miracles through their ministry. In Siji, where the community had embraced Christianity, the atmosphere within our families and the wider village was filled with spiritual enthusiasm and expectation. featured.summary_zh: 11月1日，六人在被富拉尼族极端分子关押超过六个月后，迈出了重获自由的第一步。其中一人仅两天后就去世了。13岁的哈萨娜·布卢斯（Hasana Bulus）在被送往医院时已处于危急状态，后在医院去世。布卢斯是富拉尼民兵绑架的11人之一……   这篇题为《少女被囚禁六个月后死亡》的文章最初发表在“国际基督徒关注”网站上。
featured.title_zh: 少女被囚禁六个月后死亡
featured.content: On Nov. 1, six people took their first steps of freedom after being held by Fulani extremists for more than six months. One of them died only two days later. Hasana Bulus, 13, died in the hospital where she was taken in critical condition. Bulus was one of the 11 people who were kidnapped by a Fulani militia in April. One had escaped, but five died at the camp, and the rest were released with Bulus — including the 4-year-old daughter of a woman who had died in captivity. Bulus’ village, Awon, is predominantly Christian and has been the target of Fulani attacks, just like Ariko, a neighboring village in Kaduna state. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. Ariko is home to the 37 Christians who were kidnapped during the Easter services earlier this year in a neighboring village. Of these, 17 people have died in captivity, 12 have escaped, and eight have since been released. The abductees from both these villages were held in the same forest hideout, where they were kept in inhumane conditions. “They [the villagers] told us how they would stay for two weeks without food,” one woman, whose father died in the camp, told Open Doors . “They only boil water to drink. That’s how they struggled before the bandits gave them corn flour, and they started making swallow (a porridge). The men are restrained, chained in groups; they are not free to move around.” All of the male abductees in these groups had died in the camp. Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW) is calling for Nigerian authorities to protect these communities and fight to free more people left in bondage. “We continue to urge the Nigerian government at state and federal levels to prioritize the protection of vulnerable communities throughout the nation, to combat the threat posed by the litany of terrorist groups that are active in the country far more effectively, and to secure the release of all abductees,” CSW CEO Scot Bower said. “Nigeria’s Christians do not need another statement of sympathy,” ICC’s president, Shawn Wright, said. “They need protection , justice , and accountability . When those who murder innocent Christians face no meaningful consequences, impunity becomes an invitation to the next attack. The Nigerian government must protect vulnerable communities, pursue the perpetrators, and make clear that these crimes will not go unanswered.” Story by Bella Agnello To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post Teenage Girl Dies After Six Months in Captivity first appeared on International Christian Concern .
featured.content_zh:
11月1日,六人在被富拉尼极端分子关押了6个多月后迈出了自由的第一步. 其中一人在两天后去世. 13岁的Hasana Bulus在她病情危急的医院死亡。 布卢斯是4月被富拉尼民兵绑架的11人之一.

1人逃跑了,但5人死于营地,其余的人与布卢斯一起被释放——包括一名在囚禁中死亡的妇女的4岁女儿. 与卡杜纳州邻近村庄阿里科一样,

根据非洲宗教自由观察站(ORFA)进行的一项为期六年的研究,伊斯兰富拉尼民兵是尼日利亚基督教徒最致命的迫害者。 阿里科是37名基督徒的家,他们在今年早些时候在复活节礼拜期间在一个邻近村庄被绑架。

其中,17人在囚禁中死亡,12人逃脱,8人自此获释. 这两个村庄的被绑架者被关在同一个森林藏身处,他们被关在不人道的条件下。 “他们[村民]告诉我们,他们将如何在没有食物的情况下呆两周,”一位父亲死于营地的妇女告诉Open Doors。 “他们只煮水饮用。

在土匪给他们面粉之前, 这些人被捆绑起来,被捆绑在一起;他们不能自由移动。” 这些团伙中的所有男性被绑架者都死于营地。

世界基督教团结会呼吁尼日利亚当局保护这些社区,并努力释放更多受奴役的人。

“我们继续敦促尼日利亚州和联邦政府优先保护全国的弱势社区,更有效地打击在该国活动的众多恐怖主义团体构成的威胁,并确保释放所有被绑架者。”

“尼日利亚的基督徒不需要再次表示同情, “他们需要保护、正义和问责制。 当杀害无辜基督徒的人没有面临有意义的后果时,有罪不罚就成为下一次袭击的诱因。

尼日利亚政府必须保护弱势社区,追捕肇事者,并表明这些罪行不会得不到答复。” Bella Agnello的故事 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作,

featured.title: A witch doctor got a solar radio. It was tuned to the truth
featured.summary: 🇨🇬Democratic Republic of Congo· 2010s
featured.summary_zh: 🇨🇬刚果民主共和国·21世纪10年代
featured.title_zh: 巫医有一台太阳能收音机。它被调到了真相频道
featured.content: Mbutu was a witch doctor in a remote village in the Democratic Republic of Congo. For years he cast spells, claimed power over the natural world, and sold cures to sick villagers who had nowhere else to turn. People feared him. He made his living off that fear. Then he was given a small solar-powered radio. It was fixed to one station, a local Christian broadcast, and handed out to villagers who had no other way to hear anything. Tuned to the truth So Mbutu listened. Day after day the good news came through that little speaker. He learned of the One who really controls the universe, and more than that, he learned about the love of Jesus and His offer of forgiveness. The man who had traded in fear laid his witchcraft down and gave his life to Christ. He did not keep it to himself. Mbutu now walks from village to village, finding other witch doctors and telling them what he found. Some of them have become believers. Some have become pastors, planting churches where there were none. A cheap radio and the name of Jesus were enough to turn the most feared man in the village into its brightest light. No one is beyond the reach of that name. Not the person others are afraid of. Not you.
featured.content_zh:
Mbutu是刚果民主共和国一个偏远村庄的一名巫医。 多年来,他施了咒语,声称对自然世界拥有权力,并出售给没有别处可转的病村民的治疗方法. 人们害怕他。 他靠恐惧为生 后被给予小型太阳能收音机.

它被固定在一个电台,一个当地的基督教广播,并交给没有其他办法听到任何消息的村民. 实话实说 姆博图听了 日复一日的好消息从那个小演讲者那里传来。 他得知了真正控制宇宙之人,不止于此,他还了解到了耶稣的爱和他提出的宽恕.

在恐惧中交易的人放下了巫术,将他的生命献给了基督. 他没有保守秘密。 姆布图现在从村到村走来走去,找到其他巫医,并告诉他们他发现了什么. 他们中有一部分已变成信士。 有些人成为牧师,在没有教堂的地方种植教堂。

featured.title_zh: 从迫害到毕业的旅程
featured.content: On Nov. 6, Titus Hassan Malika stood with his classmates and received his diploma — a quiet but powerful moment marking the end of a long, difficult road. The Sudanese Christian, who fled violence and persecution in his homeland, had received support from International Christian Concern (ICC). With God’s help, what once seemed impossible had become reality. “The support I received from ICC is a dream come true,” Malika said. “I never imagined that someone would stand with me for so many years, believing in my future when I could barely see it myself. This graduation is not only my achievement — it is the fruit of their faithfulness and God’s provision.” Titus grew up in Sudan, where following Jesus grew increasingly dangerous . As pressure on Christian communities intensified amid conflict and targeted hostility, he was forced to leave everything behind. With little more than his faith, he crossed into Kenya as a refugee, carrying the weight of loss, uncertainty, and the hope that God still had a future for him. By His Side In 2023, ICC stepped into that uncertainty. Through consistent support, practical help, encouragement, and the means to continue his studies, we walked with Titus through years of hardship. The path was not easy. He faced the daily challenges of life, the lingering trauma of persecution, and the enduring discipline of education while far from home. Yet he pressed on. “Jesus Christ has been the center of my life from the day I fled Sudan until this moment,” he said. “When I had no home, he was my shelter. When fear tried to silence me, he gave me courage. Every step of this journey has been possible only because he walked with me and never left me alone.” As he steps into his next chapter, Titus carries both a Bachelor’s degree in business administration and management, as well as a testimony that God can bring beauty from ashes, and that the Body of Christ, when it stands with the persecuted, can help rewrite a life marked by suffering into one marked by grace. “I give thanks to God for ICC, for they have been the hands and feet of Christ to me,” he said. “As it is written, ‘And my God will meet all your needs according to the riches of his glory in Christ Jesus’ (Philippians 4:19). Truly, the Lord has done this. May he continue to bless those who have poured out their lives so that I could stand here today.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . The post The Journey Through Persecution to Graduation first appeared on International Christian Concern .
featured.content_zh:
11月6日,蒂图斯·哈桑·马利卡与同学们站在一起,获得了他的文凭——一个静悄悄但强大的时刻,标志着漫长,艰难的道路的结束. 苏丹基督教徒在家乡躲避暴力和迫害,得到了国际基督教关注组织的支持。 在上帝的帮助下,过去似乎不可能实现的事情变成了现实。

Malika说,“我从国际刑事法院得到的支持是梦想成真”。 “我从未想到有人会和我站在一起这么多年,相信我的未来,而我几乎看不到未来。 这一毕业不仅是我的成就——这是他们忠心耿耿和上帝供给的成果。” Titus在苏丹长大,

由于在冲突和有目标的敌意中,对基督教社区的压力加剧,他被迫留下一切。 他带着微乎其微的信仰,以难民身份越境进入肯尼亚,背负着损失,不确定性的重担,希望上帝仍然有他的未来. 在他的身边 2023年,国际商会介入了这种不确定性。

通过始终如一的支持,实际帮助,鼓励,以及继续他学习的手段,我们和蒂图斯一起经历了多年的艰苦生活. 这条道路并不容易。 他每天都面临生活挑战、迫害造成的长期创伤以及远离家的持久教育纪律。 然而,他坚持着。

他说,“从我逃离苏丹到现在,耶稣基督一直是我生命的中心。” “当我没有家的时候,他是我的避难所。 当恐惧试图让我沉默时,他给了我勇气.

这段旅程的每一步都有可能,只是因为他与我同行,从未离开我。” 在他进入下一章时,Titus同时持有工商管理学士学位, 以及证明上帝能从灰烬中带来美丽, 以及基督的身体,当它与受迫害者站在一起时, 能够帮助重写以痛苦为标志的生活,

被恩典冲动 他说,“我为国际刑事法院感谢上帝,因为他们是基督的手脚。” " 上面写道: " 我 的 神 、 也 必 照 他 在 基督 耶穌 中 的 丰盛 、 满足 你 一切 的 需要 " ( 菲利浦 4: 19) 。 真的,上帝已经这样做了。

愿他继续保佑那些倾注生命的人,以便我今天能够站在这里。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件 支持电算中心在世界各地的工作, 文章《透过迫害到毕业的旅程》首次出现在国际基督教关注上。

featured.content: ABSTRACT: Just as the serpent led Adam and Eve into idolatry by reinterpreting God’s good word, so prosperity and word-of-faith preachers are today proclaiming a false and idolatrous gospel. But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology. For our ongoing series of feature articles for pastors and Christian leaders, we asked Dieudonné Tamfu (PhD, Southern Baptist Theological Seminary), pastor of Église Baptiste Bethléem and Assistant Professor of Bible and Theology and Director of the Cameroon Extension Site of Bethlehem College and Seminary, to introduce readers to the recently published Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . Christian leadership is war. When God calls a man to shepherd his flock, he calls him to war against wolves. Satan, the father of lies, and his minions hate the spiritual health of God’s people, wanting nothing more than to lead the people of God from truth to idolatry. The spiritual leaders of God’s flock are called to fight against Satan’s counterfeit gospels by proclaiming the word of God (Ephesians 6:17). When those leaders fall silent, when they fail to preach the sufficiency of Christ alone, they make space for Satan to lead the people of God into idolatry. As John Calvin rightly said, “Those in authority in the church turned over to idols the office of teaching for no other reason than that they themselves were mute.” 1 The muteness of faithful leaders gives voices to idols. Since Genesis 3, the devil has been in the business of poisoning the minds of God’s people with lies. In God’s good garden, the enemy came preaching lies: If God truly loves you, he will give you the fruit from the tree in the middle of the garden. Eve paid close attention while Adam idly stood by, mute. Thus he, his wife, and all his descendants died of the poison of Satan. The world is under the curse of sin because of a failure of leadership. 2 One of Satan’s most deceptive counterfeits plaguing both American and African churches is the prosperity gospel, a false teaching that elevates the idols of health, wealth, and power. David Oyedepo, a strong proponent of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, says, “Healing is the covenant right of every child of God . . . sickness has no right to feast on your life.” He goes on to proclaim healing over his congregation: “In the name of Jesus, I decree an end to every toil with sickness and disease.” He assures them that faith in Jesus means the end of sickness. 3 As I’ve written elsewhere, this “idolatrous perversion of the gospel” turns Jesus into “a means to God’s full blessings, primarily of health, wealth, and might” in the present life. 4 Its widespread success indicates a failure on the part of so-called shepherds to engage in spiritual warfare by speaking the whole testimony of God’s word. Today, many church leaders in Africa are boldly refusing to remain mute while the “new serpent,” the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology, reinterpret God’s goodness as mere material blessings. These bold leaders are now advancing the centrality of the true gospel by the recent publication of the Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . The present essay introduces the statement, first explaining why it is necessary, then summarizing its main points, and concluding with a warning against the syncretism of prosperity teaching. featured.title_zh: 穆斯林枪手在高原袭击中杀死6人后没有逮捕
featured.content: Suspected Muslim Gunmen killed at least six people, including a Nigerian soldier, in separate attacks on communities in Plateau state, Nigeria. The attacks occurred on Sunday night, Nov. 8, in Bel village, Sho community, Barkin Ladi Local Government Area (LGA), and Lakas community in Panyam, near the Mangu-Pankshin border in Mangu LGA. Four people, including three civilians and a soldier, were reportedly killed when gunmen stormed Bel village at about 9 p.m. and opened fire. A resident of Bel village, Bulus Bot, who confirmed the attack to International Christian Concern (ICC), said several people also sustained gunshot injuries. The attack forced residents to seek safety as gunfire rang through the community. He said the attackers are Islamic Fulani herders who want to take over their land. Rwang Tengwong, publicity secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association (BYM), confirmed the killings and identified three of the civilian victims as Emmanuel Pam Dachung, 15; Joseph Gyang, 28; and Emmanuel Yohanna, 32. The soldier has not been publicly identified. According to a six-year study conducted by the Observatory for Religious Freedom in Africa (ORFA), Islamic Fulani militias are by far the deadliest persecutors of Christians in Nigeria. The network of militias is responsible for four times more civilian deaths than the two prominent Islamic terror organizations, Boko Haram and Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP), combined. The study’s findings challenge the commonly held belief that the two organized terror groups kill the larger number of Christians, highlighting the Fulani network’s expanded efforts to target Christians. A Second Attack Two additional people were reportedly killed in a separate attack on the Lakas community in Panyam, bringing the reported death toll from the two incidents to at least six. “Muslim Fulani stopped us from going to the farm to harvest our crops, and we are now afraid to go to the church to worship,” Mathias said. “Nigerian authorities failed to protect us.” Tengwong told ICC that no arrests had been made following either attack. He specifically accused the Nigerian Army of failing to apprehend any of the suspected Fulani attackers. Tengwong condemned the killings and called on security agencies to identify and arrest those responsible, warning that the failure to apprehend attackers could leave surrounding communities exposed to further violence. Residents and eyewitnesses alleged that Fulani extremists carried out the attacks, targeting predominantly Christian communities. Some residents described the assaults as part of a pattern of violence aimed at taking over ancestral lands and forcing indigenous populations from their communities. These allegations could not be independently verified. The latest attacks add to continuing reports of armed assaults against rural communities in Plateau, particularly in Barkin Ladi, Bassa, Riyom, and Mangu local government areas, where Christian farming communities have repeatedly reported killings, destruction of property, displacement, and threats to their livelihoods. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . To support ICC’s work around the world, please give to our Where Most Needed Fund . 据报,有4人,包括3名平民和1名士兵,在晚上9时左右枪手冲进Bel村并开火时被打死。 Bel村的一名居民Bulus Bot向国际基督教关注组织证实这次袭击,他说,一些人也遭到枪伤。 袭击迫使居民在枪声响彻社区时寻求安全。

他说袭击者是伊斯兰富拉尼牧民,他们想占领他们的土地. 贝罗姆青年穆尔德斯协会(BYM)宣传秘书Rwang Tengwong证实了这些杀人事件,并指认了3名平民受害者:15岁的Emmanuel Pam Dachung;28岁的Joseph Gyang;32岁的Emmanuel Yohanna。 该士兵尚未公开确认身份。

根据非洲宗教自由观察站(ORFA)进行的一项为期六年的研究,伊斯兰富拉尼民兵是尼日利亚基督教徒最致命的迫害者。 民兵网络造成平民死亡的人数是博科圣地和西非伊斯兰国省这两个著名的伊斯兰恐怖组织的四倍。

研究结论质疑人们的普遍看法,即两个有组织的恐怖集团杀害了更多的基督徒,突出了富拉尼网络扩大针对基督徒的努力。 第二次攻击 据报告,在对Panyam的Lakas社区进行的另一次袭击中,又有两人丧生,据报这两起事件的死亡人数至少达6人。

Mathias说:“穆斯林Fulani阻止我们去农场收获作物, “尼日利亚当局未能保护我们。” Tengwong告诉国际刑事法院,在两次袭击之后都没有逮捕任何人。 他具体指责尼日利亚军队没有逮捕任何涉嫌的Fulani袭击者。

Tengwong谴责这些杀人事件,呼吁安全机构查明并逮捕肇事者,并警告说,不逮捕袭击者可能会使周围的社区面临进一步的暴力。 居民和目击者指称,Fulani极端分子进行攻击,攻击目标主要是基督教社区。

一些居民称,这些袭击是旨在夺取祖传土地和强迫土著人口离开其社区的暴力模式的一部分。 这些指控无法独立核实。

最近发生的攻击事件使有关对高原农村社区,特别是Barkin Ladi、Bassa、Riyom和Mangu地方政府地区的农村社区进行武装攻击的不断报道更为严重。 在那里,基督教农耕社区一再报告杀害、毁坏财产、流离失所和威胁其生计。 阅读更多新闻,

featured.content: A Senegalese Christian shares the gospel with event volunteers during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo As athletes and spectators from around the world fill the streets of Senegal for the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games, missionaries and local believers are praying the event will leave behind more than medals and memories. For Carson West, an International Mission Board missionary serving in Senegal, the Games represent a unique opportunity not only to engage visitors with the gospel but also to mobilize local churches to take a more active role in evangelism long after the Olympic flame is extinguished. “This is the first Olympic event ever held on the continent of Africa,” West said. “For us, it was an opportunity to ask, ‘What are we going to do with this?’” The Youth Olympic Games, which began Oct. 31 and end Nov. 13, are taking place across three host cities: Dakar, Diamniadio and Saly. Event organizers expect nearly 2,700 athletes, ages 14-17, to participate in 35 sports and represent more than 200 delegations. The Games have drawn a million spectators, and West reported more than 6,000 event volunteers are staffing all the venues. With so many people gathering in Senegal, West and his team concentrated on preparing Senegalese churches for evangelistic opportunities. “We could run and hide, or we could do this thing,” West said, recalling an early conversation with teammates. “We decided we were going to do this thing.” The 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, is the first Olympic event held on the continent of Africa. IMB Photo West serves as team leader for IMB work in Senegal, where ministry efforts focus on three areas: gospel engagement, church advancement and community development. The Youth Olympic outreach naturally aligns with the first two priorities. “Our approach has been to mobilize the local church,” he said. “This is their backyard.” Instead of relying on a large influx of international volunteers, though there is one volunteer team from the United States serving, the strategy has centered on equipping local believers. Senegal has four Baptist churches in the greater Dakar area. Many leaders representing the congregations, as well as other ministry partners, participated in evangelism training designed specifically for the Games. Church leaders and ministry partners in Senegal participate in an evangelism training session specifically designed to share the gospel during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. IMB Photo A key outreach method involves trading commemorative pins, a familiar Olympic tradition. Volunteers use the exchange as a natural conversation starter before offering gospel-centered materials. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code connected to a digital engagement platform adapted from previous Olympic and World Cup outreaches. Visitors who scan the code are directed to online resources and can connect with trained digital responders. Experienced volunteers in the U.S. are helping provide follow-up conversations. “We’re building on strategies that have been used effectively in previous Olympic Games,” West said. “It’s an easy, non-intimidating way to start gospel conversations.” Trading commemorative pins is an Olympic tradition. Volunteers use these pins to start gospel-driven conversations during the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Each pin is accompanied by a card featuring a QR code that connects people to trained digital responders. IMB Photo The effort extends beyond Dakar. IMB teams and church partners are positioned in each of the three host cities. An IMB team, which includes three global missionary partners, is helping coordinate outreach efforts in Diamniadio, and an IMB team along with a Baptist church is organizing efforts in Saly. West believes the greatest potential impact may be felt not among international visitors but among Senegalese believers themselves. Senegal is approximately 95% Muslim and 0.2% evangelical. featured.title_zh: 刚果民主共和国曼巴萨地区在埃博拉疫情期间至少有26人死亡
featured.content: Twenty-six people have reportedly been killed and several others abducted in a new attack carried out by the Islamist rebels of Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) on Nov. 10, during the night, in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, northeastern DR Congo, a country where nearly 93% of the population is Christian. According to a local association coordinator, Malikidogo, more than six villages were affected, including Kangwayi, Misele, Mingazi, and Mambaka. “The situation is very serious; we identified 26 people killed, several others abducted, and many families are still searching for their missing loved ones,” Malikidogo said. “Aside from the death of many people, five houses were burnt alongside some motorcycles. We are calling on the authorities to take urgent action to protect the population.” Left With Nothing Survivors who succeeded in escaping reported that many families had to run for their lives, leaving their homes and belongings behind. “We were very afraid when we realized that the enemies were already in the village when we heard people crying and others running in every direction,” one survivor said. “We just fled without having time to collect our belongings, just to save our lives. We do not know what will happen next, and we are afraid that they might come and reach Mambasa city where we are today.” The attack comes at a difficult time for local communities, which are already facing the threat of Ebola . Residents are now dealing with both the fear of the disease and the danger of further attacks. There are concerns that the violence could also make it harder to control the Ebola outbreak. People fleeing their villages may spread the disease to other communities, while insecurity could prevent health workers from reaching those who need medical help. A local leader also expressed concern about the situation and called for stronger protection of civilians. “We have suffered for many years because of the atrocities committed by ADF Islamist terrorists,” he said. “We are already struggling with Ebola, and now we are facing these attacks again. We cannot continue living like this. We are calling on the government and security forces to protect our communities before more innocent lives are lost.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 据当地协会协调员Malikidogo说,有6个以上的村庄受到影响,其中包括Kangwayi、Misele、Mingazi和Mambaka。 “局势非常严重;我们确认有26人被杀害,另有数人被绑架,许多家庭仍在寻找失踪的亲人。”

“除了许多人的死亡外,还有五所房屋与一些摩托车一起被烧毁。 我们呼吁当局采取紧急行动保护人民。” 成功逃脱的幸存者一无所有地离开,报告说,许多家庭不得不逃命,留下家园和财物。

一位幸存者说,“当我们意识到敌人已经在村里时,我们非常害怕,当我们听到人们在哭,而其他人则朝每个方向奔跑时”。 “我们刚刚逃离,没有时间收集我们的财产,只是为了拯救我们的生命。

我们不知道接下来会发生什么,我们担心他们会来到我们今天所在的曼巴萨市。” 袭击发生在当地社区面临埃博拉威胁的困难时刻。 居民们现在正在处理对疾病的恐惧和进一步攻击的危险。

人们担心暴力也可能使控制埃博拉疫情变得更加困难。 逃离村庄的人可能把这种疾病传播到其他社区,而不安全则可能妨碍保健工作者帮助需要医疗帮助的人。 一名当地领导人还对局势表示关切,呼吁加强对平民的保护。

他说,“由于民主同盟军伊斯兰恐怖分子的暴行,我们受苦多年。” “我们已经在与埃博拉作斗争,现在我们再次面临这些袭击。 我们不能继续这样生活。 我们要求政府和安全部队在更多的无辜者丧生之前保护我们的社区。” 阅读更多新闻,

featured.title_zh: 在最近的ADF攻击中超过30人死亡
featured.content: Fear, bloodshed, and devastation have once again descended upon communities in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) stormed Cantine in the Madiwe sector of Beni territory, in the North Kivu Province during the night of Thursday, Nov. 5, into the early hours of Nov. 6, leaving civilians dead, homes burning, and an already vulnerable population gripped by terror. Justin Paluku, president of the Civil Society Forces Vives of Madiwe, confirmed that the provisional death toll stood at more than 30 civilians. “For families that went to bed hoping to wake up to another ordinary morning, the night turned into a nightmare of unimaginable suffering,” Paluku said. “We are deeply concerned about the safety of our population. Christian Civilians cannot continue living like prisoners in their own communities, constantly wondering when armed men will strike again. Our people deserve protection, peace and the freedom to live without fear.” Seeking Safety As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing Cantine toward neighboring areas considered relatively safer. Children, women, and the elderly are among those facing the uncertainty of displacement, leaving behind homes, livelihoods, and personal belongings. For Christian survivors, the immediate concern is no longer what tomorrow will bring, but whether they will survive another attack . “We heard the sounds of violence, and fear immediately took control of us,” a survivor of the attack said. “We had no time to collect our belongings. All we wanted was to escape with our lives. We have lost our sense of security, and we do not know whether we will ever return to our homes again.” The reported burning of homes and looting of property represent more than material destruction. They strip Christian families of their dignity, deepen their vulnerability, and leave children exposed to hunger, insecurity, and psychological trauma. The wider Beni region has endured years of repeated attacks, killings, abductions, and displacement attributed to armed groups, particularly the ADF. Each new incident adds another painful chapter to the suffering of communities that continue to demand protection and justice. To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . featured.title_zh: 民主同盟军重返卢贝罗，在埃博拉危机中散布恐惧
featured.content: After nearly half a year away, fighters from the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) have returned to Lubero territory in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). On Tuesday morning, Nov. 3, the Islamic extremist ADF attacked Maikengu village, terrorizing the community. According to local authorities, “the attackers looted homes and businesses before setting fire to houses, shops, and pharmacies. As news of the attack spread, residents began fleeing for safety. Some are heading toward Kambau and Nziapanda, leaving behind their homes and everything they worked hard to build. In this attack, one Christian was found killed with a machete alongside many others who remain untraceable.” For many families, this is another painful reminder that nowhere feels truly safe. While people are already worried about Ebola and the loss of loved ones due to this disease, they are now once again facing the fear of being killed, kidnapped, or forced to flee by Islamist terrorists. “We have already lost so much to Ebola disease, and now we are afraid of losing even more,” a woman named Jannette said. “Doctors, church leaders and local leaders are advising us to avoid crowded places, or avoid unnecessary visits, but today, with the new ADF attack, we were obliged to run for our lives. Every day, we worry about our families; we just want to live in peace and feel safe in our villages.” Renewed Trauma Maikengu is no stranger to this suffering because during the ADF’s first invasion of Bapere in June 2024, the ADF Islamist killed 42 people in many villages around it. The group’s return has reopened painful memories and renewed fears among residents who had hoped to rebuild their lives and worship God peacefully in their churches. The Congolese army has begun deploying troops to the area to stop the militants’ advance. However, for local Christians and other vulnerable civilians, the urgent need is for lasting protection, peace, and the chance to live without fear. The ADF’s return comes amid growing concerns over its activities in the region, including allegations that the group is exploiting local gold resources to finance its violence. According to a report by The Sentry , “the ADF generates approximately $1 million to $1.6 million annually from gold mines it controls in the Manguredjipa area alone, and it controls several other gold-rich territories. Abduction remains the backbone of the ADF’s manpower, supplying labor, recruits, and dependents, while reinforcing control through systematic violence.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . 在这次袭击中,一名基督教徒被砍刀打死,还有许多人至今下落不明。” 对许多家庭来说,这是另一个痛苦的提醒,没有任何地方真正感到安全。 虽然人们已经担心埃博拉和由于这一疾病而失去亲人,但他们现在再次面临被伊斯兰恐怖分子杀害、绑架或被强迫逃离的恐惧。

“我们已经因埃博拉疾病而损失了这么多,现在我们害怕失去更多,”一位叫Jannette的妇女说。 “医生、教会领导人和地方领导人建议我们避免拥挤的地方,或避免不必要的探访,但今天,随着民主同盟军的新袭击,我们不得不奔跑。 我们每天都在担心家人;

我们只想和平地生活,在我们村庄中感到安全。” 由于民主同盟军于2024年6月第一次入侵巴佩尔,民主同盟军的伊斯兰教徒在附近许多村庄杀害了42人,所以再次遭受创伤的Maikengu并不陌生。

该团体的返回使那些希望重建自己生活并和平地在教堂中崇拜上帝的居民重燃了痛苦的记忆和恐惧。 刚果军队已开始在该地区部署部队来阻止好战分子的前进。

然而,对于当地基督徒和其他弱势平民来说,迫切需要持久的保护、和平和无所畏惧地生活的机会。 民主同盟军的返回正值人们对其在该地区的活动日益关切之时,包括据称该团体正在利用当地黄金资源来资助其暴力。

根据《哨兵报》的一份报告,“民主同盟军从它仅控制Manguredjipa地区的金矿中每年产生大约100万至160万美元的收入,它控制着其他几个黄金丰富的领土。

featured.title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
featured.summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
featured.summary_zh: 🇸🇩哈萨希萨·2022年
featured.title_zh: 他为母亲感染的腿祈祷。然后，他的穆斯林邻居开始前来
featured.content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.
featured.content_zh:
Abdalla Haron Sulieman牧师在苏丹El Hasahisa聚集了他的小教堂,为其母亲祈祷。 艾莎·亚当六十岁 腿部感染使她疲惫不堪 他们祈祷,她恢复了。 看起来像一个私人家庭的怜悯 并没有长期保持私人。 关于治愈的传言传遍了大部分是穆斯林的城镇。 人们开始出现在教堂。 不为辩才.

问治愈艾莎的神能否治愈他们 当治愈变成一扇门 这正是那种让人害怕的东西。 当地的极端分子逼迫警察逮捕苏利曼,他们确实如此,根据旧法指控他自称巫医,仿佛对耶稣的爱是一种巫术.

苏丹各地的信徒都认同他的名字,要求释放他。 "这是对苏丹基督徒的严重侵犯",一位名叫弗朗西斯·伊斯梅尔的福音者说. 但请注意恐惧无法消除 一个母亲很好 一个穆斯林城镇看到了耶稣的名字做一些真实的事情,从未进入教堂的邻居走进教堂寻找他.

上帝仍然痊愈,他仍然使用一个普通的应答祷告来打开一个没人能关闭的门. 他可以打开一个你的地方。

featured.title_zh: 食堂大屠杀4天后遇害
featured.content: Just days after the deadly massacre in Cantine, where at least 33 civilians were reportedly killed, suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters have struck again in Beni Territory, claiming four more lives and burning several houses in Mabalako, in the Democratic Republic of Congo. At about 12:20 a.m. on Thursday, Nov. 12, Mabalako once again faced ADF violence , with a fresh overnight attack in the Kamahume neighborhood. According to local civil society representatives, the death toll rose from an initial three to four, while more than seven houses were also set ablaze during the deadly incursion. The attack has renewed fears among civilians already traumatized by the violence that struck Cantine-Aloya less than a week earlier. The proximity of these two attacks in time and location has heightened concerns about the continuing threat posed by the ADF to civilian populations across Beni. “We are living in constant fear,” said Mulwahali, a survivor. “We have not yet recovered from the pain of what happened in Cantine, where innocent people were brutally killed and homes reduced to ashes. Now the violence has reached Mabalako, and once again we are mourning our loved ones and watching our homes burn. We do not know who will be next or where these attackers will strike again. We are even tired of burying our people without heads. All we want is to live in peace and sleep in our homes without fearing that we may never see another morning.” A Need for Security Local civil society representatives have appealed to security services to take full responsibility for protecting civilians, strengthen security operations, and prevent further attacks. Residents of Runzayi, Malondo, Ngazi, and Kibunamaru have also been urged to remain vigilant, maintain calm, and cooperate with security forces by reporting suspicious movements. “We cannot continue living at the mercy of armed attackers,” a local Catholic bishop said. “Although the intervention of the FARDC helped limit the destruction in Mabalako, the fact that the attackers could strike and disappear without their direction being known leaves us deeply frightened. We want security, not another massacre.” To read more news stories, visit the ICC Newsroom . For interviews, please email us . featured.content_zh:
据报道,在坎廷发生了至少33名平民被杀的致命屠杀事件,几天后,疑似民主同盟军(民主同盟军)战斗人员再次袭击了贝尼县,在刚果民主共和国的马巴拉科又造成4人死亡,几所房屋被烧毁。 11月,星期四上午12点20分左右.

马巴拉科再次面临民主同盟军的暴力, 据当地民间社会代表说,死亡人数从最初的3人增加到4人,而在致命的入侵中,还有七座房屋被点燃。

袭击使已经因不到一周前袭击Cantine-Aloya的暴力而受到创伤的平民再次感到恐惧。 这两起袭击在时间和地点上接近,使人们更加担心民主同盟军对贝尼各地平民继续构成威胁。 幸存者穆尔瓦哈利说:“我们生活在持续的恐惧之中”。

“我们尚未从坎廷发生的痛苦中恢复过来,在那里,无辜者惨遭杀害,家园沦为灰烬。 现在,暴力已蔓延到马巴拉科,我们再次哀悼我们的亲人,并观看我们的家园被烧毁。 我们不知道下一个是谁,也不知道这些袭击者将在哪里再次袭击。 我们甚至厌倦了无头埋葬我们的人民。

我们只想在家中过上和平的生活和睡觉,而不必担心再有早晨。” 地方民间社会代表呼吁安全部门全面负责保护平民,加强安全行动,防止进一步的袭击。

还敦促Runzayi、Malondo、Ngazi和Kibunamaru的居民保持警惕,保持平静,并与安全部队合作,报告可疑行动。 一位当地天主教主教说,“我们不能继续受武装袭击者的摆布”。

“虽然刚果(金)武装部队的干预有助于限制对马巴拉科的破坏,但袭击者可能袭击并消失而不了解他们的方向这一事实使我们深感恐惧。 我们要的是安全,而不是另一次屠杀。” 阅读更多新闻, 请给我们发电子邮件

featured.content: How old were you when you first learned that Jesus loves you? Perhaps you’ve always known it and can’t remember a day when you didn’t know the song “Jesus Loves Me” or couldn’t recite John 3:16 by heart. Maybe you were a teenager and learned about Jesus’ love through a friend or church summer camp. Or were in college and went to a concert where the gospel was clearly articulated. Maybe you were in the trenches of the workforce, and a coworker boldly shared with you about the God who radically changed their life. Regardless of how old you were, each of us who has chosen to follow Jesus has an origin story — a moment in our lives when the knowledge that “Jesus loves me, this I know, for the Bible tells me so” moved from head knowledge to heart belief. And from then on, our lives were transformed forever. This is the truth of the gospel and the power of understanding that Jesus loves you. People around the world are discovering the personal truth of John 3:16 for themselves in a language and format they clearly understand. Explore why understanding that “God so loved the world” transforms entire communities → A Changing Reality Throughout Christian history, the gospel has spread from one community to the next. Stories were told and retold, Scripture was translated, churches were planted, and discipleship deepened as people learned more about Jesus. Bible translation is foundational to all ministries of the church. It fuels evangelism, church planting, discipleship and more. It equips people to move from a blurry picture of who God is to a clear understanding and personal encounter with Jesus as Lord. Through Scripture, people are able to read, hear or see the love of God on display. Just two decades ago, most of the world’s language communities still needed Bible translation work to begin , let alone be completed. But praise God, in the last few years, we’ve seen tremendous progress made, with Bible translation underway in more languages than ever before . While the change in numbers is exciting, what’s more important is what they signify: Every number represents a person who has a story that matters to God. For these communities, the stories of future generations are being completely rewritten as children will now grow up never remembering a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. That statement bears repeating: There will now be people who never remember a day when they didn’t have access to God’s Word in a language and format they clearly understand. From the first word of Genesis to the last word of Revelation, the Bible tells one incredible story: God’s love for the world and His invitation for people from every nation and language to know Him. Get a glimpse of how God continues writing this story today as more and more people are experiencing the power of His Word. Watch the video → A New Generation Growing Up With God’s Word Let’s take a look at some of the recent communities that are experiencing not only life transformation but generational transformation as they encounter Jesus personally through Scripture. Jakalteko | Guatemala The Jakalteko Bible was dedicated in July 2026 in Guatemala! During the celebration, John 1:1-18 was read aloud — a passage that focuses on Christ, the eternal Word and our Redeemer. Early on, many women in the community memorized Job 19 . Like Job, they had faced various hardships in their lives and identified with his suffering. The book reminded them that God remains in control and that, in the midst of difficult circumstances, their Redeemer will deliver them and comfort them in their pain. Today, they have the full counsel of God’s Word and can now see this Redeemer fulfilled in Jesus in the New Testament. They are overjoyed that the Bible has arrived in the language they were born into! When the Bible was distributed, one mother who is raising her family alone said with joy and tears: “Thank God we have the Bible in our language. Now

featured.summary_zh: 在尼日利亚博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统就其未能保护人民免受袭击一事呼吁原谅的几天后，在高原州的四个地方政府辖区内发生的最新袭击中，至少有14名基督徒被杀害。
