featured.content: El “Tomus ad Flavianum”: piedra angular del dogma cristológico León Magno fue un teólogo de precisión y profundidad extraordinarias. Su famosa carta doctrinal al patriarca Flaviano de Constantinopla —conocida como el Tomus ad Flavianum— definió con claridad la doctrina católica sobre las dos naturalezas de Cristo: divina y humana, unidas en una sola Persona. Este documento fue leído en el Concilio de Calcedonia (451) ante cientos de obispos que, al escucharlo, exclamaron: “Pedro ha hablado por boca de León.” Con esa expresión, la Iglesia universal reconocía el primado de la sede romana y la continuidad entre el Apóstol Pedro y sus sucesores. En tiempos en que el poder imperial pretendía someter la doctrina al control político, León reivindicó que la autoridad del Papa no depende del César ni de los concilios, sino de Cristo mismo, que prometió: “Tú eres Pedro, y sobre esta piedra edificaré mi Iglesia.” Gracias a su intervención, el Concilio de Calcedonia se convirtió en un hito de la ortodoxia cristológica y en un testimonio de la primacía del Romano Pontífice. El Papa León no impuso su autoridad con la fuerza, sino con la verdad; no por ambición humana, sino por fidelidad al depósito recibido. El Papa que detuvo a Atila En el año 452, la amenaza de los hunos llegó hasta las puertas de Italia. Atila, llamado “el azote de Dios”, había devastado Europa central y avanzaba hacia Roma. Sin ejército ni armas, León decidió ir al encuentro del invasor acompañado solo de algunos clérigos. El encuentro en el río Mincio, cerca de Mantua, se convirtió en uno de los episodios más sobrecogedores de la historia. La tradición narra que Atila, al ver al Papa, quedó sobrecogido por una fuerza sobrenatural y decidió retirarse. Algunos cronistas antiguos dicen que el caudillo vio detrás de León a los santos Pedro y Pablo empuñando espadas. Fuera cual fuera la causa, el hecho histórico es indiscutible: el Papa, solo con su autoridad moral, salvó a Roma de una destrucción segura. Tres años después, en el 455, León volvió a intervenir ante el vándalo Genserico, quien, aunque saqueó la ciudad, accedió a no incendiarla ni matar a sus habitantes. En una era de barbarie y desesperanza, el Papa se convirtió en defensor de la dignidad humana y de la civilización cristiana naciente. Un pastor de almas y doctor de la fe Más allá de los hechos históricos, el legado espiritual de León Magno se encuentra en sus Sermones y Cartas, textos que combinan rigor teológico, belleza retórica y profundidad pastoral. Sus homilías sobre la Encarnación y la Pascua son verdaderas joyas del pensamiento cristiano. En ellas resuena una teología que no separa la doctrina de la vida, ni la fe de la caridad. Fue también un reformador eclesial: disciplinó al clero, combatió los abusos, promovió la vida monástica y fortaleció la autoridad episcopal. Instituyó la solemnidad de la Natividad del Señor en Roma y consolidó la liturgia romana, que más tarde se extendería a toda la cristiandad. En un tiempo en que el caos amenazaba con disolver las instituciones, León mostró que la verdadera reforma de la Iglesia comienza en la santidad de sus pastores. De su espiritualidad brota una enseñanza perenne: el cristiano no puede dejarse arrastrar por el miedo ni por la confusión del mundo. Como escribió en una de sus homilías más célebres: “Reconoce, cristiano, tu dignidad. Y, puesto que has sido hecho partícipe de la naturaleza divina, no vuelvas a la antigua vileza con una conducta indigna.” En esas palabras se resume toda su visión: la fe no es una idea, sino una transformación de la persona; una participación real en la vida de Cristo. El Doctor que iluminó siglos León Magno murió el 10 de noviembre del año 461. Fue sepultado en la Basílica de San Pedro y proclamado Doctor de la Iglesia en el siglo XVIII por el Papa Benedicto XIV. Su influencia doctrinal se extendió por siglos y moldeó el pensamiento cristiano sobre el sacerdocio, la autoridad papal y la teología de la Encarnación. Su magi

Si certains villages ont été entièrement dépeuplés et rasés, d’autres se maintiennent, non sans grandes difficultés. Lundi 9 novembre, les maires de cinq villages chrétiens ont lancé un appel à l’aide au Conseil des patriarches et des évêques catholiques du Liban, dont la session annuelle se tient toute la semaine. Les cinq édiles demandent aux chefs de l’Église un soutien pour sécuriser les routes, permettre le « retour volontaire des déplacés » et l’accès sans risque aux terrains agricoles, ou encore la protection du patrimoine religieux. Le père Najib Alamil, prêtre dans l’un des cinq villages, à Rmeich, témoigne des nombreuses épreuves vécues par les habitants au quotidien. « On dit souvent que les habitants du Sud-Liban sont habitués à la guerre. featured.summary_zh: 在拉塞尔·布兰德的伦敦强奸案庭审中，经其律师提出异议，检方同意从开庭陈述中删除提及凯蒂·佩里的内容。该决定于11月5日星期四公布。

featured.content: Prosecutors agreed to remove references to Katy Perry from their opening statement at Russell Brand's London rape trial after objections from his lawyers. The decision emerged on Thursday, 5 November 2026, after a jury returned verdicts at Southwark Crown Court. Brand, 51, was convicted of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault involving four women. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape charges and one count of attempted indecent assault. He had denied all seven charges, which concerned six women. Details of the pretrial discussions became public after reporting restrictions ended. They showed how Brand's former marriage was kept out of the prosecution's opening address, although he later mentioned Perry while giving evidence. Why Katy Perry References Were Removed From the Opening Lead prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones KC acknowledged in written submissions that references to Brand's relationship with Perry after 2009 'may be sensitive'. According to Sky News' court reporting, prosecutors were 'content to remove these from the opening' following defence submissions. The agreement was limited to the opening statement. It did not prevent every mention of Perry during the proceedings or establish that the relationship itself was evidence of wrongdoing. Perry was not accused of any offence. Prosecutors also agreed to leave out references to Brand's earlier religious beliefs and his 2024 baptism. His Christian conversion was nevertheless mentioned during questioning of his wife, Laura, showing that the restrictions on the opening did not cover all subsequent testimony. Other arguments before the trial concerned references to Brand's past drug and alcohol use. His lawyers challenged their relevance to the allegations, and material about treatment at a sex addiction clinic was omitted from a former assistant's evidence. Those disputes were separate from the agreement concerning Perry. The Crown Prosecution Service confirmed that investigators had not asked Perry for a witness statement. Senior Crown Prosecutor David Roberts said reasonable lines of inquiry relevant to the charges had been pursued. There is no basis in that statement to suggest Perry refused to cooperate. Katy Perry's Marriage Still Entered the Courtroom Perry and Brand began dating in 2009 and married in Rajasthan, India, in 2010. They separated in December 2011, and their divorce was finalised in 2012. The offences for which Brand was convicted took place between 2004 and 2009. During his evidence, Brand referred to the marriage and said it had brought him 'staggering fame'. The comment arose from his own testimony, not the prosecution's opening statement. It did not turn Perry into a witness or complainant. The Crown Prosecution Service said the women whose cases resulted in convictions came forward independently after a television investigation aired in September 2023. Prosecutors relied on their accounts and testimony from other witnesses to present evidence of Brand's conduct. Following the verdict, Roberts said Brand had 'used his celebrity status to commit sexual crimes'. The agency thanked the women for coming forward and stressed that sexual offences can be prosecuted years after they occur. The complainants have lifelong anonymity. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan refused Brand bail and remanded him in custody ahead of sentencing on Monday, 9 November. The judge warned that he faced a 'significant custodial term'. Rape carries a maximum penalty of life imprisonment in England and Wales. © Copyright IBTimes 2026. All rights reserved.

陪审员宣布他无罪,罪名是另外两项强奸指控和一项企图猥亵罪。 他否认了涉及6名妇女的所有7项指控。 审前讨论的细节在报告限制结束后公布。 他们展示了布兰德以前的婚姻如何被保留在检方的开幕词之外,尽管他后来在提供证据时提到了佩里.

为何Katy Perry的参考文献被从开业首席检察官Riel Karmy-Jones KC删除, 根据Sky News的法庭报道, 检察官在辩方陈述之后, 协议仅限于开场白。

然而,在审问他的妻子劳拉时,他皈依基督教被提到,这表明对开庭的限制并不包括后来的所有证词。 审判前的其他论点涉及布兰德过去吸毒和酗酒的情况。

他的律师对这些指控的相关性提出质疑,前助理的证据中遗漏了在性瘾诊所治疗的材料。 这些争端与关于佩里的协议是分开的。 皇家检察机关确认调查人员没有要求佩里提供证人证词.

高级皇家检察官David Roberts说,已经对指控进行了合理的调查。 该声明没有根据表明Perry拒绝合作。 Katy Perry's Marriage Still into the Courtroom Perry and Brand)于2009年开始约会,2010年在印度拉贾斯坦邦结婚. 他们于2011年12月分居,2012年最终离婚.

Brand被定罪的罪行发生在2004年至2009年期间。 在他的证据中,布兰德提到了这段婚姻,并说这给他带来了"恶搞的名声". 评论来自他本人的证词,而不是检方的开场白。 它没有将Perry变成证人或投诉人。

皇家检察院说,在2023年9月播出的电视调查之后,那些案件导致定罪的妇女独立地站出来。 检察官依靠他们的陈述和其他证人的证词来提出布兰德行为的证据. 判决后,罗伯茨表示布兰德"利用名人身份犯下性犯罪".

该机构感谢这些妇女站出来,并强调在性犯罪发生数年后可以对其进行起诉。 申诉人一生匿名。 Joel Bennathan法官拒绝了Brand保释,并在11月9日星期一判决前还押候审。 法官警告说,他面临“重大监禁期”。

featured.content: I’m excited to tell you the story of how God used a simple verse, from a complicated passage, to change the life of a man named Charles Spurgeon. His story is for everyone, but it may have a special word to speak to a few groups in the room. One is laymen — that is, people who work for a living in normal jobs, outside of Christian ministry. People without a seminary education, people who aren’t pastors or have ministry jobs. We recognize that this series has profiled four men who were preachers. Now, there is an interesting flow to our series: - first, Saint Augustine, - then, Luther, who was an Augustinian monk, - then, John Bunyan, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Luther’s commentary on Galatians, - now, Charles Spurgeon, whose favorite book outside the Bible was Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress. We’ve moved from one convert to another, each building in some way on the previous one, but a weakness of our series (in some sense) is that they all became preachers. And we don’t expect you all to become preachers; we’d like a few, but most will be laymen, and that’s good. Now, Spurgeon is known as “the Prince of Preachers.” But the hero, under God, in Spurgeon’s story is not Spurgeon, and not a trained, paid preacher, but a layman. So, Spurgeon’s story has a special word for laymen who are willing to open their mouths and say what they know about Jesus. Spurgeon’s story also has a special word for teens and young adults. Spurgeon came to faith at age fifteen, which in his day was far more like young adulthood. Still, his story offers a challenge to those who are no longer children and not yet established adults: teens, college students, grad students, even young professionals. Don’t let the world (or the church) lower your standards of what’s possible in being deeply converted and dedicated to Jesus — and how God can make his Son thrilling to a young soul. My prayer is that God might be pleased to give some their own engine. So often, parents, college workers, and pastors help young adults along and give them pushes. And then sometimes, God is pleased in the life of teenagers to give them their own engine, and they don’t need any more pushing. They say, “Get out of my way! I am going to follow Jesus. You can’t keep me from him and worship, my Bible, and prayer!” That’s what God did for Spurgeon at age fifteen — he gave him his own engine. And I pray he might be pleased to do that even here this morning. Spurgeon’s story speaks to one more group: those in the room who are willing to admit, “I’m here but I’m not saved.” For two thousand years, unsaved people have shown up at churches for all sorts of reasons. That’s Spurgeon’s story. He was searching. He was unsaved and in a church on a Sunday morning when God broke through. So, if you’d say this morning, “I haven’t settled the issue of my sin and rebellion against God,” or “I haven’t ‘been saved,’” or “if I died on the drive home today, I wouldn’t be at peace with my Maker,” this story has a special word for you. So, let me tell you about Charlie Spurgeon. His Early and Whole Life He was born in 1834, about 40 miles northeast of London, into a Christian family. In fact, both his father and grandfather were pastors. But his father met financial troubles and sent the young Charles to live with his grandparents from ages one to six. I don’t think this is an insignificant part of the story; don’t underestimate the effects of a good grandma and grandpa in the lives of our children. From their influence he emerged as “precocious,” learned to read, and first found Bunyan’s Pilgrim’s Progress (which he would read more than a hundred times). From his earliest days, he was unusually sharp, ahead of his age level, “always reading books” (Spurgeon: A Biography, 8). He returned home at age six and excelled at school in both math and reading. 我非常兴奋地向大家讲述上帝如何用一段简单的诗句, 从一段复杂的段落中, 他的故事是针对每个人的,但可能有一个特别的单词,可以和房间里的几个团体交谈. 一个是外行者,也就是在基督教部之外从事正常工作谋生的人。

没有神学院教育的人, 我们承认,这一系列的描述 4人谁是传道者。

现在,我们的系列有一个有趣的流传:首先,圣奥古斯丁, 然后,路德,他是一个奥古斯丁的修道士, 然后,约翰·邦扬,他最喜欢的书是路德对加拉提安的评论, 现在,查尔斯·斯普吉翁,他最喜欢的书是"邦扬朝圣者的进步"。

但我们系列的一个弱点(某种意义上的)就是他们都成了传教士。 我们并不期望你们都成为传教士;我们想做几个,但多数是外行,这很好。

现在,斯普吉翁被称为"道教的王子". 但是,在上帝的统治下,在斯普吉翁的故事里,英雄不是斯普吉翁,也不是一个受过训练,有报酬的传教士,而是一名外行人. 因此,斯普吉恩的故事有一个特别的词来形容那些愿意张开口子,说出自己对耶稣所了解的. Spurgeon的故事中也有一个针对青少年和年轻成年人的特殊词.

斯普吉安在15岁时开始信仰,在他这一天,这更像是年轻的成年. 然而,他的故事给那些已经不是孩子和还没有成年的人带来了挑战:青少年,大学生,研究生,甚至年轻专业人员.

不要让世界(或教会)降低你对于什么是可能的, 我的祷告是 上帝可能很乐意 给一些自己的引擎。 父母、大学员工和牧师经常帮助年轻的成年人并给予他们推动。

有时,上帝在青少年生活中很高兴给他们自己的引擎,他们不需要再再推了. 他们说:你们离我远点! 我要跟随耶稣。 你无法阻止我远离他, 这是上帝在15岁时为斯波克森所做的——他给了他自己的引擎. 我祈求他今天上午也乐意这么做

featured.content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. 博客由Mody出版社赞助, 门徒不可能失去人 这听起来很明显。 也许太明显了,甚至不能大声说出来。 但当教堂淡化或忽略了好消息时,毁灭就留在了它的后面.

这是40年的牧师, 我们今天不只是有门徒问题。 我们有一个福音问题。 在做门徒之前,我们开始重新定义皈依本身。 我们慢慢地用超自然再生来换取人类的决定。

救世主成为了重复的祷告,签字的名片,行走的走道,而数百万人则得到天堂的保证,永远没有被上帝的力量所改变. 我们并没有给他们一个没有权力的信仰, 其结果是一代人被深深地基督教化,但不一定改变. 他们知道语言。 他们知道歌曲。

他们知道何时可以站起,何时可以坐起,何时可以说阿门. 他们被浸入了教会文化中,然而许多人从未被从死亡中带入生命. 我们向教会灌输了那些学会如何在 " 基督教 " 内和周围运作而不真正遵循基督的人。 当这种情况发生时,门徒们在人类努力的重压下崩溃了.

当福音会以人类的决定为中心时,门徒不可避免地会变得自强自强. 追随耶稣被贬为行为管理、道德努力和“下次更努力”的人。 基督所承诺的超自然生命被取而代之的是身穿宗教外衣的自救. Dallas Willard谈到了教会未能培养出门徒的“大意念”。 他说得对。

但我相信发生了更深层的事 在我们忽略了门徒身份之前,我们破坏了出生的门徒们最初的福音。 这就是危机。 这是伟大的欺骗。 直到我们恢复改变一切的真正信仰之前,我们将继续尝试向从未真正被活生生地培养出来的门徒.

我们每个周末都坐在教堂的椅子上和教堂的树上,即使是好的,也是圣经教学的教堂。 我们有许多人相信自己是被拯救的,但除了自己的努力之外没有权力,他们的生活只显示新出生的表面证据。 人们猜想自己拥有的只是上帝给他们的一切,他们不知道自己是文化上的基督徒,所以距离上帝还相去甚远.

曾被教过基督教的人脱离了忏悔、投降、门徒费用以及可悲的使福音无法被阻止的力量。 许多人信奉基督, 我们让人们需要更多,需要更多, 伟大的欺骗必须结束。 精神上死去的人有生命

投降导致生命而不是损失。 有悔过感产生出一个繁荣的灵魂的节奏. 纪律是从优雅而不是恐惧或表现中产生的。 当基督变成一切时,有深刻的,解放的,不可磨灭的自由. 这就是为什么必须捍卫真理。 不是作为一个想法,而是作为一个现实,削减、澄清和召唤我们前进。

featured.title_zh: 我们的刑事司法制度在哪些方面存在缺陷（与Matt Martens合著）
featured.content: When you really want to dive into the details of big questions about public policy—how we can live better together—you run into two problems: The experts and other stakeholders don’t want to consider Christian arguments, and Christians don’t want to engage in the details. That combination of a Christian argument from a legal expert was rare when Matt Martens’s book Reforming Criminal Justice: A Christian Proposal came out in 2023 from Crossway. And it’s still rare today. Matt is a trial lawyer and partner at an international law firm in Washington, DC. He and his wife are members at Capitol Hill Baptist Church, and they have two sons and a daughter. I read this book when it came out, and it’s stuck with me. Just the other day, I was thinking about the book when talking to one of my pastors, who was preparing to preach from 1 Peter on justice and obeying authorities. I thought about how I’d want to see the criminal justice system reformed if there were a good shot I’d be either a victim or criminal defendant. Isn’t that the law summed up in loving our neighbors as ourselves? From the death penalty to AI to the decline of violent crime—Matt and I covered a great deal. featured.title: What We Get Wrong About the Tears of Jesus
featured.summary: Was Jesus’s grief at Lazarus’s tomb over his friend’s death or the response of the mourners? Pastor John explains how Jesus’s perfect emotions captured his indignation over unbelief. Listen Now
featured.summary_zh: 耶稣在拉撒路的坟墓前悲伤是因为朋友的离世，还是因为哀悼者的反应？约翰牧师解释了耶稣完美的情感如何表达了他对不信的愤慨。立即聆听
featured.title_zh: 我们对耶稣的眼泪有什么误解
featured.content: Audio Transcript “Jesus wept” (John 11:35). It’s the shortest verse in the Bible. We read it together in the Navigators Bible Reading Plan yesterday. But it’s so brief we can pass it too quickly. Maybe we pass over it because we think we know what it means. Jesus’s friend Lazarus died. Jesus wept because his friend was gone. But what if we got that wrong? Or, what if we mistakenly thought his emotions were simple when they were complex? What if Jesus wept not simply in the loss of death but from a frustration with the living? Today on Ask Pastor John: what we get wrong about the tears of Jesus. Henry, a listener, writes in with a timely question on John 11:35. “Pastor John, thank you for taking my question today. I’d like to ask you about John 11:35. Why do you think Jesus wept at the tomb of Lazarus? One way to read this account is that he’s simply sharing in Mary and Martha’s sorrows over his death. But I wonder if something deeper is going on here. Jesus already planned to raise Lazarus, and he even told his disciples he was going to do it in John 11:11–15. “So, my questions are these two: First, why does Jesus ask, ‘Where have you laid him?’ Was he simply asking to be taken to the tomb? When they answer, ‘Lord, come and see,’ it’s almost like they still don’t appreciate who he is as the Messiah. And that is my second question: This whole event leaves me wondering if this weeping is more like Jesus’s weeping over Jerusalem in Luke 19:41 — weeping because he is heartbroken over the city’s unbelief. Is it a stretch to connect these two moments? Is Jesus grieving the dead Lazarus? Or is he grieving the unbelief of the living?” I doubt that any of Jesus’s emotions were simple. I think they were always complex. We finite creatures have emotions that respond to one or two, maybe three, happy or painful aspects of a situation. So, we may feel sorrow and joy mingled because, say, a very old saint has just gone to be with the Lord, and we will miss him, and yet we’re so happy for him. But Jesus could see every angle, every imaginable aspect of a situation, some of which called for very different emotions. So, I doubt that he ever had a simple emotion. For example, in Mark 3:1–5, there’s this man with a withered hand in the synagogue, and the people are watching to see if Jesus would heal him so that they could accuse Jesus. Can you imagine? They don’t give a hoot about this man’s pain. All they want is to accuse Jesus if he heals him. And in verse 5, it says, “He looked around at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart.” And that’s what I mean by complex emotions: anger and grief perfectly mingled in the sinless heart of Jesus. Another example would be that he looked on unbelieving Jerusalem and wept: “Would that you, even you, had known on this day the things that make for peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes” (Luke 19:42). But in Luke 10:21, it says Jesus “rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, ‘I thank you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you have hidden these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to little children; yes, Father, for such was your gracious will.’” He could weep and rejoice over the wise and bitter providence of God. So, we come to John 11 and the death of Lazarus. And I think Henry, who’s sending us this question, is right when he says Jesus’s tears in John 11 aren’t just about sharing our human grief — that maybe he is genuinely mourning their spiritual blindness. Yes, and I’m going to say not just mourning — he’s indignant. The story begins in John 11:1–6 with Mary and Martha sending words to Jesus that their brother Lazarus is very sick. Jesus waits two more days before going and intentionally lets Lazarus die. He says in John 11:14–15, “Lazarus has died, and for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe.” That’s an amazing statement: “I let him die for the sake of your faith.” “They needed to see the glory of Jesus more than they needed the
featured.content_zh:
" 耶稣哭泣 " (John 11:35)。 这是圣经中最短的一首诗。 我们昨天一起在《航海家圣经阅读计划》上读到的。 但时间太短了, 也许我们通过它,因为我们认为 我们知道它意味着什么。 耶稣的朋友拉扎鲁斯去世. 耶稣因为朋友不在而哭泣. 但如果我们搞错了呢?

或者,如果我们错误地认为 他的情绪是简单的 当它们是复杂的? 如果耶稣不仅在死亡中哭泣,而且在对活人的挫折中哭泣呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"(Pastor John):我们对于耶稣的眼泪有什么错误. 亨利是一位听众,他及时写下约翰11:35的问题. “约翰神父,谢谢你今天接受我的问题。

我想问你约翰11点35分的事。 你觉得耶稣为什么在拉扎鲁斯的坟墓上哭泣? 他只是分享玛丽和玛莎对死亡的悲伤。 但我想知道这里是否发生了更深层的事情。 耶稣已经计划要抚养拉撒路人,他甚至告诉门徒他要在约翰11:11–15中完成.

我问的是这两个问题:首先,耶稣为什么问:你们把他放哪儿了? 他只是要求被带去坟墓吗? 当他们回答“主啊,快来看”时,

这是我第二个问题: 这整起事件让我怀疑这起哭泣事件是否更像是耶稣在路加19:41为耶路撒冷所哭泣, 连接这两个瞬间是不是很长一段时间? 耶稣在哀悼死去的拉撒路吗? 还是他痛恨众生的不信呢?” 我怀疑耶稣的任何情绪都很简单。

我觉得他们总是很复杂 我们有限的生物的情绪 反应了一两个, 也许三个,快乐或痛苦的方面 一个情况。 因此,我们可能感到悲伤和欢乐,因为,比如说,一个非常老的圣人刚刚与上帝在一起,我们将怀念他,然而,我们为他感到如此的高兴。

但是,耶稣可以看到每个角度,一个局势的每一个可想象的方面,有些需要非常不同的情绪. 所以我怀疑他有没有过简单的情绪 例如,在Mark 3:1–5中,有一个人手在犹太会堂里枯萎了,人们正在观察耶稣能否治愈他,以便他们指控耶稣。 你能想象吗?

他们不关心这个人的痛苦。 他们只想指控耶稣 如果他治愈他。 在第5节中,他说:他愤怒地注视着他们,他们为自己的坚硬而悲伤。 这就是复杂的情感的含义:愤怒和悲伤完全混入了耶稣的无罪之心。

另一个例子是,他注视着不信的耶路撒冷并哭道:"但愿你,甚至你,在今天知道什么是和平的! 但是现在它们被隐藏在你的眼睛之外”(19:42)。

但在"路加福音"第10:21节中说:"耶稣在圣灵中欢喜,并且说:我感谢你,天地之主,你把这些东西隐藏在智者与明者之间,并把它启示给小孩子;是的,神父,这是你的仁慈的意志". 他可以为上帝的睿智和痛苦的上帝而哭泣和欢乐。 所以,我们来到约翰11号 和拉撒路的死亡。

我认为亨利(Henry)向我们提出这个问题, 他说耶稣在约翰十一世的眼泪并不只是分享人类的悲痛, 我不仅要表示哀悼, 故事从约翰11:1–6开始,由玛丽和玛莎向耶稣发送了他们的兄弟拉扎鲁斯病得很重的话.

耶稣再等两天,然后故意让拉撒路死去. 他在"约翰·11:14-15"一文中说:"拉撒路已经去世了,为了你,我很高兴我没有在场,以便你相信". 这是一个惊人的说法:“我让他为了你的信仰而死。 ” 他们需要看到耶稣的光荣 而不是他们需要的

featured.title: Small-Church Elders, Here’s How to Give Your Pastor a Sabbatical
featured.summary: Our church has 74 members and two lay elders. Here’s how we raised up five men to preach seven expository sermons and give our pastor a summer sabbatical.
featured.summary_zh: 我们的教会共有74名会友和两名平信徒长老。以下是我们如何培养五位弟兄来宣讲七篇解经性讲道，并让我们的牧师度过一个夏季安息假。
featured.title_zh: 小型教会的长老们，以下是为你们的牧师安排安息假的方式
featured.content: “He should have had a sabbatical six years ago,” my fellow elder said. “I know,” I said. “We know he needs it, but how are we going to do this? We have full-time jobs and young families.” “Well, the cattle on thousand hills are the Lord’s. Let’s ask him to provide it.” I nodded in agreement, but honestly, cattle felt like less of an ask for our church. Our church consists of 74 members. We have one full-time pastor and two lay elders. And yet, exactly two years after that initial elders’ meeting, we managed to give our pastor a much-needed, six-week summer sabbatical. Five male members of our church delivered seven expository and Christ-exalting sermons. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We preached through an entire book of the Bible (Habakkuk). We preached a doctrinal sermon from our confession of faith (on baptism and Communion). Two men preached for the first time. The men ranged from age 20 to 46, and I was the seasoned preacher with 25 sermons under my belt. So how did we pull this off? 1. We prayed. We knew we couldn’t do this. Only God could. This reality framed our prayers over the next two years. God was glorified, our pastor rested, and our church loved it. We came to realize that just as the Sabbath was a gift from God to man (Mark 2:27), so a sabbatical is a gift from God to a pastor. As lay elders, we were called to take steps of faith to this end while relying on the Holy Spirit’s leading and enablement. Just as Jesus is Lord of the Sabbath (Matt. 12:8), so too is he Lord of a sabbatical. As we began to make plans, we prayed that we’d hold them with an open hand and continually lay them at the feet of Jesus. We borrowed words from Jehoshaphat (2 Chron. 20:12) for our prayer in this season: “Lord, we do not know what to do, but our eyes are on you.” 2. We planned backward. We began by identifying the ideal time of year for the sabbatical. We landed on July and August, since that’s when church programming is minimal and vacations are in vogue among our congregation. This decision indirectly led us to the length of sabbatical we felt could responsibly plan for: six weeks. From there, we planned backward. The first Sunday we discussed was the Sunday our pastor would return. How did we want our brother and his wife to reintegrate into the church? We decided we wanted him to feel the warmth of our church’s love in his homecoming without being distracted by sermon preparation. So we chose to begin and end his sabbatical on Fridays. This meant our pastor had a workweek before leaving, so he could help with administrative functions. And by returning from the sabbatical on a Friday, he’d be able to join us for an elder meeting to get updates on members prior to attending church two days later. Preaching could wait another week. We created a two-year timeline that included all of the specific events and developments we thought could be feasible with the Lord’s help. This timeline helped us to answer several looming questions: Should we start the sabbatical by sending our pastor somewhere to create physical and emotional separation between him and our congregation? We agreed we should. We also felt this was an opportunity to invite our church to be generous and to tangibly show their love to our pastor of 12 years and his wife by paying for this trip. How many of our male members would be willing to assist with the preaching? We estimated three to four. How and when would we get them trained? This was the hardest question to answer but also the most rewarding part of this process. 3. We created a brotherhood. We realized our biggest hurdle would be recruiting and training men to aid in the preaching. To address the issue, we settled on offering a six-week preaching cohort during the summer prior to the sabbatical. To identify potential men for the cohort, we asked, “Which men currently do Scripture readings and prayers exceptionally well in our worship services?” Then we talked to each man indiv
featured.content_zh:
“六年前,他应该有一个安息日。” “我知道,”我说。 “我们知道他需要,但我们如何做到这一点? 我们有全职工作和年轻家庭。” " 千山上牛是主的. 让我们请他提供。 我点头同意,但说实话, 牛感觉没有要求我们的教堂。 我们的教堂由74名会员组成.

我们有一位全职牧师和两位无业长老。 然而,在最初的长老会议两年之后,我们设法给我们的牧师一个急需的六周的暑假。 我们教会的5名男性成员进行了7次宣讲会和基督赞美会的布道会。 上帝被赞美,我们的牧师休息, 我们的教会很喜欢它。 我们通过一本《圣经》(哈巴克库克)来宣扬。

我们通过信仰的忏悔(洗礼和圣餐)来进行理论布道。 二人初传道. 这些人的年龄从20岁到46岁不等,我是老练的布道家,我的腰带下有25个布道。 我们怎么做到的? 1. 我们祈祷。 我们知道我们不能这样做。 只有上帝会 这一现实使我们在接下来的两年里祈祷。

上帝被赞美,我们的牧师休息, 我们的教会很喜欢它。 我们意识到,正如安息日是上帝送给人的礼物(马克2:27)一样,安息日是上帝送给牧师的礼物. 作为普通的长者,我们被要求为此而采取信仰步骤,同时依靠圣灵的领导和力量。 犹如耶稣是安息日的主一样。

12: 8),他也是安息日的主. 当我们开始计划时, 我们祈祷我们用开阔的手抓住他们, 我们在本季的祈祷中借用了Jehoshaphat(2 Chron. 20:12)的话,他说:我们的主啊!我们不知道该怎么办,但我们的眼睛在注视着你。 2. 我们计划落后。 我们首先确定了每年安息日的理想时间。

我们于7月和8月登陆, 这一决定间接导致了我们感到可以负责任地规划六个星期的休假时间。 从那里,我们计划向后。 我们讨论的第一个星期日 是牧师回来的星期日

featured.title: ‘I Was a Child of War’: How to Help Abuse Survivors Understand the Past
featured.summary: Yes, we were weak, but we were warriors, not victims.
featured.summary_zh: 是的，我们很弱小，但我们是战士，不是受害者。
featured.title_zh: “我曾是战争的孩子”：如何帮助虐待幸存者理解过去
featured.content: I grew up in a violent home, and it took me decades to find terms and categories that finally let me understand that aspect of my childhood. My first conversation partners and readings said I was a victim of abuse, but that framing was too passive to resonate with me. I believe the passive voice is valid, even essential. But when I discovered another framework, the child of war, I finally began to understand my past. Personal History That Led to Thoughts of War My father was a gifted professional, a compelling speaker who also possessed a shrewd wisdom. My mother seemed like a match—gifted, educated, and kind. But he was violent, even though for 16 years he was a pastor, and my mother couldn’t contain him. His behavior was our family secret, and if I hoped to understand it, I was on my own. Eventually, I read stories about one-dimensional moral monsters called “abusers”; their children were “victims.” But my parents seemed too admirable to be monsters, and the idea that I was a passive victim didn’t label my experience. I left home at 16 and essentially forgot the past until the month my father died. At that point, my readings on war let me see that my childhood had much in common with people who tried to resist and endure the aggression of a superior power. Terms like “resistance,” “war,” and “agency” fit better. They fostered understanding and healing. My first sharp memory is as ragged as a torn fingernail. Four years old, I’m hiding in my mother’s closet, behind dresses that smell of dust and skin cream. My skin stings and a deep ache runs beneath the surface. I’ve been spanked enough to know how it feels, but this is different. I think, I did something wrong, but what? I must deserve this, but why did he hit me so hard? Why does it hurt . . . so . . . much? I’m baffled by what we call mistreatment and betrayal. Fifty years later, I realized that 4-year-olds shouldn’t have the ability or experience to reflect critically on their beatings. And yet, because I could judge his actions, I could separate myself from him—he was “the” father rather than “my” father—and that gave me agency. When I turned 7, my favorite birthday gift was a miniature cowboy wagon. It was cheap, and the father quickly detected a flaw in the plastic. “This will snap,” he declared. He tugged and pulled at it until it broke, then he handed me the pieces and said, “See, I told you that would happen.” The playground had taught me that this was cruelty, so I decided to feel nothing , to sever his capacity to wound me. It was a foolish vow, one no child can fully keep, but it gave me a sense of agency or control. Two years later, it paid off. The chief gift for my 9th birthday was a basketball. When he decided I liked it too much, he stabbed it with a long knife. But by then, I’d hardened myself enough (agency again) to feel no grief, no surprise. It registered as a problem: Where would I get the money to buy another ball? How would I keep it safe? Because I could judge my father’s actions, I could separate myself from him, and that gave me agency. As time passed, my older brother and I began to resist him. We wore thick jeans when it seemed a belt might begin to fly. If a blow landed? Physical pain usually doesn’t last long. Social pains were tougher. The family moved often, because the father could always get a job but was too erratic to keep one. I attended five schools in seven years, chiefly in insular towns. I discovered that my athletic skills let me make friends through one team or another. Yet it was wise to mask my academic abilities-—unless the boys needed a math champion to wipe the smirks off the smart girls’ faces. I was making a way, until the dynamics at home shifted. Perhaps it was the alcohol. Perhaps it was the professional failure. The father was now reduced to the oversight of a tiny country church, two part-time jobs, and summer work for the Red Cross. Whatever the reasons, his behavior became ominous. He cursed and raged day after day,
featured.content_zh:
我在一个暴力的家庭里长大,我花了几十年的时间才找到最终让我理解我童年的这一方面的术语和类别. 我的第一个谈话伙伴和读者说,我是虐待的受害者,但这种陷害太被动,无法与我产生共鸣。 我认为被动的声音是有效的,甚至是必不可少的。

但当我发现另一个框架,战争的孩子, 我终于开始理解我的过去。 个人历史 我父亲是一位有天赋的专业人士,一位很有说服力的演讲者,他拥有精明的智慧。 我妈妈看起来是一对配对, 虽然他16年来都是牧师,

他的行为是我们家族的秘密, 如果我希望理解它,我独自一人。 最终,我读到了关于一维道德怪物的故事,称为“滥用者 ” ; 他们的孩子是“受害者 ” 。 但我的父母似乎太令人钦佩了,

我16岁离开家 基本上忘记了过去 直到我父亲去世的那个月 那时,我对战争的解读让我看到,我的童年与那些试图抵抗和忍受一个超级大国的侵略的人们有许多共同点。 " 抵抗 " 、 " 战争 " 和 " 机构 " 等用语比较合适。 它们促进了理解和愈合。 我的第一个尖锐的记忆就像一个撕裂的手指甲一样

我躲在母亲的衣柜里, 我的皮肤刺痛 和深深的痛 运行在地表之下。 但情况不同。 我想,我做错了什么? 我必须得这样 但他为什么打我这么重? 为什么这么痛?

我对所谓的虐待和背叛感到困惑。 50年后,我意识到4岁的孩子不应该有批判性地反思殴打他们的能力或经验。 然而,因为我可以判断他的行为,我可以把自己与他分开——他是“父亲”而不是“我的父亲”,这给了我代理权。

当我七岁的时候 我最喜欢的生日礼物是一辆小型牛仔车 它很便宜,父亲很快发现了塑料的缺陷. 他宣称,“这将崩溃”。

他拉着它,拉着它,直到它破碎,然后他把碎片递给我,他说:你看,我告诉你了。 游乐场告诉我,这是残酷的, 所以我决定没有任何感觉, 切断他伤害我的能力。 这是一个愚蠢的誓言,一个没有孩子能完全保持的,但它给了我一种代理感或控制感. 两年之后,它得到了回报。

我九岁生日的主要礼物是篮球 当他决定我太喜欢它时 他用长刀刺它 但到那时,我已使自己变得足够坚固(又是一个机构),不感到悲伤,也不感到惊讶。 它是一个问题: 我哪来的钱买另一球? 我怎么保证它的安全?

因为我可以判断我父亲的行为, 随着时间流逝,我和哥哥开始反抗他. 我们穿着厚厚的牛仔裤 当它看起来可能开始飞翔。 如果一击落地? 身体疼痛通常不会持续很长时间。 社会痛苦更严重。

家里人经常搬家,因为父亲总是可以找到工作,但是过于不稳定,无法保留工作。 我在七年中就读了五所学校,主要在岛屿城镇。 我发现我的运动能力 让我通过一个或另一个团队交朋友。 除非男生需要数学冠军来抹去聪明女孩脸上的笑容,

我在想办法 直到家里的动态变化 也许是因为酒 也许是职业上的失败 父亲现在被降格为一个小乡村教会的监督,两个兼职工作,以及红十字会的暑期工作. 不管是什么原因 他的行为变得不祥 他日复一日的诅咒和愤怒,

featured.summary: When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost.

featured.title_zh: 数千次家庭查经的累积效应
featured.content: The alarm goes off, and another busy day begins. Getting kids up and ready for school, meal prep, work, after-school activities. Before you know it, the day is racing to its close. And you’re exhausted again. As Christian parents, we want our lives to count for Christ. We sincerely want our children to live their lives for Christ too. We want them to be changed by the same amazing grace that has transformed us. But how does this happen? How can we find the time and energy to effectively disciple our kids? Where will we find the creativity and passion to teach them what matters most? If you’re discouraged by your limited time and ability to shepherd your children, consider the cumulative effects of thousands of family Bible readings over the course of many years. Think Small What if a brief Bible reading today, a couple more later this week, and a few more next week eventually became a pattern, a deeply rooted habit for your family? Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over a couple decades. Small investments of time and intentionality can make a big difference over the span of a couple decades. Years ago, Trevin Wax wrote an article titled “ 1000 Sermons Will Change Your Life .” What he says to pastors about preaching also applies to parents who lead their kids in family Bible reading: Pastors, don’t underestimate the cumulative effect of your preaching. You are not dumping information into brains. You are forming the habits of your people, teaching them how to read and understand and apply the Bible for themselves. Similarly in family life, our discipleship has cumulative effects that may not come to fruition for years. As parents, we’re in this for the long haul. If your children live in your home from birth to age 18, that’s 6,570 days. If you read the Bible together on average every third day, that’s 2,190 Bible readings over the course of your sons’ and daughters’ childhood and teenage years. Keep that big picture in mind when you feel defeated after a couple days on the go, when those family discipleship moments have eluded you. Think of Timothy, who was acquainted with the sacred writings from childhood because of his mother’s and grandmother’s faithful witness (2 Tim. 1:5; 3:14–15). May we be influential parents like them, who little by little and day by day pass on our life of faith to the next generation. Be Consistent, Establish a Habit With the long view in mind, think small in terms of your goals for this week, month, or year. Aim for consistency, for establishing a habit that you can pray will take root in your kids’ lives. Joe Carter recently shared the results of a sociological study of how faith moves across generations. He summarized the findings: The behaviors that most strongly predict lasting faith are active and verbal: praying together as a family, saying grace, embedding faith in the rhythm of the week rather than reserving it for Sunday, and, above all, talking about it. Children raised in homes where faith was discussed at least several times a week were more than twice as likely to attend church, pray daily, and rate religion as very important in young adulthood. The simplest way to put this truth into practice in your home is by creating a rhythm of opening the Bible regularly, reading some verses, and discussing them. You may never have a sense that one particular devotional was transformative. But keep at it. When your kids are inattentive or disruptive, don’t be overly discouraged. If the milk spills, if a fight erupts, all is not lost. Resist the temptation to quit. Come back to the reading the next day, or the day after that. Keep finding times to open the Bible with your family. Let the Word Do the Heavy Lifting Another deterrent that may get in the way of family discipleship is “the intimidation factor.” If you feel ill-equipped to teach the Bible to your kids, you may be inclined to leave that task to Sunday school teachers and youth pastors. featured.content: “Hold the lettuce.” The simple sentence, perhaps stated more frequently than we might hope, captures a crucial hallmark that predominates in the thinking of many. At a recent lunch with a friend, I saw this firsthand. For my friend, it wasn’t just the lettuce. The instructions he gave restrained the cook from adding anything remotely vegetable-like to the hamburger. Notwithstanding my jibe, my friend held fast to his decision. He was the one ordering. And he expected (rightly so!) to be served what he desired. After all, the customer is king. This cluster of expectations animates the modern marketplace. We want products tailored to our specific needs. We seek out services that let us pay only for what we want. We get frustrated when we take the car to a mechanic who not only fixes the problem we knew about but also takes the liberty of repairing other problems (and charging liberally for them). In short, we want (and expect) to be served according to our preferences and felt needs. Innocuous enough when it comes to the morsels on our plates, the reign of personal preferences involves more serious implications when it extends over the rest of life. And in the life of faith, the consequences are serious indeed. For preference-driven faith will, in the end, produce a Christless Christianity. Have It Your Way What do we hope for when we join the church for worship? Parsing motives presents no easy project, especially if there are children in tow or responsibilities for some aspect of the service or fellowship. Few of us have the personal or cognitive space to search out the depths of our hearts en route to the Sunday morning service. But the way home often presents opportunities to interrogate those hidden recesses. The questions we pose shed light on what is in our hearts: “How did you like the sermon this morning?” “Didn’t the worship team nail it today?” We tend to ask not about a confrontation with gospel truth but about measures of personal satisfaction. If our questions begin illuminating this tendency, the answers we give put our motives on clear display: “I thought the pastor did a great job! I really liked . . .” or “Ya know, I just wasn’t feeling it this morning; the sermon didn’t really speak to me.” “Yes, the worship was great!” or “I thought the team was a bit off. Did you hear them mess up on that one song?” So often, whether at the sandwich shop or on the way home from church, preference-driven language bubbles out of our mouths like boiling water from an unwatched pot. For many, our post-service concerns center far too frequently on how well certain aspects of the service met our felt needs. What did I gain from the sermon? Did I enjoy the music? Service to the ascendant self predominates. We reflect on the worship gathering in a manner unsettlingly similar to how we might reflect on a hamburger: It was decent, but I’ve had better elsewhere. I think they overdid the mayonnaise, and I would have preferred sesame rather than a brioche bun. Whether we want to admit it or not, our expectations of being served as we please spill into our perceived relationship to the church’s gathered worship. Those same expectations shape how we approach our Lord. We tend naturally, in our sin, to want merely an affirming savior. We like to hear that Jesus loves sinners so much that he died to win them, for hearing this affirms that our need for forgiveness has been met. We like to hear that his love for his sheep never falters, for hearing this quells the fear that perhaps our snide words or dubious choices or the train wreck of our inner thoughts might put our hope in jeopardy. We like to hear how our Lord railed against the hypocrisy and legalism of the Pharisees, for hearing this makes us smile inwardly, pleased that we are not so pretentious and uptight. Messages such as these leave us content, unruffled, ready to carry on with life as normal, affirmed in our preferred way of life by a (truncated) gospel that accomplishes little b

“抓住生菜。” 这个简单的句子,也许比我们所希望的更频繁地说,抓住了在许多人的思想中占主导地位的关键标志。 最近和一个朋友共进午餐时 我亲眼看到的 对我的朋友来说, 他给厨师的指示 禁止在汉堡里添加任何类似蔬菜的东西

我的朋友坚持他的决定 是他订的 他希望自己所欲达到的, 毕竟客为王. 这一组期望激发出现代市场。 我们需要适合我们具体需要的产品。 我们寻求服务,让我们只为所欲为。

我们感到沮丧的是,我们把车送到一个技工那里,他不仅解决了我们所知道的问题,而且还自由地修复了其他问题(并且对这些问题收取宽松的费用)。 简言之,我们希望(并期望)根据我们的喜好和感受到的需要得到服务。

谈到我们盘子里的泥潭时,个人偏好的统治,如果延续到余生,就会产生更严重的影响。 在信仰的生活中,后果确实很严重。 因为受偏好驱使的信仰,最终会产生出一种没有基督的基督教. 我们加入教堂做礼拜时希望什么?

分析动机并非易事,特别是如果有儿童被拖走或承担某些方面的服务或研究金责任。 我们当中很少有人拥有个人或认知空间,在前往周日早间礼拜的路上去探寻内心深处. 但回家的方式往往为审讯那些隐蔽的休庭提供了机会。

我们提出的问题揭示了我们心中的心事,“你今天早上喜欢讲道吗?” 我们往往不问与福音真相的对抗,而是问个人满意的措施。 如果我们的问题开始说明这一趋势,我们给出的答案清楚地显示了我们的动机:“我认为牧师做了一件伟大的工作!

我真的很喜欢. . . . . . . . . “是的,崇拜是伟大的!”或“我认为队伍有点偏差。 你听到他们把那首歌弄乱了吗?” 所以,无论是在三明治店,还是在从教堂回家的路上,偏好驱动的语言泡从我们嘴里喷出,就像从一个无人观察的锅中取出沸水来.

对许多人来说,我们的服务后关切过于频繁地集中在服务的某些方面在多大程度上满足了我们的需要。 我从布道中得到什么? 我很喜欢音乐吗? 服务于上层的自我占主导地位。 我们以令人不安的方式思考礼拜聚会, 但我在别处生活得更好。

我觉得他们做了蛋黄酱, 我更喜欢芝麻,而不是布洛克包。 无论我们是否愿意承认这一点,我们期望得到服务,因为我们希望与教会所聚集的礼拜的感同身受。 同样的期望决定了我们如何接近我们的主。 我们的罪孽中,自然而然地只想要一个坚定的救世主。

我们喜欢听到耶稣如此地爱罪人,以至于他为了赢得他们的胜利而去死,因为听到这个消息,肯定了我们对宽恕的需要已经得到满足了. 我们想听到,他对他的羊的爱从未动摇,因为听到这种平息的恐惧,也许我们的暗语或可疑的选择,或者我们内心思想的火车残骸会使我们的希望陷入危险.

我们想听听我们的主如何反对法利赛人的虚伪和法西斯主义,因为听到这使我们对内微笑,很高兴我们没有这么自大和紧张。 这样的讯息给我们留下了内容,没有磨损,准备继续正常生活,在我们所偏爱的生活方式中,用一个(经磨练的)福音来证实,这些福音成就不大。

featured.title: The Festive Attire We Really Need
featured.summary: Even in our finest clothes we can still be dirty on the inside. Advent reminds us that Jesus dresses us in his righteousness.
featured.summary_zh: 即使穿着我们最好的衣服 内心还是可以脏的 基督提醒我们,耶稣穿戴我们的正义。
featured.title_zh: 我们真正需要的节奏
featured.content: Read He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years. (Mal. 3:3–4) Reflect My grandmother always made going to church a special event. She helped me pick the right dress, made sure my shoes were shiny and clean, and withstood burns from the curling iron to perfect my hairdo. I know church attire can vary. But I still get dressed up for corporate worship because, no matter how cliché it sounds, I want to wear my Sunday best for Jesus. Yet even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Hidden sins are, after all, hidden. We can sing hymns at max volume, forgetting the way we treated our coworkers last week. We can kneel in prayer, easily dismissing what we posted on the internet earlier that morning. We can take the bread and wine even if we lost it with our kids in the car. People at church only see what’s on the outside, but God looks on the heart (1 Sam. 16:7). And unless we come clean, we can’t come into his presence at all. Even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Purity in God’s presence is a major theme in Scripture. In Leviticus, we learn how Israel was to distinguish between the clean and unclean. These categories extended to foods and animals. Even people could be defiled by disease or by touching unclean things such as a dead body. The temple was off-limits for the unclean. Only ritual washings and animal sacrifices made reentry into God’s presence achievable. But even this wasn’t permanent—for the blood of bulls and goats couldn’t fully atone for sin (Heb. 10:4). Like Israel, we dare not present ourselves before God in our sinful condition. As the psalmist asks, “Who shall stand in [God’s] holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (Ps. 24:3–4). While soap and water might wash our filthy hands, what can purify our sin-stained hearts? In today’s verses, the prophet Malachi announced the coming of One who would refine his people as gold and silver. Later, the author of Hebrews clarified the refiner’s identity: If the blood of goats and bulls . . . sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God. (Heb. 9:13–14) During Advent, we remember that Jesus is the great Refiner. He came to shed his purifying blood to cover our sins and forgive us. Then, like a refiner who heats metal to remove impurities, the Lord sanctifies us so that on judgment day we’ll be an unblemished offering to God. On that day, because of Jesus, we’ll wear white robes of righteousness (Rev. 6:11). Grandma made sure I looked pretty for church, but I wasn’t truly clean. Jesus, the great Purifier of sinners, is the only One who can wash away every stain and remove every impurity. When he dresses us in white robes, we’ll enter God’s presence because we’ll be clean—not just on the outside but on the inside too. Respond Sometimes the Lord refines us through trials and difficult circumstances. How have you experienced his refining process this year? Write a prayer thanking God for Christ who cleanses, purifies, and refines us so we’ll one day be holy and acceptable in his presence.

读取 他必坐作炼银的精炼者,他必洗涤利未之子,并如金银般精炼,他们必以善报主耶和华. 犹大和耶路撒冷的供奉,将像往年和往年一样,为耶和华所喜悦。 (3:3-4) 反映 我奶奶总是把去教堂做成一件特殊的事

她帮我选合适的裙子 确保我的鞋子光亮洁洁 从卷曲的铁里烧伤 我知道教堂的服装会有所不同 但我还是穿好衣服去参加公司礼拜 因为不管这听起来多么陈词滥调 我想穿我的星期天最好的耶稣。 即便穿着我们最好的衣服 我们内心仍然可以肮脏

隐藏的罪恶毕竟是隐藏的。 我们可以用最高音量唱颂歌 忘记上周我们对待同事的方式 我们可以跪在祷告中, 轻易地放弃我们当天早晨在互联网上发布的内容。 我们可以拿走面包和酒 即使我们失去了它与我们的孩子在车里。 人们在教堂只看到外面的东西,但上帝看着心脏(1Sam. 16:7).

除非我们坦白,否则我们根本无法进入他的存在。 即使穿着我们最好的衣服, 我们内部仍然可以脏。 上帝面前的纯洁是圣经中的一个主要主题。 在利维提库斯,我们了解到以色列如何区分干净和不干净。 这些类别扩大到食物和动物。

甚至人们也可能因疾病或触摸尸体等不干净的东西而受到玷污。 该寺对不洁者禁入. 只有仪式洗涤和动物牺牲才能使重返上帝的存在。 但即使是这也不是永久的 — — 因为公牛和山羊的血无法完全赎罪(Heb. 10:4)。

与以色列一样,我们不敢在罪恶的条件下站在上帝面前。 正如诗人所问的, " 谁会站在[上帝]的圣地? 手清净而心清净者”(第24:3-4页)。 虽然肥皂和水可能洗我们的脏手,但什么能净化我们的罪恶的心? 先知马拉奇在今天的诗文中宣布,

后来,希伯来人的作者澄清了提炼者的身份: 如果山羊和公牛的血... ...为净化肉体而神圣化, 基督的血会有多少, 他通过永恒的灵献给自己 没有污垢上帝, (Heb. 9:13-14)在"启示录"中,我们记得耶稣是伟大的炼油者.

他为了掩盖我们的罪孽 并原谅我们而来 然后,像精炼者一样,他用金属加热去除杂质,主使我们圣洁,这样,在审判日,我们将成为向上帝献礼的无瑕疵者。 因为耶稣的缘故, 外婆确保我看起来很适合教堂,

耶稣,罪人的伟大净化者,是唯一可以洗去每一个污点,去除每一个杂质的人. 当他穿白袍时, 我们将进入上帝的面前, 有时主会通过考验和困难的环境来完善我们 你今年是怎么经历他的提炼过程的?

感谢上帝净化、净化、精炼我们,

featured.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
featured.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
featured.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
featured.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

featured.title_zh: 滚动灵魂浅滩
featured.content: Audio Transcript We lived through a decade of smartphone abuse and overuse (roughly 2015 to 2024). We talked at length about it on this podcast. I wrote books about it. Most of us have come to terms with when and where we’ve been online too much. We lament the wasted time, knowing we should have been doing more important things. The clock sped up as we lost ourselves in the everlasting scroll of eye-grabbing images and video. But what if time was not the greatest cost? What if something more serious happened to us, a lingering damage still present inside of us now? Today on Ask Pastor John: scrolling the soul shallow. It’s a question from Noah, a young man in Akron, Ohio. “Pastor John, I have made Titus 2:6–8 my aim as a young man. I know Paul is speaking to a young pastor. I am not a pastor, but I want to be self-controlled. I want to show myself ‘to be a model of good works,’ and I want to display ‘integrity, dignity, and sound speech.’ The main struggle I face is the shallowness of the culture in which we live. On my phone, computer, and TV, I see endless examples of flippancy. That’s really all I see some days. The whole world seems bent on numbing our souls to eternal realities. How can a young man resist all this and stay spiritually alert and cultivate these virtues?” One of the reasons I love this question is because I have said many times that the worst problem with television (or now let’s just say Instagram or any online media in general) is probably not the pervasive sexualization of all of life — that’s big enough — but rather the pervasive trivialization of all of life. You can scarcely watch TV ads or be online for more than ten seconds without being dump-trucked with banality and silliness. Grown men and women, even famous grown men and women, act like eleven-year-olds whose high point at summer camp was to bob for apples in a toilet filled with Mello Yello — the apex of satisfaction. That’s the quality that we’re being dumped on every day. This is the world we live in: silliness, humor, fun, joking, casual, flippant, cleverness, whimsical. And all that has made its way tragically into parenting, worship services, preaching, and hosting an event, even a serious one. Many modern people have never tasted serious joy, glad gravity, happy earnestness, or joyful weightiness. They have no category for such a thing. There’s fun and there’s boredom. That’s it. Life is that shallow, that insignificant. So, Noah asks, “How can I resist all this? How can I march to the beat of a different drummer?” 1. Distinguish between joy and fun. First, make sure that you are clear that joy and fun are not identical. Today, the word fun has virtually taken over the experience of serious joy. “Think about the shortness of life and the inevitability of death and the great realities of God.” Fun is what you have when playing with your kids on the living-room floor, flag football with the guys on Saturday, or a day at Disney World. That’s fun — nothing wrong with it. But now, church planting is fun, worship services are fun, Bible studies are fun. It’s as if you learn the language of trees while walking among twenty-foot Georgia pines, and then you visit three-hundred-foot, two-thousand-year-old redwoods in California and you have no language. They’re just fun trees. They’re not magnificent. They’re not breathtaking. They’re not humbling. They’re just fun trees. So, Noah, grow your vocabulary of joy and significance and wonder, because more often than we would like to admit, the heart shrinks to the language we have to express it rather than the other way around. If you call enough magnificent things “fun,” before long, that’s all they’ll be. Your heart will have shrunk to your vocabulary. 2. Know you’re not crazy. Second, listen to the warnings of Scripture to know you’re not crazy. The Bible is very aware of people who are incapable of being happily serious, and all their language is just clever or joking or trifling. - “Like a madman w

音频记录 我们经历了十年的智能手机虐待和过度使用(大约2015年到2024年). 我们在播客上详细谈论了这个问题。 我写过书 我们大部分人都同意我们上网的时间和地点。 我们对浪费时间感到遗憾,因为我们知道我们应该做更重要的事。

时钟加速了,因为我们迷失了自己 在永恒的卷轴 挖眼影像和视频。 但如果时间不是最大的代价呢? 如果更严重的事情发生在我们身上, 那现在我们体内仍然存在的伤害呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"上:滚动灵魂浅浅. 俄亥俄州Akron的年轻人Noah问:

“约翰神父,我把提图斯2:6-8作为我作为年轻人的目标。 我知道保罗在和一个年轻的牧师说话 我不是牧师,但我想自我控制。 我想展示自己“成为优秀作品的典范”, 我面临的主要斗争是我们所生活的文化的浅浅.

在我的手机、电脑和电视上, 我看到无尽的翻转例子。 这些日子我只看到这些。 整个世界似乎都想把我们的灵魂麻木于永恒的现实。

一个年轻人怎么能抗拒这一切,保持精神警惕,培养这些美德呢?” 我喜欢这个问题的原因之一 是因为我已经说过很多次了 电视最糟糕的问题(或者现在我们只说Instagram或任何一般的网络媒体) 可能不是 普遍的性化 生活的所有 - 这已经够大了 - 而是 普遍的轻视所有o

有乐趣和无聊。 就这样。 生命是那么浅,那么微不足道。 诺亚问道:我怎能抗拒这一切呢? 我怎能走向一个不同的鼓手呢?” 1.区分欢喜乐. 第一,确保你明白快乐和乐趣并不相同。 今天,乐趣一词几乎取代了严肃的欢乐经历.

所以,诺亚, 增加你的喜悦和意义 和奇异的词汇, 因为比我们想承认的更多时候, 心脏收缩到 语言 我们必须表达它而不是相反。 如果你在不久之前就称它为“有趣”的话, 你的心会缩到词汇里 2. 知道你没有疯。

第二,听从圣经的警告, 圣经中非常了解那些不能快乐严肃的人,他们所有的语言都只是聪明或开玩笑,或三思而行. - 像个疯子

featured.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. featured.title_zh: 你就不能帮我吗?
featured.content: Several times now, I have been out in creation with unbelievers, speaking to them of eternal matters, and, passing by a dying branch at the base of a tree, I have picked it up and said, “This is your life apart from Christ.” Speaking about their souls, Jesus’s illustration is irresistible. The conversation goes something like this: Jesus gives us this illustration. He looks you in the eye and says that he is the tree (to augment the illustration slightly), and you are the branch. Look up and see the branches above us, beautiful leaves waving, healthy in their vibrant greens, bearing evidence of life. And then there is this branch. Dry. Leafless. Withered. Why? Because it is detached from the source of its life. Cut off from the one it was made to have communion with. And so, it lies here, detached from its purpose and severed from the only thing that can make it flourish. Jesus claims to be man’s source. He claims to be the Tree to whom you belong. In relationship with him, you have life. Apart from him, he teaches, you spend life withering. I usually pause to let the claim have its proper space. I ask what they think of such an assertion. I give them an opportunity to respond. I have often expected indifference or offense, but I have consistently been met with quiet consideration or outright acknowledgment that such an illustration made sense to them. Or at least they would like to hear more. So I go on to wonder aloud with them. What is it like to be a branch fallen from the tree that is, as Jesus says, withering ? Don’t you know? Need we ask? The restlessness, the fatal dryness, the looming death. The reaching out to anything and everything for life — except for the tree standing beside and over us. Him we do not want. Him we can do without. We can make it our own way. The adverb is different, but the end is the same — restless withering, drunken withering, religious, secular, or thoughtless withering . Some overdose on pleasure. Others get high on their own morality. Still others distract themselves from death’s shadow creeping over them with fantasy football and rounds of golf. But for all that, withering. But Jesus himself asserts that he is the Tree. He is the one we were made for; in him alone can we find the life that haunts us in still and sober moments. Be grafted to him through repentance and faith, be attached to him by the Spirit of the living God, have his words live in you, direct you, amaze you, and dead things will come to life. And what will it be on that day, I am compelled to continue, for those dry and fruitless branches who refused life in him? They will be gathered and thrown into the fire and burned as useless things. But Jesus came that you might have otherwise. He told us his mission was to bring life — life abundantly . Imagine the branch grafted to the tree, suddenly infused with life and purpose and the vital sap of God’s own Spirit. We are as branches; the Father, Son, and Spirit are the source of everlasting life. With him, we flourish though all may seem to go poorly. Without him, only sapped wood remains. Would you like to know more about this Jesus? Now, I tell you this to highlight one of many places where the Bible addresses the interiority of man and its solution: God. I want you to see how dangerous the alternative answers found in modern therapeutic culture are to our souls and our churches. It is a scourge, especially to this inward age, not because a therapeutic culture takes distresses of the heart seriously, but because it too often sends branches reaching out for anything but the Tree. Ingrown Toenails The problem comes not from a focus on the inner man. Anyone who says the Bible has little to say about internal battles, demons, depressions, anxieties, doubts, and the despairs of human life should not air his ignorance. The Scriptures abound with stories of the faithful brought into all the perplexities and pains of life in a fallen world. The Psalms, as one profound example, give u

他看着你的眼睛,说他是树(稍加插图),你是树枝。 抬头看上面的树枝,美丽的叶子挥舞着, 健康地在生机勃勃的绿色中,有生命的证据。 然后是这个分支。 干,无叶. 废. 为什么? 因为它脱离了生命的来源。

切断了与它 与圣餐。 因此,它躺在这里,脱离了它的目的,从唯一能够使它蓬勃发展的东西中分离出来. 耶稣自称是人类的来源. 他自称是你所属的树 在他的关系,你有生活。 除了他,他还教书,你一辈子都在消磨 我通常会停下来 让权利主张有它的适当空间。

那天我不得不继续 对那些拒绝他生命的干枯和无果树枝 他们将被集合并投入火中,被烧成无用的东西. 但耶稣来了,你也许有 否则。 他告诉我们,他的使命是带来生命——充满生命。

想象一下树上的树枝, 突然注入生命和目的, 我们如枝条一样;父、子、精神是永恒生命的源泉。 和他在一起,我们蓬勃发展,尽管一切似乎都不好。 没有他,只有树枝残骸。 你想知道更多关于这个耶稣的事吗?

现在,我告诉你,这要强调 圣经涉及人类的内在性及其解决方案的许多地方之一:上帝。 我想让你们看看现代治疗文化中找到的替代答案对我们的灵魂和教会有多危险.

它是一个祸害,特别是在这个内在时代,不是因为治疗文化认真对待心灵的烦恼,而是因为它常常发出枝条去寻求除了树以外的任何东西。 内生脚趾甲 问题不在于关注内心的人。

featured.title_zh: 谁或什么？明智使用人工智能的连续体
featured.content: It is sometimes hard to believe that it has been only four years since AI became widely available. Few technologies have made so massive and rapid a leap into our daily lives, to the extent that AI now exists in the background of all of our lives and, for many of us, in the foreground as well. Few technologies have evolved as quickly, so that the latest ChatGPT model bears about as much resemblance to its debut as the latest MacBook does to a Commodore 64. If all this has happened in just four years, imagine what the next four—or the next fourteen—might hold. As AI’s capabilities have increased, so too have the ways we can use it in our homes, churches, and workplaces. It seems like every month or two we read of a feature that can make a difference to our lives by adding a new ability or taking on work that used to be done by a person. The latest trend is the rise of agents—AI tools like Meta’s Muse or xAI’s Grok Bot that can carry out tasks, routines, and duties on an ongoing basis. With all of the tools available to us and all of their capabilities, it can be difficult to know which uses are legitimate and which are not. We all know that just because AI can do a task doesn’t mean that it should . So how can we determine the legitimate roles AI can play in our lives? I think sketching out a continuum of some of AI’s potential roles can help us. At the beginning are roles that most of us would agree are illegitimate, and at the end roles that most of us would agree are legitimate. Between them are roles that may be illegitimate in some cases and perfectly fine in others. These demand that we approach them thoughtfully to determine whether integrating them into our lives would be an act of wisdom or folly. As you will see, illegitimate roles tend to be those that require a who whereas legitimate roles tend to be those that require a mere what . The Continuum AI as God . There are some people, most of them deeply engaged in the tech industry, who ascribe to AI god-like qualities and who relate to it accordingly. They may believe it is an evil god that is likely to destroy humanity or a benevolent god that is likely to redeem humanity, but in either case, they treat AI as something far more than software. These people go too far and commit idolatry as they attribute to tech what rightly belongs to God. AI as Friend . There are some people who relate to AI as a friend, and even a few troubled people who relate to it as a lover. While AI is capable of mimicking the kind of relationship one might enjoy with a fellow human being, it can only ever mimic it. To relate to AI as a friend is to anthropomorphize a mere technology and worse, to deprive oneself of actual friendship. Though AI can imitate friendship, it cannot be a friend in any legitimate sense of the word, for friendship depends upon personhood. Not only that, but friendship depends upon mutuality and both the blessings and risks that come with relationship. You cannot be friends with AI any more than you can be friends with a tree, a PlayStation, or any other non-being. AI as Counselor . Many people today relate to AI as a counselor—a confidant who will listen patiently and counsel them with a trusted voice. Yet because AI is a what , not a who , it cannot offer answers based on a true understanding of their circumstances, true wisdom that comes from learning and experience, or true compassion that comes from sharing their humanity. It cannot empathize with them, pray for them, or plead with the Holy Spirit for wisdom in helping them. AI is capable of advising in many ways, but not of counseling, for counseling is inherently personal. AI as Pastor . Increasingly, people bring to AI the matters of spiritual health, growth, and well-being that in the past would have been addressed to a pastor. Every Christian needs to be under the loving oversight of a pastor who will care for their soul, and such crucial matters must be entrusted not to AI, but to a pastor who is called and
featured.content_zh:
有时很难相信,自AI广泛提供至今才四年。 很少有技术使我们的日常生活如此巨大和迅速地跃入,以至于AI现在存在于我们所有生活的背景中,对我们许多人来说,也存在于前景中。

很少有技术发展得这么快,因此最新的ChatGPT模型与其首发版的相近程度与最新的MacBook对准将64的相近程度相同. 如果这一切在短短的四年内就发生了,想象下四年,或下十四年可能发生的情况。 随着AI能力的增强,我们在家里、教堂和工作场所使用它的方式也一样。

我们似乎每个月或两个月都读到一个特点,通过增加新的能力或从事过去由一个人完成的工作,可以改变我们的生活。 最近的趋势是,诸如Meta的Muse或xAI的Grok Bot等能够持续执行任务、例行公事和职责的代理-AI工具的兴起。

有了我们可以利用的所有工具及其所有能力,就很难知道哪些用途是合法的,哪些用途不是。 我们都知道, 我们如何确定AI在生活中可以扮演的合法角色? 我认为勾画出AI的一些潜在角色可以帮助我们。

开始时,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是非法的,最后,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是合法的。 两者之间是在某些情况下可能是非法的,而在另一些情况下则完全正确。 这些要求我们深思熟虑地对待他们,以确定将他们融入我们的生活是明智还是愚蠢。

你会看到,非法角色往往是那些需要谁的角色,而合法角色往往是那些只需要什么的角色。 连续AI作为上帝。 有一些人,其中大多数人深入从事技术产业,他们把AI的神性描述为"类似"的特质,并与之相应相通.

他们可能相信是邪恶的神有可能毁灭人性或者仁慈的神有可能赎回人性,但无论在哪种情况下,他们都把AI视为远远超出软件的东西. 这些人太过分了 以偶像为神 因为他们把属于上帝的东西归为技术 作为朋友的AI.

有些人以朋友身份与AI有关,甚至有少数人以恋人身份与之有关系. 虽然AI能够模仿人们可能享受的那种与人类同胞的关系,但它只能模仿它. 作为朋友与AI的关系就是人类化,将一种简单的技术变成更糟糕的技术,剥夺了自己的实际友谊。

虽然大赦国际可以模仿友谊,但它不能是任何合法意义上的朋友,因为友谊取决于人性。 不仅如此,友谊还取决于相互以及关系带来的幸福和风险。 你不可能成为AI的朋友 也不可能成为树上的朋友,PlayStation,或者其他的不幸福. 作为律师的AI.

今天,许多人都把大赦国际当作一个顾问——一个会耐心地倾听他们的意见并以一个值得信赖的声音给他们提供建议的告密者。 然而,由于大赦国际是一个什么人,而不是谁,它不能根据对他们情况的真正理解、来自学习和经验的真正智慧或来自分享其人性的真正同情来提供答案。

它不能同情他们,不能为他们祈祷,也不能恳求圣灵的智慧帮助他们。 大赦国际能够在许多方面提供咨询,但不能提供咨询,因为咨询本质上是针对个人的。 作为牧师的AI. 人们越来越多地将精神健康、成长和福祉等问题带到大赦国际,这些问题过去本来是交给牧师的。

每个基督徒都需要接受一位会关心自己灵魂的牧师的慈爱监督,这种关键事项必须不委托给大赦国际,而委托给一位被叫作"和"和"的牧师".

featured.title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
featured.content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
